# Exposure-conditioned measured response from evolving low-rate morphology in Li2025

## Scientific decision and substantive advance

This child replaces the parent's OCV-fitted degradation-mode outcome with directly measured electrochemical performance. It asks whether, after conditioning on current measured state, the capacity contained in the curve itself, and a declared two-RPT ageing exposure, the evolving non-affine shape of a 0.1C discharge curve predicts subsequent measured capacity and resistance response when the entire experiment family is absent from fitting.

A curve model can appear prospective by re-encoding current capacity, static specimen/protocol identity, or an OCV fit made from the same curve. A transportable association with later measured capacity loss and resistance growth would instead identify an electrical signature of susceptibility to a subsequent exposure. It could improve diagnostic triage and model validation without identifying a microscopic mechanism.

The required new deliverable is out-of-family prediction of two measured response endpoints by a scalar/exposure baseline, a static-curve identity control, a prespecified structured morphology model, and a learned full-shape model, together with exposure-support diagnostics, endpoint-specific uncertainty, and one rule-coded joint or narrowed conclusion. No model has yet been fit and no outcome is presumed.

## Evidence-supported and unresolved claims

Direct inspection supports only availability and design feasibility: the Li2025 archive contains 40 composite specimens, 511 chronological RPT states, a measured 0.1C discharge curve and measured C/10 capacity at every state, and pulse-resistance summaries on a deterministic every-other-RPT schedule. It does not show that morphology predicts response.

Li et al. (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-57968-3, state in the accessible abstract that models can agree on capacity and resistance while differing in degradation modes. That establishes why capacity/resistance prediction cannot validate a unique internal mechanism; it does not establish this hypothesis. A focused public fetch inspected the abstract/opening material but not the complete paper or supplement (frozen source e61748d1748f109cd34dd23b65cb372431b8b6b39dff33bc0b110e7e824f0931). A Crossref record identifies Ibraheem, Strange, and dos Reis (2023), DOI 10.1016/j.jpowsour.2022.232477, as related constant-current-voltage forecasting work, but acquired full text was unavailable; no claim about its methods or results is imported.

The strongest present claim is that these measurements permit a bounded within-archive transport test. The unresolved claim is whether evolving shape contains response information beyond current measured state and dose. Even a supportive result would remain predictive/diagnostic association within one LG M50T experimental lineage, not proof of LLI, LAM, SEI growth, plating, dry-out, or any other mechanism.

## Hypotheses and estimands

The horizon is RPT t to RPT t+2, not t+1. Resistance is observed at all 265 even-numbered RPT states, at no odd-numbered state, and consequently has zero complete one-RPT changes but 225 complete two-RPT changes. Aligning both endpoints at two RPTs avoids outcome imputation and makes t+2 the next scheduled resistance observation for resistance-eligible rows.

For specimen i, let measured capacity C be "C/10 Capacity (mA.h)" and measured resistance R be "Mean_R (Ohms)". Define:

- capacity response Y-C = (C[t+2]-C[t])/C[0];
- resistance response Y-R = log(R[t+2]/R[t]), only when both values are observed and positive.

The fitted response can be added back to current state to report absolute C[t+2]/C[0] and log(R[t+2]/R[0]). With a fixed current-state offset, absolute-state and change error are algebraically the same; response is primary because it makes susceptibility and the exposure interval explicit. A separately tuned absolute-state fit is only a parameterization sensitivity and cannot rescue a failed response test.

Primary endpoint hypothesis H-C: the learned evolving-shape correction reduces family-balanced, specimen-balanced MAE for Y-C by at least 10% relative to the full scalar/exposure baseline under leave-one-family-out (LOFO) evaluation.

Key secondary endpoint hypothesis H-R applies the same 10% criterion to Y-R. The headline joint susceptibility claim requires both H-C and H-R. Support for one endpoint only must be reported as endpoint-specific evidence and not generalized to the other.

## Population, chronology, and feasibility

A specimen is "experiment directory|cell letter"; cell letters alone are not unique. Model-facing family labels are opaque E1-E5. Folder descriptions remain in audit files and are never tokenized as predictors.

| Family | Exact directory | Specimens | States | Capacity t-to-t+2 | Resistance t-to-t+2 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| E1 | Expt 1 - Si-based Degradation | 9 | 118 | 100 | 54 |
| E2 | Expt 2,2 - C-based Degradation 2 | 6 | 78 | 66 | 36 |
| E3 | Expt 3 - Cathode Degradation and Li-Plating | 9 | 107 | 89 | 47 |
| E4 | Expt 4 - Drive Cycle Aging (Control) | 8 | 80 | 64 | 32 |
| E5 | Expt 5 - Standard Cycle Aging (Control) | 8 | 128 | 112 | 56 |
| Total |  | 40 | 511 | 431 | 225 |

Dates span 2020-06-26 to 2021-07-22. Sort within specimen by parsed "RPT start date", require the unnamed CSV index to equal sequential RPT 0 through n-1, and create only exact t,t+1,t+2 triples. No later endpoint or curve can enter an index-time feature.

Resistance absence is scheduled: all 265 even-RPT values are observed and all 246 odd-RPT values are absent. Resistance outcomes are never forward-filled, backfilled, or interpolated. The 225 complete responses retain all 40 specimens. Capacity uses all 431 rows and is also scored on the 225 resistance-complete rows to expose population dependence.

Unfavorable observations remain. E5 specimen A has "Mean_R" 0.028214, 0.150686, and 0.031328 ohm at RPT2/4/6; all four supplied resistance summaries show the RPT4 excursion. It is not declared an artifact. Primary MAE retains it, while median absolute error, alternate resistance definitions, and leave-one-specimen-out influence analyses reveal sensitivity.

## Immutable source and table bindings

Read-only source "li_full":

- source path: [private path]
- runtime mount: /data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip
- SHA-256: 51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c

Catalog:

- source: [private path]
- runtime mount: /data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json
- SHA-256: 02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5

The supporting file "li2025_measured_binding_manifest.csv" enumerates all 551 required catalog table names and archive members: 511 discharge curves and 40 extracted summaries. All required columns were found.

Curve table pattern:
"li_full/SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{experiment-short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C discharge data.csv"

Required curve columns: "Time (s)", "Voltage (V)", "Current (mA)", "Charge (mA.h)", "Temperature (degC)".

Summary table pattern:
"li_full/SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{experiment-short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv"

Required summary columns: unnamed RPT index (catalog header empty string, read by pandas as "Unnamed: 0"), "Ageing Sets", "Ageing Cycles", "Age set start date", "Age set end date", "RPT start date", "Days of degradation", "Age set average temperature (degC)", "Charge Throughput (A.h)", "Energy Throughput (W.h)", "C/10 Capacity (mA.h)", "C/2 Capacity (mA.h)", "0.1s Resistance (Ohms)", "Mean_R (Ohms)", "R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)", and "R_100SOC (Ohms)".

Join summaries to curves one-to-one by exact experiment directory, cell, and parsed RPT. Assert catalog membership, columns, unique keys, sequential chronology, and equal state counts; abort rather than silently trim.

No DMA, fitted-capacity, fit-parameter, fit-RMSE, or simulation table is an input or outcome. This is the principal scientific change from the parent.

## Curve handling and separation of capacity from morphology

Keep rows with negative current and 450 <= |I| <= 550 mA. The audit found all 511 curves pass: minimum 15,733 unique active points, minimum active charge span 2,184.901 mAh, median currents from -500.199 to -499.573 mA, and median temperatures from 21.492 to 29.625 degrees C.

Before normalizing the horizontal coordinate, calculate current curve-derived discharge capacity Qcurve[t] = max(Q)-min(Q) from "Charge (mA.h)". It is included in every substantive baseline together with measured summary C[t]. Across 511 states its correlation with "C/10 Capacity" is 0.999999999971; their median difference is -0.00833 mAh (5th to 95th percentile -0.01000 to -0.00028 mAh). Thus a morphology claim cannot be credited for recovering the curve's length/capacity.

Set s = 1-(Q-Qmin)/(Qmax-Qmin) and interpolate voltage only at s=0.02,...,0.98 (97 points). Form delta-V[t](s)=V[t](s)-V[0](s), remove its least-squares affine component in s, and condition each coordinate using regressions fitted only in the current training partition on median active current, median curve temperature, both differences from RPT0, current summary capacity, and Qcurve[t]. This discards bulk capacity, offset, tilt, and acquisition-condition variation from the morphology channel. Unadjusted and non-detrended versions are sensitivities, not alternate positive-result searches.

## Intervening exposure and future-action boundary

The primary estimand is conditional on realized exposure between t and t+2. For each of the two intervening age sets, use only:

- increment in cumulative "Ageing Cycles";
- duration from "Age set start date" to "Age set end date";
- "Age set average temperature (degC)";
- elapsed days between index and target "RPT start date";
- nominal ageing temperature parsed from the summary member.

These fields at rows t+1 and t+2 are post-index information. Their use is valid only because the claim is an exposure-conditioned response association evaluated after exposure has been recorded. It is not a forecast available at RPT t, and the report must say so.

Do not use post-index "Charge Throughput (A.h)" or "Energy Throughput (W.h)" in primary models: they are accumulated electrical quantities that may reflect achieved operation and voltage response. Do not use future capacity, resistance, curve, fitted output, or simulation. A prespecified t-only forecast sensitivity removes every post-index exposure field; it answers a different deployment question and cannot be conflated with the primary estimand.

Two-RPT cycle dose is family-specific: E1=514, E2/E3/E4=1034, and E5=156 cycles. Under strict cross-family support calipers (same nominal temperature; current normalized capacity +/-0.01; latest normalized resistance +/-0.05; cycle-dose ratio within 1.25; RPT gap +/-14 d; exposure temperature +/-3 degrees C), E1 and E5 have zero supported rows because their dose is absent from the other families. E2-E4 provide 104 supported capacity rows (28/41/35) and 55 resistance rows (11/23/21), with 290 and 116 candidate edges respectively. Therefore five-family LOFO is a predictive extrapolation test for E1/E5, not a common-support causal comparison. Any common-support conclusion is limited to E2-E4. This limitation is frozen and cannot be hidden by pooled results.

## Comparable models and what each can reveal

All models use identical endpoint rows, exposure definition, outer folds, target scaling, and inner selection.

P0 — trivial response baseline. Training-family median response within nominal-temperature strata, with fallback to the training-wide median. This checks whether complexity beats a transparent exposure-stratified constant.

B0 — simple measured-state/exposure baseline. Fit separate standardized ridge models for capacity and resistance. Inputs available at t are current C[t]/C[0], current Qcurve[t]/Qcurve[0], their discrepancy, causal backward capacity changes and Theil-Sen slope, latest measured R/R[0] plus staleness for capacity rows, directly observed current R/R[0] and prior even-RPT resistance changes for resistance rows, RPT index, prior cumulative cycles and elapsed time, nominal temperature, and current curve median temperature/current. Add declared two-interval cycle counts, durations, temperatures, and total RPT gap. Missing-history indicators are explicit. Use fixed main effects and temperature-by-log-dose interactions; select ridge alpha from 10^-4,...,10^4. No family code is used.

S0 — static identity/protocol control. Add the 97-point RPT0 curve shape to B0, passed through the same residualization and PLS component search as B2. This measures how much specimen/batch/protocol identity present before ageing predicts response.

B1 — prespecified structured evolving shape. Add fixed summaries of condition-adjusted, affine-detrended delta-V[t](s) to B0: signed and absolute area and RMS in five fixed s windows, plus locations/prominences of fixed-rule derivative extrema after Savitzky-Golay order 3/window 11. Ridge uses the B0 grid. B1 can localize predictive voltage regions but cannot name electrode reactions.

B2 — learned distributed evolving shape. Add all 97 condition-adjusted, affine-detrended delta-V[t](s) coordinates to B0. Fit a PLS residual correction with 1-12 components, bounded by rank and selected by inner family-held-out validation. Construct its target from cross-fitted B0 residuals, never in-sample residuals. B2 preserves distributed deformation that B1 summaries may lose. B2 is primary; B1 is explanatory and cannot rescue failed B2.

S0 and B2 have matched preprocessing, component grids, targets, and folds. Primary contrasts are B2 versus B0 (morphology beyond scalar and curve-derived capacity) and B2 versus S0 (evolving signal beyond static identity). A neural sequence model is deferred: 40 independent specimens and five families do not justify extra capacity before a stable lower-rank signal exists. Revisit only with more independent families or reproducible residual structure.

## Splits, scoring, and controls

Primary evaluation is five-fold LOFO: every specimen, state, exposure record, and outcome from one experiment family is held out. Inner selection leaves one of four training families out. All transforms, imputers, residualizers, target scales, ridge penalties, PLS components, and conformal residuals are fitted inside training partitions. No random row split is permitted.

Within each endpoint and held family, average absolute errors over RPTs within specimen, then specimens; average the five family scores equally. Define I = 1-MAE(B2)/MAE(B0). Report B2-versus-S0 identically, every family effect, MAE in physical response units, RMSE as outlier-sensitive context, and reconstructed absolute-state error. Capacity and resistance are never pooled into one unscaled loss.

Required negative controls:

1. Static identity: S0 replaces evolving morphology with RPT0 shape. B2 must beat S0; otherwise static specimen/protocol information explains the gain.
2. Within-specimen time permutation: permute delta-V[t] among eligible times within each specimen, separately inside training and held partitions, preserving specimen/family identity and marginal chronology while breaking state-response alignment. Refit over 1,000 seeds.
3. Lag control: replace current delta-V[t] with the most recent available delta-V[t-2], with an early-row missing flag. Equal performance narrows the result to persistent history, not current evolving signal.
4. Target shuffle: shuffle complete response trajectories among training specimens within family and nominal temperature. Any retained outer advantage is a leakage/computation failure.
5. Exposure boundary: rerun without all post-index exposure variables. Results from this t-only branch are labeled forecast-like; disagreement does not invalidate the conditional estimand but changes deployment meaning.
6. Protocol encoding: classify family from RPT0 shape, evolving shape, and exposure separately under specimen-held-out folds. Predictability diagnoses identity encoding but is not proof of confounding.

For resistance, repeat the complete analysis with "0.1s Resistance", "R_80to48_SOC", and "R_100SOC"; all share the same 265-state schedule. Retain all values in primary analysis. Report median absolute error, Huber-loss fitting sensitivity, and leave-one-specimen-out influence; support for H-R requires the gain sign to survive removal of each single specimen, including E5|A.

## Uncertainty and frozen interpretation

Use 10,000 paired hierarchical bootstrap replicates that resample specimens within each fixed held family and retain each sampled specimen's full trajectory. This quantifies finite-specimen uncertainty for these five families; it is not a five-family superpopulation interval. Report fold effects and a family sign count. Training-only group-conformal intervals are descriptive and report coverage and width by family and endpoint.

Support H-C or H-R only if, for that endpoint:

1. B2 improves on B0 by at least 10% and its 95% specimen-within-family bootstrap interval is above zero;
2. at least four of five family effects are positive and none worsens by more than 5%;
3. B2 improves on S0 overall and in at least four families;
4. the corresponding E2-E4 strict-common-support effect is positive;
5. time permutation and target shuffle remove the advantage;
6. acquisition-condition and absolute-state parameterization sensitivities retain the sign;
7. for resistance, the sign also survives every leave-one-specimen-out analysis and at least two alternative supplied resistance summaries.

The joint hypothesis is supported only if both endpoints satisfy these rules. A positive result supports only incremental prediction of measured response under recorded exposures and represented lineage.

Adverse at the planned effect size: an upper 95% bound below 0.10 rejects the stipulated 10% benefit for that endpoint. An upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm. If S0 matches B2, conclude static identity/protocol information, not evolving morphology, explains the apparent gain. If B0 performs as well as B2 after inclusion of both capacity measures, conclude morphology adds no detectable susceptibility information at this resolution.

Inconclusive: an interval crosses zero or 0.10; family effects conflict; gain exists only in E1/E5 exposure-extrapolation folds; common-support and all-row signs disagree; resistance depends on one specimen or one resistance definition; calibration is poor; or a negative control retains gain. Capacity-only or resistance-only support is endpoint-specific, not joint support.

Invalid: failed hashes/columns/joins/chronology, any future outcome or future curve used as input, post-index exposure described as known at t, target imputation, non-grouped splitting, or target-shuffle advantage. Repair and issue no scientific verdict.

A supportive result does not establish why capacity or resistance changed. An adverse result does not show that low-rate curves are useless under another horizon, chemistry, protocol, or endpoint. Stronger causal or mechanistic conclusions require planned exposure metadata, replicate pulse uncertainty, half-cell/reference-electrode or post-mortem evidence, electrochemical expert adjudication, and an independent cohort outside Li/Kirkaldy lineage.

## Outputs, compute, and verification

Required solver outputs: "source_audit.json", "source_manifest.csv", "state_table.parquet", "response_rows.parquet", "exposure_schema.json", "folds.csv", "features_schema.json", "predictions.parquet", "metrics.json", "common_support.csv", "bootstrap.parquet", "calibration.json", "negative_controls.json", "resistance_sensitivity.json", "exclusions.csv", "model_artifacts/", "environment.json", and "report.md". Each prediction records endpoint, model, outer/inner fold, family, specimen, t, target RPT, response, prediction, current-state offset, reconstructed future state, exposure branch, support flag, and sensitivity. Every numerical conclusion in "report.md" cites an output field.

The independent audit read the 835 MB archive in 20.2 s using 4 CPUs/8 GiB, joined all 511 curves, and generated the 551-row catalog-bound manifest. Proposed full execution is 8 CPUs, 32 GiB, zero GPUs, up to 7,200 s: approximately 15 minutes for cached curve extraction and 60-120 minutes for nested fits, controls, and bootstraps. GPU use offers no clear benefit for ridge/PLS at this size; this is a workload choice, not a claim that GPUs are unavailable.

The verifier can check hashes, exact members/columns, joins, resistance schedule, response construction, post-index exposure labeling, forbidden inputs, fold isolation, training-only processing, model/metric recomputation, controls, uncertainty units, and verdict mapping. It must reject a forecast-at-t claim from the conditional branch, any mechanism claim, joint support from one endpoint, all-family common-support language, or support after failed controls. It cannot establish causal exposure effects, measurement validity of the resistance excursion, novelty, microscopic mechanism, or external transport.

## Change from parent and deferred questions

The parent tests future OCV-fitted DMA state. This child removes every fitted-DMA product, changes the target to directly measured two-RPT capacity and scheduled resistance responses, conditions explicitly on intervening exposure, adds curve-derived capacity to B0, and introduces matched-complexity static-identity and evolving-signal controls. The audit newly establishes the deterministic resistance schedule, 431/225 endpoint counts, near identity of curve span and C/10 capacity, resistance influence risk, and absence of strict exposure support for E1/E5.

Not chosen: one-RPT response, because resistance has zero complete pairs; carrying resistance forward as an outcome, because it fabricates measurements; future charge/energy throughput, because it can encode achieved electrical response; fitted DMA as a covariate or endpoint, because it reintroduces same-curve fit coupling; and mechanistic labels from directory names. Revisit these only with denser resistance tests, prospectively declared schedules, fit-replicate uncertainty, or independent physical diagnostics.

# KIT operating-state EIS acquisition value

## Objective and evidence boundary

Determine whether the complete current operating-state EIS acquisition adds prospective information for the next room-state source-index change beyond the complete current room EIS and all measured second-acquisition metadata, and localize any value to repeated index frequencies, broader non-index geometry, or a reciprocal-temperature response representation.

This is an open-ended scientific computation. You must newly construct the cohort, fit the models, quantify uncertainty and controls, and report the conclusion warranted by the computed outputs. A favorable finding is not required.

The strongest evidence already supported is limited to the configured archive: it has 1,022,975 rows, 35,275 complete 29-frequency spectrum keys, and 228 filename-defined specimens, three under each of 76 opaque condition codes. A prior independent audit constructed 3,459 visits, 2,935 eligible paired transitions, and a primary cohort of 2,071 transitions from 167 specimens and 57 conditions. These counts are readiness expectations that you must independently reproduce, not supplied scientific results.

The unresolved primary hypothesis H-A is that, under the historical room-first sequence, complete current operating-state impedance improves condition-balanced prediction of the next source-defined room-EIS-index change by at least 10% RMSE relative to room EIS plus complete operating-acquisition metadata. The gain must transfer to held-out conditions and exceed specimen-pairing controls. H-S asks, only if H-A is supported, whether non-index operating geometry adds at least 5% beyond a four-frequency repeated-index acquisition. H-R asks whether a signed SOC-50/90 reciprocal-temperature secant adds transferable information beyond metadata while surviving state, order, pairing and near-isothermal controls.

The endpoint is a source-defined EIS index. It is not capacity, pulse/DC resistance, an independent assay, or a degradation-mechanism label. The archive cannot identify a causal temperature effect because condition nearly determines operating temperature, room EIS always precedes operating EIS, and elapsed procedure/rest/bookkeeping are not counterbalanced. Do not claim thermal causality, a specific microscopic mechanism, economic value, or physical equivalence of a retrospectively masked sparse scan.

## Bound sources

Use only these read-only runtime inputs:

- /data/75850054cd-kit-corrected-eis.zip, logical source kit_corrected_eis, 17,307,136 bytes, SHA-256 21f7942224c99bbcadb6c1ba3d229d5591a034c2d8785bfaf659fc8281078d34.
- /data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json, frozen catalog, SHA-256 02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5.

The ZIP contains exactly 228 semicolon-delimited members matching cell_eisv2_P###_<replicate>_S##_C##.csv. Parse condition P###, replicate 1/2/3, specimen P###_<replicate>, and audit-only hardware tokens S## and C## from each filename. The example table is kit_corrected_eis/cell_eisv2_P001_1_S01_C10.csv. Inspect and enumerate every member; do not assume that filename order is acquisition order.

Required source columns are:

timestamp_s, timestamp_origin, sd_block_id, cyc_charged, is_rt, soc_nom, valid, z_ref_init_mOhm, z_ref_now_mOhm, soh_imp, ocv_est_avg_V, t_avg_degC, eis_duration_s, uptime_ticks, seq_nr, freq_Hz, z_amp_mOhm, z_ph_deg, z_amp_comp_mOhm, z_ph_comp_deg, z_re_comp_mOhm, z_im_comp_mOhm.

The spectrum key is (specimen, timestamp_s, sd_block_id); append seq_nr for the row key. Verify filename identities, all headers, unique row keys, 29-row frequency grids, within-spectrum metadata constancy, finite keys, source hashes and catalog membership. Units are seconds, Hz, mOhm, degrees, volts and degrees Celsius as named in the headers.

Use the reliable non-index sequence set {3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,14,15,16,17,18,20,21,22,24}, corresponding respectively to 5000, 3125, 2083.3333, 1470.5883, 1000, 675.6757, 500, 312.5, 147.0588, 67.5676, 50, 31.25, 20.8333, 14.7059, 6.7568, 5, 3.125 and 1 Hz.

The source-index rows are 10, 2.0833, 0.5 and 0.2083 Hz with corrected sequence numbers {19,23,25,26}. The frozen proposal wrote seq_nr 27 for 0.2083 Hz, but direct source inspection shows seq_nr 26; seq_nr 27 is 0.1 Hz. This is a mechanical binding correction, not a scientific-design change. Select by frequency and verify the sequence number. Recompute each spectrum's mean raw z_amp_mOhm over these four rows and require absolute agreement with z_ref_now_mOhm no greater than 0.001 mOhm before using the index block.

## Cohort, chronology and outcome

1. Within specimen, sort spectrum keys by timestamp_s and start a visit after an adjacent gap greater than 48 hours. Also report complete 24-hour and 72-hour grouping flows and maximum chain-grouped visit duration.
2. For repeated (specimen, visit, is_rt, soc_nom), keep valid=1 spectra and select in this order: timestamp_origin=1; greatest number of finite primary corrected complex pairs; earliest timestamp_s; earliest sd_block_id. Never choose an operating duplicate by closeness to 25 degrees Celsius. Record every choice.
3. A room or operating state is complete when selected spectra exist at each soc_nom in {10,30,50,70,90}, each with at least 17 of the 18 reliable non-index corrected real/imaginary pairs. Represent one missing point with a mask; larger deficits are ineligible.
4. A unit at visit t requires the immediately previous raw visit t-1 to be room-complete, t to be room- and operating-complete, and the immediately next raw visit t+1 to be room-complete. Never skip an intervening visit. Require the current-to-next room-anchor interval to be 18 through 24 days inclusive.
5. The primary population also requires the absolute median across the five SOCs of T_op(t,s)-T_rt(t,s) to be at least 8 degrees Celsius. Reproduce 2,071 units, 167 specimens and 57 conditions or stop with a transparent audit failure.
6. Define room anchor A_v as the median timestamp of the five selected room spectra. Define I_v as the median z_ref_now_mOhm at SOC 30, 50 and 70. The current information cutoff is the maximum timestamp of every current room or operating predictor spectrum.
7. Fit future level F_t=I_(t+1). For each out-of-fold prediction, compute h_t=(A_(t+1)-A_t)/86400, observed Y_t=21*(I_(t+1)-I_t)/h_t and predicted Yhat_t=21*(Fhat_t-I_t)/h_t. Future interval and endpoint data may only define and score the outcome; they cannot tune, preprocess or predict.
8. Assert all predictor timestamps are at or before the cutoff and all future endpoint components are later. Report current-to-next horizons and cutoff-to-future leads.
9. Inference is conditional on a complete next check-up. Report excluded conditions and specimens; do not assume non-informative follow-up.

For C scored conditions, m_c eligible specimens in condition c, and n_ci transitions in specimen i, use transition weight 1/(C*m_c*n_ci). Recompute analogous normalized training weights inside each fold.

## Frozen split

Assign conditions to five outer folds by sorting SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string KIT_EIS_acq_v2: plus condition separately within the approximately 0, 10 and 40 degree Celsius operating-temperature strata, then round-robin. Each condition, specimen and visit stays in one fold. Save the literal mapping and exact stratum rule. Inner tuning must also be condition-grouped and stratum-balanced. Repeat the complete outer pipeline with five prespecified alternative salt suffixes 1 through 5 as a sensitivity; do not replace the primary split.

## Model ladder

Use identical units, target, folds, weights, inner loss and train-only preprocessing for every model. Fit weighted ridge with block-specific penalties from 10^-4 through 10^4 on a log10 integer grid. If inner losses are within 1%, choose fewer components and then stronger regularization.

Report three elementary predictors: no change in the future level, prior normalized slope persistence, and outer-training equal-condition mean rate.

B-scalar includes I_t, prior normalized index slope, log acquisition age, previous interval, current room-temperature median and range, five room OCV values, finite-point, duplicate and timestamp-origin indicators, and cyc_charged.

B-RT adds current room corrected signed complex impedance at all five SOCs and the 18 non-index frequencies. Fit eight fixed cubic B-spline functions over log10 frequency separately for each SOC and real/imaginary channel, yielding 80 coefficients. Standardize using outer training only and apply outer-training SVD rank q in {4,8,12,16,24}.

B-T is the primary comparator. Add to B-RT, without operating impedance, all five operating temperatures and room differences, reciprocal-temperature differences, operating-minus-room OCV differences, acquisition lags, duration differences, finite masks, timestamp-origin indicators, observed temperature-stratum indicator and source counter difference. Never include condition or hardware identity. eis_duration_s may enter B-T as observed full-acquisition metadata because this task tests the acquired complete second-state bundle; it must not be represented as impedance.

A-index adds, at each of five operating SOCs, the four individual raw amplitudes at 10, 2.0833, 0.5 and 0.2083 Hz. Recompute but do not add their collinear mean. Residualize the 20 values on B-T using outer training only and fit a separately penalized block. This is same-assay information, not an independent endpoint.

A-shape adds operating corrected signed complex impedance at the same 18 non-index frequencies and five SOCs. Use the same 80-coefficient spline representation, residualize on B-T in outer training, then apply outer-training SVD q in {4,8,12,16,24}; fit a separate penalty.

A-full combines A-index and A-shape with separate penalties. Primary impedance-specific gain is A-full versus B-T. Also report A-full versus B-RT for the whole observed second-state bundle and B-T versus B-RT for metadata value. Report A-full versus A-index and A-full versus A-shape for localization.

R-sec is the structured alternative. At SOC 50 and 90 for every non-index frequency and channel compute (Z_op-Z_rt)/(1000/(T_op+273.15)-1000/(T_rt+273.15)). Fit 32 spline coefficients, residualize on B-T in outer training, apply SVD q in {2,4,8,12,16}, and use a separate penalty. It is a two-point reciprocal-temperature secant, not an activation energy, equilibrium derivative or isolated thermal effect.

A-full and R-sec must receive comparable tuning budgets. A neural sequence model and DRT inversion are deferred because only 57 independent condition groups are available and neither more cleanly adjudicates the acquisition source. Revisit them only if residual surfaces show stable held-condition structure not represented by splines/SVD or if repeated temperatures and equilibration metadata become available.

## Scoring, uncertainty and controls

Pool each out-of-fold prediction exactly once. Compute condition-balanced weighted RMSE and MAE, per-condition and per-specimen losses, temperature-stratum, age, lead, sparse-condition and first-transition summaries. For any model M relative to comparator B define G=1-RMSE_M/RMSE_B.

Bootstrap whole conditions 10,000 times within temperature stratum. Save all draw-level gains, percentile and BCa 95% intervals, and leave-one-condition-out jackknife gains. This is fixed-pipeline sensitivity across the 57 observed conditions, not full retraining uncertainty or a random-protocol superpopulation claim.

In each of the 54 primary conditions retaining all three specimens, enumerate the five non-identity donor mappings. Substitute each donor's complete second-acquisition block at the same ordinal visit; if absent use nearest room-anchor age within 10.5 days and report distance. Keep B-T and label fixed. Exclude unmatched units only from the shuffle metric, require at least 90% coverage, and make 10,000 stratum-balanced null draws by choosing one non-identity mapping independently per condition. Conditions with fewer than three eligible specimens remain in primary scoring but not pairing adjudication.

Run and report these controls:

- direct A-full, A-index and A-shape on approximately 25 degree Celsius paired transitions;
- SOC-50/90 A-shape and R-sec with both absolute OCV difference no greater than 20 mV and lag no greater than 24 hours;
- room-first lag and source-counter differences;
- each temperature stratum and leave-one-stratum-out extrapolation;
- raw amplitude/phase reconstruction of signed complex values;
- deliberate future-feature leakage failure and permuted-future-label sham;
- 24/72-hour visit grouping, complete 18/18 spectra, first transition only, removal of conditions with fewer than five transitions, and five alternative split salts.

Index rows cannot enter B-RT, B-T, A-shape or R-sec. Report correction/sign instability and any invalid baseline or chronology rather than suppressing it.

## Prespecified interpretation

Use 10% as the smallest important primary gain and 5% as the futility margin. Apply invalidity/inconclusive checks before supportive or adverse labels.

Primary H-A is supportive only when A-full versus B-T has point gain at least 0.10, condition-bootstrap lower 95% bound greater than zero, A-full MAE no worse than B-T, observed gain exceeds the trajectory-permutation 95th percentile, at least 45 conditions remain, and direction does not reverse under strict OCV+lag, first-transition, correction/sign, sparse-condition and split-salt checks.

Classify H-A as adverse only when controls and chronology are valid, B-T beats no-change, pairing adjudication is valid, and either the upper 95% bound is below 0.05 or A-full is worse than B-T. If A-full beats B-RT but not B-T, attribute value only to metadata. This does not imply that EIS or paired-state testing is generally uninformative.

Classify H-A as inconclusive when chronology fails; B-T fails to beat no-change; fewer than 45 conditions survive; observed gain does not exceed the pairing-null 95th percentile; required controls reverse direction; the primary interval spans the 0.05 to 0.10 decision region; or neither supportive nor adverse criteria are met. Support for acquisition with unstable localization leaves required frequencies unresolved.

Only after supportive H-A may H-S support broad non-index sweep value: A-full must improve over A-index by at least 0.05, its multiplicity-adjusted lower 95% bound must exceed zero, and A-shape must be directionally consistent. If A-index accounts for the gain, support only a reduced repeated same-assay test and recommend a prospective sparse-acquisition experiment.

H-R is supportive only if R-sec versus B-T meets the 0.10 rule, exceeds the pairing null, is directionally consistent across cold/hot, strict OCV+lag, direct-difference and correction checks, and near-isothermal gain is materially smaller. Even then call it a transferable paired-state response signature, never causal thermal susceptibility.

## Required outputs

Write every path below directly under /workspace.

audit.json must contain schema_version, source and catalog hashes, archive/member/row/spectrum/visit counts, primary counts, index frequency-to-sequence map, index reconstruction error summary, schema/key/frequency/metadata checks, chronology checks, visit sensitivity counts, units, sign convention and an explicit data_scope string.

member_manifest.csv must have one row per archive member and columns member, condition, replicate, specimen, hardware_s, hardware_c, rows, spectra, header_sha256, schema_ok, filename_ok.

duplicate_resolution.csv must record specimen, visit_id, is_rt, soc_nom, every candidate spectrum key, validity and tie-break quantities, selected boolean and selection reason. pairing_flow.csv must record stage, n_units, n_specimens, n_conditions and exclusion reason.

transitions.parquet must contain transition_id, condition, specimen, current_visit, previous_visit, next_visit, A_t_s, A_next_s, cutoff_s, earliest_future_s, h_days, I_t, F_t, Y, weight, temp_stratum, delta_temp_median, fold and eligible_primary.

folds.json must store the primary salt, stratum rule, exact condition-to-fold map and five sensitivity maps.

room_features.parquet, operating_index_features.parquet, operating_shape_features.parquet and response_features.parquet must each key rows by transition_id, retain feature names and masks, and contain no future endpoint or future interval feature. basis_svd_diagnostics.json must record knots/basis definition, train-only scaler/SVD dimensions, chosen ranks, penalties, fold-level diagnostics and loading surfaces.

predictions.parquet must have exactly one row per primary transition and model for no-change, prior-slope, condition-mean, B-scalar, B-RT, B-T, A-index, A-shape, A-full and R-sec, with columns transition_id, model, fold, y_true, y_pred and weight.

metrics.json must contain weighted primary RMSE/MAE for every model, all named ladder contrasts, per-condition/per-specimen summaries and effect thresholds. uncertainty.json must contain, for each decision contrast, point gain, exactly 10,000 condition-bootstrap gain draws, percentile and BCa intervals, leave-one-condition-out gains and any multiplicity-adjusted interval.

trajectory_permutations.parquet must contain 10,000 draws with draw_id, a complete auditable non-identity mapping assignment for each of 54 conditions, matched coverage and null_gain. sensitivities.csv must include sensitivity, model, comparator, n_units, n_conditions, gain_rmse, direction_reversal, valid and notes for every required control.

conclusions.json must state primary_status as supportive, adverse or inconclusive; broad_spectrum_status; response_status; the exact computed evidence fields used by each decision rule; supported_claims; unsupported_claims; limitations; and required_next_evidence. Each claim must cite output paths and metric keys, not prose alone.

A complete submission includes all outputs, one prediction per unit/model, finite values, internally consistent arithmetic, train/test isolation evidence and a rule-linked interpretation. Preserve adverse and inconclusive results.

## What verification can and cannot establish

The verifier checks hashes, archive schema/member identities, corrected index mapping, population and chronology invariants, fold isolation, weight and target arithmetic, feature/prediction coverage, metric arithmetic, resampling summaries, pairing mappings and consistency of conclusions with the prespecified rules. It rejects favorable overclaims, adverse overclaims and unsupported causal/mechanistic language.

Passing does not prove H-A, temperature causality, degradation mechanism, economic utility, protocol equivalence or external transfer. Those require expert scientific review, missing condition/protocol records, counterbalanced temperature/order measurements with matched SOC/OCV/rest, independent capacity or pulse outcomes, measured acquisition cost, a prospective reduced-acquisition trial and external validation.

## Resource envelope

The prior source audit used 4 CPUs and 32 GiB for 85.2 seconds. Plan the full study for up to 16 CPUs, 64 GiB, no GPU and approximately 4 to 6 hours; the allowed solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. GPU use is unnecessary for this frozen method. Readiness checks only imports, bindings, hashes, headers and a tiny index-map sample; readiness is not a solved experiment.

# Proposal: Does the complete second operating-state EIS acquisition add prospective value, and which information carries it?

## Scientific question, evidence boundary, and substantive repair

### Strongest claim already supported

The configured KIT_EIS archive contains 1,022,975 rows, 35,275 complete 29-frequency spectra, and 228 filename-defined specimens, exactly three under each of 76 opaque condition codes. It contains repeated source-labelled room-state (`is_rt=1`) and operating-state (`is_rt=0`) EIS, measured temperature, nominal SOC, estimated OCV, validity, timestamps, and acquisition metadata. The acquired full public article by Luh and Blank describes check-up EIS and other modalities, but the configured snapshot contains only selected corrected EIS; capacity/EOC, pulse, raw logs, equilibration records, operating-temperature setpoints, and the condition dictionary are unavailable.

The selected parent established two essential limits. First, `z_ref_now_mOhm` is the rounded mean of raw amplitudes at 0.2083, 0.5, 2.0833, and 10 Hz, hence a source-defined EIS index rather than an independent pulse/DC-resistance or capacity outcome. Second, paired room/operating observations are not a randomized temperature intervention: temperature is almost condition-coded, operating EIS always follows room EIS, and the source cycle counter changes uniformly by -1.

An independent full-archive stress audit (job `job-d1dc291361c4e03d63e5b1ef`, output SHA-256 `d08fa4d2650612f615016651aa2904b609edbc244cf6a513794168950814a474`) reproduced 35,275 spectra, 3,459 constructed visits, 2,935 eligible paired transitions, and the parent's 2,071-unit primary population from 167 specimens and 57 conditions. It found 573/697/801 transitions in the approximately 0/10/40 °C strata, respectively. All 2,071 units contain the four index-defining rows at SOC 50 and 90. A strict joint sensitivity requiring both SOC-50/90 |operating-room OCV| <=20 mV and lag <=24 h retains 1,545 transitions, 158 specimens, and 55 conditions. Thus those controls are feasible rather than merely aspirational.

### Consequential flaw in the parent

The parent's scientific response question is valid, but its stated adverse acquisition decision is not. Its sole primary alternative adds a reciprocal-temperature-normalized, non-index response at SOC 50 and 90. It then treats failure of that representation as evidence that collecting the second operating spectrum has no useful increment. That conclusion does not follow: the acquired spectrum can carry useful forecast information through (a) direct operating-state geometry not well represented by a two-point reciprocal-temperature secant, (b) SOC 10/30/70 observations, or (c) the four low-frequency amplitudes that define the source index. Excluding these channels is appropriate for a narrow non-index temperature-response claim, but not for a decision about whether the second acquisition is worth collecting.

This child repairs the mismatch by making a complete second-acquisition model the primary test and retaining the parent's secant as a prespecified structured alternative. A nested decomposition distinguishes a cheap four-frequency repeat, broader non-index spectral geometry, and a temperature-oriented secant. The population, temporal boundaries, future endpoint, condition-held-out estimand, and evidence limits remain unchanged.

### Unresolved falsifiable hypotheses

**Primary acquisition hypothesis H-A:** Under the historical room-first check-up sequence, the complete current operating-state EIS acquisition adds at least 10% condition-balanced predictive RMSE improvement for the next source-defined room-EIS-index change beyond scalar history, the complete current room EIS, and all measured second-acquisition temperature, OCV, timing, duration, and quality metadata. The increment must transfer to held-out condition codes and exceed specimen-pairing controls.

**Nested localization hypothesis H-S:** If H-A is supported, non-index operating-spectrum geometry adds information beyond an operating-state four-frequency index-only acquisition. This is the claim required to recommend retaining a broad EIS sweep rather than a reduced low-frequency repeat.

**Secondary response hypothesis H-R:** A signed SOC-50/90 reciprocal-temperature secant adds transferable information beyond the metadata baseline and survives near-isothermal, state-match, order/lag, and pairing controls. This can support a paired-state response signature, but never causal thermal susceptibility.

The primary null/futility claim is that the full second acquisition improves RMSE by less than 5% or is reproduced after breaking specimen pairing. Failure of H-R alone does not falsify H-A. Conversely, improvement confined to the four endpoint frequencies supports only repeated low-frequency same-assay value, not spectrum-wide or thermal-response value.

## Exact read-only data binding

- Logical source: `kit_corrected_eis`.
- Source ZIP: `[private path]`; 17,307,136 bytes; SHA-256 `21f7942224c99bbcadb6c1ba3d229d5591a034c2d8785bfaf659fc8281078d34`.

Recompute each spectrum's four-frequency amplitude mean and require agreement with `z_ref_now_mOhm` within 0.001 mOhm before using the index block.

## Population, pairing, time, and outcome

1. Within specimen, order spectrum keys by `timestamp_s`; begin a visit after an adjacent gap greater than 48 h. Report 24 h and 72 h sensitivity flows and maximum chain-grouped visit duration.
2. For repeated `(specimen,visit,is_rt,soc_nom)`, select among `valid=1` spectra by `timestamp_origin=1`, then the greatest number of finite primary complex pairs, then earliest `timestamp_s,sd_block_id`. Do not select operating duplicates by closeness to 25 °C.
3. A room or operating visit state is complete when all five `soc_nom in {10,30,50,70,90}` have selected spectra with at least 17 of 18 finite primary corrected complex points. Fit one missing point with a mask; a larger deficit is ineligible.
4. A forecast unit at visit t requires the immediately previous raw visit t-1 to be room-complete, t to be room-and-operating-complete, and the immediately next raw visit t+1 to be room-complete. Never skip an intervening visit. Require the current-to-next room-anchor interval to be 18–24 days.
5. The primary population additionally requires `|median_s(T_op(t,s)-T_rt(t,s))| >= 8 °C`. The independently reproduced flow is 2,071 transitions, 167 specimens, and 57 conditions; solvers must recompute it.
6. Define room anchor `A_v` as the median timestamp of the five selected room spectra and `I_v=median_{s in {30,50,70}} z_ref_now_mOhm(v,s)`. The current information cutoff is the maximum timestamp of every current room/operating predictor spectrum.
7. Fit future level `F_t=I_(t+1)`. Transform each out-of-fold prediction to `Yhat_t=21*(Fhat_t-I_t)/h_t`, where `h_t=(A_(t+1)-A_t)/86400`; score against `Y_t=21*(I_(t+1)-I_t)/h_t`. The future interval is used only to define and score the outcome, never as a predictor or tuning feature.
8. Assert every predictor timestamp is at or before cutoff and every future endpoint component is later. The stress audit found 20.027–22.039-day horizons and 457.25–512.67 h from cutoff to the earliest future endpoint.
9. Inference is conditional on a complete next check-up. Report excluded conditions/specimens and do not assume non-informative follow-up.

## Matched model ladder

All models use identical forecast units, target, folds, hierarchical weights, inner loss, and train-only preprocessing. Fit weighted ridge with block-specific penalties selected from `10^-4,...,10^4`; ties within 1% choose fewer components and stronger regularization.

### B-scalar: simple baseline

Use `I_t`, prior normalized index slope, log acquisition age, previous interval, current room-temperature median/range, five room OCV values, finite-point/duplicate/origin indicators, and `cyc_charged`. Also report no-change, prior-slope persistence, and outer-training equal-condition mean-rate predictors.

### B-RT: strong room-spectrum baseline

Add current room corrected signed complex EIS on the 18 non-index frequencies at all five SOCs. Fit eight fixed cubic B-spline functions over log10 frequency separately by SOC and real/imaginary channel (80 coefficients), standardize on outer training only, and reduce with outer-training SVD rank `q in {4,8,12,16,24}`.

### B-T: metadata-complete acquisition baseline and primary comparator

Add to B-RT, without operating impedance, all five operating temperatures and room differences, reciprocal-temperature differences, operating-minus-room OCV differences, acquisition lags, duration differences, finite masks, timestamp-origin indicators, the observed temperature-stratum indicator, and the source counter difference. This asks what is learned from knowing when and under what measured state the second acquisition occurred without using its impedance values. No condition or hardware identity enters.

### A-index: reduced four-frequency repeat

For each of five operating SOC spectra, add the four individual raw `z_amp_mOhm` values at 10, 2.0833, 0.5, and 0.2083 Hz (20 values); recompute their mean as an audit quantity rather than adding a collinear predictor. Residualize the 20 values on B-T within outer training and apply that map unchanged to validation/test. Fit them as a separately penalized block. This represents the least expensive acquisition contained in the archive that can reproduce the source index; it is not independent of the endpoint assay.

### A-shape: direct non-index operating-spectrum alternative

Add the operating corrected signed complex spectrum on the same 18 frequencies and all five SOCs to B-T. Use the same 8-by-5-by-2 spline representation as B-RT. Residualize all 80 coefficients on B-T in outer training, apply an outer-training SVD with `q in {4,8,12,16,24}`, and fit a separately penalized score block. Because B-T already contains room geometry and acquisition metadata, these residual scores represent operating impedance not predictable from the room spectrum or measured acquisition state. They preserve direct level and SOC geometry that a reciprocal-temperature secant can discard.

### A-full: primary acquisition-complete alternative

Combine A-index and A-shape with separate penalties. The primary impedance-specific contrast is A-full versus B-T. Also report A-full versus B-RT as the value of the entire observed second-state bundle and B-T versus B-RT as the part attributable to its metadata. If only the bundle contrast improves, the evidence supports measured temperature/OCV/timing information, not collecting impedance. A-full versus B-T is the strongest available test of whether operating impedance itself has prospective value because it includes every prespecified quality-qualified impedance channel while controlling all room and metadata information.

### R-sec: structured response alternative

For SOC 50 and 90 and each non-index frequency/channel, compute

`R=(Z_op-Z_rt)/(1000/(T_op+273.15)-1000/(T_rt+273.15))`.

Fit the parent's 32 spline coefficients, residualize them on B-T in outer training, apply SVD rank `q in {2,4,8,12,16}`, and add them with a separate penalty. This two-point reciprocal-temperature secant can align cold/hot direction and reveal a compact response signature, but it is not an activation energy, equilibrium derivative, or isolated temperature effect.

A-full and R-sec are comparably specified on the same target, units, folds, controls, and tuning budget. A-full answers the acquisition question without imposing a thermal-response form; R-sec tests whether a scientifically structured response compresses the useful signal. A neural sequence model and DRT inversion are deferred: only 57 independent condition groups are available, and neither adds a cleaner adjudication of acquisition source. Revisit them only if direct residual surfaces show stable held-out-condition structure that spline/SVD cannot represent or if repeated temperatures and equilibration metadata become available.

## Split, weighting, uncertainty, and pairing test

Assign conditions to five outer folds by sorting SHA-256 of `"KIT_EIS_acq_v2:"+condition` separately within the approximately 0, 10, and 40 °C strata, then round-robin. Each fold contains 3–4 held-out conditions per stratum; every specimen and visit of a condition stays together. Inner tuning repeats condition-grouped, stratum-balanced folds. Save the literal fold map. A five-salt repeated-fold sensitivity assesses partition dependence without replacing the frozen primary split.

For C conditions in a scored set, m_c eligible specimens in condition c, and n_ci transitions for specimen i, assign each transition weight `w_cit=1/(C*m_c*n_ci)`. Use the corresponding training-fold normalization for fitting/tuning. Pool each out-of-fold prediction once. Report condition-balanced RMSE and MAE, `G_full=1-RMSE_A-full/RMSE_B-T`, all ladder contrasts, per-condition/specimen losses, temperature strata, age, lead, sparse conditions, and first-transition cold start.

Bootstrap whole conditions 10,000 times within temperature stratum and report percentile/BCa intervals and leave-one-condition-out jackknife. This is fixed-pipeline sensitivity to the 57 observed designed conditions, not proof about a random protocol superpopulation and not full model-training uncertainty.

The parent's “nearest-age bin” shuffle is replaced by an exact, auditable trajectory permutation. In each of the 54 primary conditions retaining all three specimens, enumerate the five non-identity specimen mappings. For each recipient transition, substitute the donor specimen's complete second-acquisition block at the same ordinal visit; if absent, use the nearest room-anchor age within 10.5 days and report the match distance. Keep B-T and the label fixed. Exclude unmatched units from the shuffle metric only, require at least 90% coverage, compute each condition's five mapped losses, and form 10,000 stratum-balanced null draws by choosing one non-identity map independently per condition. The three conditions with fewer than three eligible specimens remain in primary scoring but cannot adjudicate pairing. A shuffled gain comparable to the observed gain means the value is condition/age-level rather than specimen-specific.

## Prespecified controls and interpretation

- **Acquisition estimands:** report A-full versus B-RT (entire second-state bundle), B-T versus B-RT (metadata component), and A-full versus B-T (impedance-specific value). A metadata-only gain cannot justify collecting EIS.\n- **Full-versus-reduced acquisition:** compare A-full with A-index and A-shape. This prevents a result confined to endpoint frequencies from being called broad-spectrum value.
- **Near-isothermal sequence control:** apply direct A-full/A-index/A-shape representations to the approximately 25 °C paired transitions. Gain there remains valid repeated-acquisition information but defeats a temperature-response interpretation.
- **State control:** rerun A-shape and R-sec using only SOC 50/90 with both |ΔOCV|<=20 mV; jointly impose lag <=24 h. The audit shows 1,545 units/55 conditions survive both restrictions.
- **Fixed-order limit:** report room-first lag and source-counter difference. No model result identifies temperature rather than elapsed time, rest, intervening procedure, or bookkeeping.
- **Temperature-stratum control:** report approximately 0/10/40 °C separately and leave one stratum out as extrapolation. Single-stratum gain does not establish a general response.
- **Index provenance:** A-index uses recomputed raw amplitudes. Index rows never enter B-RT, B-T, A-shape, or R-sec. Improvement confined to A-index supports only a reduced repeated assay.
- **Correction/sign:** reconstruct signed complex values from raw amplitude/phase and repeat shape models; unstable loadings bar interpretation.
- **Chronology/sham:** audit cutoff, ensure future features fail a deliberate leakage test, and require permuted future labels to show no gain.
- **Visit/sparsity:** repeat 24/72 h grouping, complete-case 18/18 spectra, first transition only, removal of conditions with fewer than five transitions, and alternative fold salts.

The smallest important primary effect is 10% RMSE reduction; 5% is the futility margin.

- **Supportive acquisition result:** A-full versus B-T has point `G_full>=10%`, condition-bootstrap lower 95% bound above zero, MAE not worse, and observed gain exceeds the trajectory-permutation 95th percentile; direction does not reverse under strict OCV+lag, first-transition, correction, sparse-condition, and fold-salt checks. Conclude that operating-state impedance, beyond the observed second-state metadata, adds prospective information for this source-defined endpoint; separately report the total bundle contrast versus B-RT.
- **Broad-spectrum localization:** only after primary support, conclude non-index sweep value if A-full improves over A-index by at least 5% with a multiplicity-adjusted lower bound above zero and A-shape is directionally consistent. If A-index accounts for the gain, recommend testing a reduced four-frequency repeat rather than claiming full-spectrum value.
- **Response support:** conclude a transferable paired-state response signature only if R-sec versus B-T meets the 10% rule, exceeds pairing shuffle, remains directionally consistent across cold/hot, strict OCV+lag, direct-difference, and correction checks, and near-isothermal gain is materially smaller. This still is not causal thermal susceptibility.
- **Adverse acquisition result:** if the upper 95% bound for A-full versus B-T is below 5%, or A-full is worse while baselines and controls are valid, conclude no practically useful increment from operating impedance beyond the captured second-state metadata for this endpoint/horizon. If A-full versus B-RT improves while A-full versus B-T does not, attribute value only to the metadata bundle. This does not imply EIS or paired-state testing is generally uninformative.
- **Inconclusive:** the primary interval spans 5–10%; B-T fails no-change; pairing null is comparable; fewer than 45 conditions survive; results reverse under strict state/timing, correction, sparse-condition, or fold-salt checks; or chronology fails. A-full support with unstable localization supports acquisition value but leaves the necessary frequencies unresolved.

Operational cost-effectiveness still requires acquisition time/cost and a prospective decision analysis. A positive A-index result does not prove that four isolated frequencies acquired under a new protocol reproduce the historical scan; that requires a reduced-acquisition experiment.

## Deliverable, compute, and adjudication boundary

The future solver must newly construct the cohort and fit B-scalar, B-RT, B-T, A-index, A-shape, A-full, and R-sec. Required outputs are:

- `audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_resolution.csv`, `pairing_flow.csv`, and `transitions.parquet`;
- `folds.json`, `room_features.parquet`, `operating_index_features.parquet`, `operating_shape_features.parquet`, `response_features.parquet`, and basis/SVD diagnostics;
- `predictions.parquet`, `metrics.json`, `uncertainty.json`, `trajectory_permutations.parquet`, `sensitivities.csv`, and `conclusions.json`.

Completion requires one out-of-fold prediction per primary unit for every model, acquisition/localization contrasts, uncertainty, controls, loading surfaces, and a rule-linked supportive/adverse/inconclusive conclusion. Positive confirmation is not required.

The stress audit used 4 CPUs/32 GiB and completed in 85.2 s. The expanded nested linear/spline/SVD experiment is estimated at 12–16 CPUs, 64 GiB, no GPU, and 4–6 h including repeated fold sensitivities, 10,000 condition bootstraps, and trajectory permutations. This is within the configured 16-CPU, 262,144-MiB, 28,800-s solver envelope. GPU use is unnecessary for these small dense matrices; this is a workload choice, not a scientific merit claim.

An automatic verifier can recompute hashes, schemas, keys, frequencies, source-index reconstruction, visit/pair selection, chronology, fold isolation, hierarchical weights, train-only transformations, predictions, metrics, permutation mappings, resamples, and decision-rule consistency. It must accept correctly supported adverse and inconclusive results and reject an acquisition claim based only on R-sec or metadata.

A verifier cannot establish that the second acquisition acts through temperature, that the counter offset is a completed cycle, that electrical loadings name a degradation mechanism, that 10% is economically worthwhile, or that a reduced scan reproduces the full historical procedure. Those require scientific/expert review, the missing condition and protocol records, counterbalanced temperature/order measurements with matched SOC/OCV/rest, an independent capacity or pulse endpoint, acquisition costs, and external prospective validation.

## Literature and provenance

Luh and Blank, *Scientific Data* (2024), DOI `10.1038/s41597-024-03831-x`, was inspected through acquired full public XML (PMCID `PMC11405776`; source id `5c3de8fa937542c503c49aa0d7832107792c4f28fc8e9ad7cdadfe7403cbeabd`; SHA-256 `e55315f55e0b3ac2ce10deb1bcbe58a9babcac5e00a252ac058d27ee975ea115`). It supports the 228-cell/76-condition context and multi-state check-up measurements; the exact pairing, endpoint identity, temperature coding, timing, OCV, and control counts come from archive audits, not the article.

Zhang et al., *Nature Communications* (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`, remains conceptual precedent for spectrum-wide prediction. Only metadata/abstract were available in the inherited research record; no claim is made that its full methods or supplements were inspected, reproduced, or that it supports H-A.

The consequential acquisition question is whether measuring impedance before charge adds transferable prognostic information when a predictor already has ten measured discharge capacities and a complete rested-full-charge state-V spectrum. The proposed signal is the signed same-cycle response from state I before charging to state V after charging and 15 minutes of rest. This response may capture protocol-state dependence that an absolute V spectrum loses; it may instead be redundant, a better state-I snapshot, a stable specimen/contact offset, or a proxy for charge/rest duration.

Zhang et al. (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7, is available as inspected full-text XML (PMCID PMC7136228; source ID 33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79; SHA-256 ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144). ## Frozen identity policy

The state-IX files are used only as an auxiliary acquisition-clock identity audit, never as predictors or as a reason to move the I→V prediction boundary. For ten tokens, IX cycle c ends 0.000995–0.002005 s before the ox/red=1 charge portion of same-token capacity cycle c begins at every overlap. For EIS 25C02, this continuity occurs only with Capacity data/Data_Capacity_25C03.txt (table-bcf417da4b0ec35a; 201/201 overlapping cycles); for EIS 25C03 it occurs only with Capacity data/Data_Capacity_25C02.txt (table-c1a7d5457afe5054; 180/180). Same-label joins have zero exact handoffs. The auxiliary members are EIS data/EIS_state_IX_25C02.txt / table-bef5e6d817e378a9 and EIS data/EIS_state_IX_25C03.txt / table-34429864895747b9. The source audit zhang_v_ix_audit.py and result zhang_v_ix_audit.json record this evidence.

This is strong computational evidence of a 25C02/25C03 capacity-filename transposition, but not sufficient authority to relabel physical specimens. Therefore:

1. Confirmatory inference excludes EIS tokens 25C02 and 25C03 before any outcome fitting, tuning, calibration, or threshold evaluation.
2. Secondary sensitivity A is the acquisition-clock-resolved cross-map: EIS 25C02 uses capacity 25C03, and EIS 25C03 uses capacity 25C02.
3. Secondary sensitivity B is the literal filename-label map: each disputed EIS token uses the same-name capacity file.
4. Both sensitivities include all 12 cells, are dependent reanalyses of the same cohort, are not external or independent validation, and cannot overturn the ten-cell confirmatory conclusion. Their disagreement is identity-sensitive and requires author/data-owner or electrochemical expert adjudication.

## Pairing, protocol order, prediction time, and target

A complete I or V sweep has exactly 60 finite rows, 60 unique frequencies, and one Re/-Im pair at each canonical frequency. Pair only on EIS token and integer cycle c; never pair by row order, nearest timestamp, or capacity filename.

The executed streaming I/V audit found 2,788 complete V spectra and 2,788 complete same-cycle I/V pairs. Every pair satisfies max(time_I) < min(time_V); the minimum V-start minus I-end is 1,713.63462 s; all pairs have the same ordered 60-frequency grid; and the canonical JSON-grid SHA-256 is 651b878c886a5deb40c50a612343b25bbd45ff97c5919d49a76419517d54d226. Exact frequencies 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz must occur within 1e-5 Hz. I has extra late cycles for 25C01, 25C04–25C06, and 45C01, but no I-only cycle enters analysis. This verifies source feasibility, not prognosis.

State I is before charging. State V is after charge plus a 15-minute rest. Prediction is issued only when the complete V sweep finishes. Thus I and V are both available, but no capacity from c onward and no EIS after V is a predictor. States II–IV are deferred because the endpoint question is identifiable without a larger state search. States VI–IX are excluded as predictors because they occur after V and would change the acquisition decision and prediction boundary.

For specimen i, define Q[i,k] as the maximum finite positive Capacity/mA.h among primary ox/red=0 rows of capacity cycle k. Q is measured cycler discharge capacity in mAh, not SOC, a BMS estimate, a fitted state, or a mechanism label.

At prediction time for EIS cycle c, allowed information is Q[i,0] through Q[i,c-1], complete I(c) and V(c), c, and fixed protocol temperature. For H in {10,20}, the frozen outcome is un-clipped absolute measured loss:

L[i,c,H] = Q[i,c-1] - Q[i,c+H-1].

The future block is capacity cycles c through c+H-1. Retain negative loss from recovery or noise. Each horizon requires ten consecutive finite positive past capacities Q[c-10:c-1], complete paired I/V spectra, exact sparse bins, and finite positive Q[c+H-1]. Prohibit nearest-bin substitution, interpolation, future smoothing, outcome imputation, and late-life deletion.
