Normalize to
`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,point_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.
Set `specimen_key="G{group}_C{cell}"` and `point_index=1..35` in stored
order. Join only on
`(group,cell_id,SOC_label_pct,point_index)`. Require 66 canonical tables,
2,310 stage rows, 1,155 paired rows, and three SOCs by 35 points per
specimen-stage.

There is no row-level frequency field; `point_index` is not frequency. SOC
is supplied nominal metadata, not independently validated physical SOC,
coulomb-counted SOC, or a BMS estimate. Current sign, charge return, capacity
normalization, and SOC anchoring are unavailable.

## Frozen quotient and representation audit

For each specimen-stage form (Y), a 3-by-35 matrix in SOC order 20,50,80 and
stored point order. Let (u=(point_index-1)/34). Apply exactly
`SplineTransformer(n_knots=5,degree=3,knots="uniform",include_bias=False,extrapolation="constant")`
to (u). Residualize its six columns against (A=[1,u]), take deterministic
SVD, orient each retained left singular vector so its largest-absolute entry
is positive, and retain singular values exceeding (10^{-10}) of the
maximum. Require (U_A) of shape 35-by-2 and (V) of shape 35-by-5,
orthonormal and mutually orthogonal within (10^{-10}).

Use
(h_0=(1,1,1)/\sqrt3),
(h_1=(1,-1,0)/\sqrt2),
(h_2=(1,1,-2)/\sqrt6), and (H=[h_1,h_2]). Require
([h_0,H]) orthonormal within (10^{-12}). Define
(Z_{ct}=H^T Y_{ct}V) and reconstruct
(Y^{XS}_{ct}=H Z_{ct}V^T).

The endpoint is exactly unchanged by adding any specimen-stage SOC-common
35-point curve or arbitrary SOC-specific affine function of stored index.
The repaired fit is also invariant to orthogonal rotations of (H) or (V)
that leave (Y^{XS}) unchanged. Verify this numerically with fixed signed
orthogonal test rotations; require reconstructed predictions, losses, and
each scalar estimate to agree within (10^{-10}) relative error.

Audit common-affine, contrast-affine, common-non-affine, and
contrast-non-affine blocks and require reconstruction of the rank-21 smooth
projection within (10^{-10}) relative error. Report retained/discarded
energy by cell, stage, and SOC. The quotient can still retain SOC-dependent
non-affine fixture/contact effects.

## Matched baseline and substantive alternative

Let (X_i=Y^{XS}_{i,BoL}) and (Y_i=Y^{XS}_{i,MoL}). Code
`r=+1/-1` for C/2/C/4, `p=+1/-1` for short/long, and `rp`.
All models predict the same absolute (Y_i):

- **P, simple protocol-only baseline:** (Y_i=D(r_i,p_i,r_ip_i)+e_i).
- **U, fixed scientific baseline:** (Y_i=X_i+D(r_i,p_i,r_ip_i)+e_i).
- **A, learned scalar alternative:** (Y_i=\gamma X_i+D(r_i,p_i,r_ip_i)+e_i).

A asks whether the same full quotient geometry persists with one common
attenuation/amplification factor. It preserves linkage direction information
that P discards and permits non-unit transport that U forbids, without
estimating a rotation or coordinate-specific map.

For every fitting set (I), define training-only physical-grid scales
[
q_{sj}(I)=\max\{raw\_MAD_i(Y_{i,sj}:i\in I),10^{-6}\ \Omega\}.
]
Within each protocol group in (I), center (X_i) and (Y_i) at every
physical-grid location. Estimate
[
\hat\gamma_I=
\frac{\sum_g\sum_{i\in g}\sum_{s,j}
 (X_{i,sj}-\bar X_{g,sj})(Y_{i,sj}-\bar Y_{g,sj})/q_{sj}(I)^2}
 {\sum_g\sum_{i\in g}\sum_{s,j}
 (X_{i,sj}-\bar X_{g,sj})^2/q_{sj}(I)^2}.
]
This uses only within-protocol specimen contrasts and exactly the final loss
geometry. Require a finite denominator above (10^{-12}); otherwise A is
unestimable and that run is invalid/inconclusive.

After fixing `gamma` (0 for P, 1 for U, fitted above for A), vectorize
((Y_i-\gamma X_i)/q(I)) over the 105 physical-grid locations. Fit those
outputs from training-standardized `r,p,rp` with multi-output ridge and an
unpenalized intercept. Use
`alpha in {1e-4,1e-3,...,1e4}`, selected by mean inner
leave-one-specimen-out loss under the inner-training (q); ties choose the
larger alpha. Recompute group means, (q), protocol standardization,
zero-variance drops, (gamma), and coefficients inside every split. Positive
ridge gives a unique fit even when an inner training set lacks one protocol
combination; log its design rank and prediction leverage.

Use 11 outer leave-one-specimen-out folds. No held-cell MoL value may enter
fitting, scaling, tuning, or model choice. For model (m) and held cell (c),
[
L_{m,c}=105^{-1}\sum_{s,j}
[(Y_{c,sj}-\hat Y_{m,c,sj})/q_{sj}(I_c)]^2,
quad E_m=11^{-1}\sum_c L_{m,c}.
]
Set (G_U=1-E_U/E_P), (G_A=1-E_A/E_P), and
(G_{AU}=1-E_A/E_U). Select W as the larger-gain identity model, choosing U
on a tie, and set (G^*=\max(G_U,G_A)). Report raw-ohm RMSE, SOC-row losses
and gains, all predictions, cell differences, alphas, ranks, leverages, and
outer-fold (gamma).

The inherited 10-by-10 full ridge map is only a capacity diagnostic. With six
within-protocol specimen degrees of freedom in every outer fold, its
unobserved directions and apparent rotation are penalty-defined. It cannot
select W, enter the linkage statistic, rescue a primary failure, or support a
rotation claim.

## Exact linkage calibration and conditional uncertainty

Enumerate all (2!3!3!3!=432) within-group allocations, including identity.
Move each donor's complete three-SOC BoL bundle jointly to a recipient's fixed
protocol and MoL bundle. Rerun all nested U and A fits, including
training-only (q), scalar fitting, and tuning. P may be cached only after
exact equality checks. For allocation (a), compute
(T_a=\max(G_{U,a},G_{A,a})) and
(p_{link}=\#\{T_a\ge T_{observed}\}/432).

This max statistic adjusts selection between U and A. It tests only the sharp
conditional null that physical linkage is irrelevant within documented
protocol groups. It is not a treatment-randomization or population p-value.
Its finite-sample scientific interpretation requires within-group
exchangeability, which is unverified. The archive informed model development,
including this repair; therefore call (p_{link}) a conditional linkage tail
fraction and do not represent it as pristine external confirmation.

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, draw 10,000 resamples
independently within groups at sizes 2/3/3/3. Apply common multiplicities to
frozen outer losses for P/U/A and report percentile intervals for gains and
SOC-row gains. Separately refit full-data A in every resample using resample
(q), scalar fit, and alpha selection; report the (gamma) interval,
failure fraction, and fractions below 0, in [0,1], and above 1. These are
observed-cell weighting stability summaries, not population confidence
intervals. W is frozen from observed outer gains before stability summaries.

Delete each specimen and rerun the complete observed nested pipeline on the
remaining ten, keeping W fixed for stability assessment. Flag folds that lack
a training member from the held protocol; they remain conservative
extrapolation stress tests and are not reinterpreted as within-protocol
validation. Repeat with spline `n_knots=4` and 6, alpha grid extended one
decade, and equal-group rather than equal-specimen weighting. Report every
reversal and boundary selection.

Retain the parent's nuisance-localization companions: run the same
metric-aligned P/U/A, max-model 432-allocation calibration, stability, and
deletion pipeline on (i) the complete rank-21 smooth projection and (ii) the
two-coordinate common-affine block. Holm-adjust the two companion tail
fractions. Contrast-affine and common-non-affine analyses remain descriptive.
The label **nuisance-compatible concentration** is allowed only if the primary
result is adverse and each companion has gain at least 0.10, adjusted tail
fraction at most 0.05, positive stability lower bound, positive gain in every
deletion with at least 9/11 at or above 0.10 for the full projection, and no
SOC-row gain at or below -0.10. This label never establishes fixture/contact
causation.

## Frozen outcome rules and falsification

The 10% relative-loss threshold is a dataset-scale materiality margin, not a
validated engineering utility threshold. Always report absolute raw-ohm
errors and descriptive 5%/20% sensitivity; those thresholds cannot change the
registered classification.

The result is **internally supportive for material contrast-invariant
longitudinal identity** only if all hold:

- (G^*\ge0.10) and (p_{link}\le0.05);
- the fixed-W 95% conditional-stability lower bound is above zero;
- every deletion gives W positive gain and at least 9/11 gains are at least
  0.10;
- no SOC-row W gain is at or below -0.10;
- both spline sensitivities, extended alpha grid, equal-group weighting, and
  basis-rotation audit retain W gain at least 0.10 without branch reversal.

The warranted claim is only that correctly linked BoL relative nonlinear
cross-SOC real-impedance shape contains held-specimen information about the
corresponding ordinal-MoL projected shape beyond documented protocol in these
cells.

A stronger **scalar transport beyond unit persistence** label requires A to be
W, primary support, (G_{AU}\ge0.10), A to beat U in at least 9/11 outer
losses and every deletion aggregate, and the refit stability interval for
(gamma) to exclude both 0 and 1. Call attenuation only if that interval and
every deletion estimate lie strictly in (0,1); amplification only if all
exceed 1; sign reversal only if all are below 0. These remain nonmechanistic
internal descriptions.

The result is **adverse for margin-qualified invariant identity** only if
(G^*<0.10), the fixed-W stability upper bound is below 0.10,
(p_{link}>0.05), neither identity model has a stable SOC-row gain of at least
0.10, and no registered sensitivity is supportive. Conclude only that this
archive and model family do not identify a 10%-margin fingerprint.

All other valid patterns are **inconclusive**, including margin-spanning
stability, tail-fraction/stability disagreement, deletion dependence,
opposing SOC rows, basis or spline sensitivity, unstable (gamma), apparent
full-map gain without scalar support, or signal only in discarded components.
Preserve adverse and inconclusive results.

## Alternative selection record

P is the simple baseline. U and A are matched substantive alternatives on the
same outcome; A is selected because one within-protocol scalar is estimable
and asks whether the preserved geometry is attenuated rather than exactly
unit-valued.

A two-coefficient linear-SOC/curvature-SOC transport was made equally
specific and evaluated in the bounded audit. Inputs were the same 66 tables
and fixed five spline modes; targets were the same absolute MoL quotient;
splits were the same 11 cells; uncertainty would require the same 432 max
calibration. It could reveal different persistence of first-order SOC
dependence and SOC curvature, which A averages. It was deferred because it
adds a heterogeneity claim with only six within-protocol specimen contrasts
per outer fold and its simple held-cell gain (-0.295 versus P) was worse than
the global scalar's (-0.192). Revisit with an independent larger cohort or an
inconclusive registered result showing opposite component behavior.

Ten diagonal gains, the six-parameter SOC-by-shape surface, and the full map
are deferred because their coordinate heterogeneity or rotation is not
identified by this cohort. Equivalent-circuit, DRT, and frequency-localized
models remain unavailable because row-level frequency and imaginary-channel
semantics are absent. Neural or kernel models provide no separately
adjudicable information at (n=11).

## Solver deliverable, compute, and verification

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted, basis-invariant P/U/A evidence:
all nested fits; all 432 relinkings in each confirmatory domain; 10,000
conditional loss resamples and scalar refits; 11 deletion refits; registered
sensitivities; nuisance localization; and a deterministic conclusion trace.
Readiness or conversion alone is not completion.

Required outputs are `source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`,
`duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`, `basis_audit.json`,
`representation_blocks.parquet`, `energy_audit.csv`,
`metric_invariance_audit.json`, `outer_predictions.parquet`,
`outer_losses.csv`, `scalar_transport_fits.csv`,
`training_weight_audit.parquet`, `tuning_log.parquet`,
`linkage_allocations.parquet`, `conditional_stability.parquet`,
`scalar_bootstrap.parquet`, `deletion_metrics.csv`,
`sensitivity_metrics.csv`, `full_map_diagnostic.json`,
`localization_metrics.json`, `metrics.json`, and `conclusion.json` with
sentence-to-field provenance.

Use 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS, and allocation-level
parallelism. Native conversion measured 18.46 s in this episode; bounded
diagnostics took under 2 s each. The full run remains estimated at 30-90
minutes and fits the configured 9,000 science-second discovery limit and
28,800-second future solver envelope. Checkpoint every 25 allocations.

The verifier can check hashes, expected-table selection, duplicate equality,
joins, quotient reconstruction/invariances, specimen splits, fit-local
physical-grid weights, within-group scalar fitting, ridge predictions, all
432 allocations, resamples, deletions, sensitivities, and deterministic
outcome wording. It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outputs
when warranted and reject correct numbers paired with unsupported frequency,
mechanism, fixture, causal, population, or deployment claims.

Scientific adjudication remains necessary for within-group exchangeability,
the importance of the 10% margin, SOC accuracy/equilibration, MoL
comparability, and whether retained components are artifacts or
electrochemistry. Stronger conclusions require authoritative frequency and
complex-impedance semantics, repeated EIS with fixture/contact controls and
acquisition order, timestamp/throughput/cycle/capacity records defining a

held-out cohort with several cells per protocol.

## Inspected provenance

The Oxford source README, configured dataset guide/metadata/catalog binding,
archive member inventory, all 66 selected native containers, parent proposal,
and all three parent support files were inspected on 2026-09-23. Fresh export

# Task: frozen Zhang2020 longitudinal landmark experiment

Implement and execute the scientific experiment below. This is an open-ended readiness-mode research task: no result is supplied and no favorable outcome is expected. Your submission must newly fit every declared model, compute held-cell predictions and uncertainty, preserve adverse results, and emit the machine-readable outputs defined after the frozen design. Do not change the population, landmarks, outcomes, estimands, analyses, or decision criteria.

# Zhang2020 anchored longitudinal landmark experiment: are late gains calibration, accumulated change, or a current capacity proxy?

## Scientific decision, challenge to the parents, and falsifiable hypothesis

The selected parent correctly treats

`D[i,c] = IX_start[i,c] - V_end[i,c]`

as an observed protocol-transition interval. The configured rows do not continuously record current, voltage, control actions, rest, charge passed, or SOC inside that interval. This proposal never calls D a discharge duration and never assigns D or an impedance contrast a degradation mechanism.

The remaining inferential flaw is that the parent's held-cell predictor `Dhat(B)` cannot learn an unknown, time-stable offset for the held cell. Such an offset is necessarily placed in `eD=D-Dhat(B)`; consequently, a gain from eD need not be within-cell transition-clock change. The leader's stale and cycle-1-centered checks are useful sensitivities, but they do not put stable calibration, previously accumulated longitudinal change, and the newly observed current update into the primary matched estimand.

The unresolved hypothesis is therefore:

> After a five-cycle, outcome-free calibration block and all measurements through cycle c-1 are made explicit, the newly observed within-cell update in the V-to-IX clock at IX start and/or the newly observed within-cell update in the IX-minus-V spectrum at IX end improves held-cell prediction of both H10 and H20 future measured-capacity loss, including the post-c remainder, by at least 5% beyond a strong end-V model. The increment must not be explainable solely by fixed early-cell calibration, already-observed longitudinal evolution, or near-current measured capacity.

This matters scientifically because raw clock or IX gains can support three different conclusions with different acquisition implications: a one-time calibration signature, a slowly evolving history already known before the current IX acquisition, or genuinely new same-cycle information. The experiment can distinguish those predictive explanations. It cannot identify what physical operation generated D, prove causality, or infer a microscopic degradation mechanism.

**Strongest evidence already supported.** The parent audits establish 2,786 complete same-token, same-cycle I/V/IX triples on one exact 60-frequency grid, universal I-before-V-before-IX ordering, 2,054 H10 and 1,974 H20 origins in ten conservatively linked cells, and a 0.000995–0.002005 s gap from IX end to the next capacity-cycle charge record. They also establish a descriptive pooled correlation of 0.9399 between D and Q[c]. The inspected full-text Zhang article (DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`; PMCID `PMC7136228`; source ID `33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79`; SHA-256 `ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144`) supports the 12-cell, nine-state, >20,000-spectrum setting and the paper's EIS capacity/RUL models. It also says states V and IX were electrochemically stable measurement states, but that does not supply interval-resolved semantics for D. No complete supplement inspection is claimed here.

A new read-only audit, `zhang_anchor_audit.py` (SHA-256 `8dcec6cfd3fbe23dc4380a8c38128e89d6573a9dede5a49b7347baaddbefaedc`) with output `zhang_anchor_audit.json` (SHA-256 `8fde9f9e0f6bff2ddcb06a7283a14adbb04457069bb0744fe9e9e078b5262a21`), shows that all ten retained cells have complete, contiguous V/IX spectra from cycle 1 through their last complete cycle. Thus cycles 1–5 and cycle c-1 exist for every frozen c>=10 origin and add no exclusions. Across cells, the SD of the five-cycle median D anchor is 165.26 s; median within-cell post-anchor D SD is 105.81 s. The pooled descriptive correlation is 0.93986 for D versus Q[c], but 0.26404 for first differences of D versus Q[c]. The median L2 norm of post-anchor change in the 120-component IX-minus-V vector is 0.2680 ohm. These repeated-cycle summaries establish feasibility and nonzero variation only. They are not held-cell prognostic evidence, do not make cycles independent, and do not identify stable physical calibration or a mechanism.

The substantive advance is an exact, observation-based decomposition rather than a cross-cell fitted residual. For z equal to scalar D or the 120-component `X=dIX=IX-V` vector, define:

- `S_z[i] = componentwise median(z[i,1],...,z[i,5])`, the fixed early calibration anchor;
- `P_z[i,c] = z[i,c-1] - S_z[i]`, accumulated change already observed before origin c;
- `U_z[i,c] = z[i,c] - z[i,c-1]`, the current within-cell update.

Then `z[i,c] = S_z[i] + P_z[i,c] + U_z[i,c]` exactly. “Anchor,” “accumulated change,” and “current update” describe recorded quantities, not latent physical states.

## Population, temporal boundaries, and outcomes

The confirmatory physical-cell keys remain exactly:
`25C01, 25C04, 25C05, 25C06, 25C07, 25C08, 35C01, 35C02, 45C01, 45C02`.

EIS tokens `25C02` and `25C03` remain excluded before tuning or outcome inspection because capacity filenames conflict with acquisition-clock continuity. Clock-resolved cross-map and literal-filename 12-token populations remain separate sensitivities and cannot overturn confirmation. A row, frequency, spectrum, cycle, origin, or window is not an independent specimen.

For every origin c retain the exact chronology:
`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

All anchors use cycles 1–5 and all prior blocks use cycle c-1, so they precede the current landmarks:

1. **LV, end V(c):** Q through c-1, I(c), V(c), S_D, P_D, S_X, and P_X are available. Freeze every LV forecast.
2. **LD, IX(c) start:** D(c), hence U_D(c), first becomes available. No IX(c) impedance value is available.
3. **LX, IX(c) end:** X(c), hence U_X(c), becomes available.

`L[i,c,H] = Q[i,c-1] - Q[i,c+H-1]`, H in {10,20}.

## Frozen predictors and primary chronological decomposition

The unchanged base history B contains c, log(1+c), fixed numeric and one-hot temperature family, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, ten Q[c-10:c-1]/Q0 values, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle OLS slopes, their difference, ten-cycle quadratic coefficient and residual SD, and predeclared temperature-by-age/level/slope interactions. No post-V value enters B.

Let `dI(c)=V(c)-I(c)` and `X(c)=dIX(c)=IX(c)-V(c)`, each with Re and stored -Im at all 60 frequencies. Do not form ratios. Let:

- **P:** OLS extrapolation from Q[c-10:c-1], predicting `-H*slope10` without clipping.
- **B:** standardized ridge on history only.
- **V:** B plus the 120 current V components.
- **EV:** V plus the 120 current dI components, frozen at LV.
- **A0:** EV plus stable anchors S_D and S_X, frozen at LV.
- **A1:** A0 plus prior accumulated changes P_D and P_X, frozen at LV.
- **AD:** A1 plus current clock update U_D, frozen at LD.
- **AX:** AD plus current spectral update U_X, frozen at LX.

The primary chronological estimands for Y in {L,R} are family-balanced held-cell MAE reductions:

- `Delta_I,L = [E(V,L)-E(EV,L)]/E(V,L)`, preserving the parent's I-information test;
- `Delta_stable,Y = [E(EV,Y)-E(A0,Y)]/E(EV,Y)`;
- `Delta_prior,Y = [E(A0,Y)-E(A1,Y)]/E(A0,Y)`;
- `Delta_Dnew,Y = [E(A1,Y)-E(AD,Y)]/E(A1,Y)`;
- `Delta_Xnew,Y = [E(AD,Y)-E(AX,Y)]/E(AD,Y)`;
- `Delta_current,L = [E(A1,L)-E(AX,L)]/E(A1,L)`, the fair stop/continue contrast after using all prior diagnostics;
- `Delta_continue,L = [E(EV,L)-E(AX,L)]/E(EV,L)`, preserving the parent's total post-V information contrast.

Report absolute MAE changes as well. Percentage increments are not additive and the order is deliberately chronological, not causal.

To identify modality rather than only the joint ladder, fit two matched side ladders on identical rows and folds:

- clock: `EV -> EV+S_D -> +P_D -> +U_D`;
- spectrum: `EV -> EV+S_X -> +P_X -> +U_X`.

Also fit `EV+D(c)`, `EV+X(c)`, and `EV+D(c)+X(c)`. Because S+P+U equals the current raw quantity exactly, a directional reversal between raw and decomposed parameterizations makes the affected attribution inconclusive; ridge shrinkage can prevent numerical equality. Save maximum reconstruction errors, required <=1e-9 s for D and <=1e-12 ohm for X.

S_D and S_X are held-cell measurements known from cycles 1–5, not predictors learned from held-cell outcomes. They change the deployment question from zero-measurement transfer to prognosis after five early diagnostic cycles, which is already compatible with the ten-cycle capacity-history requirement. They must never be described as cell identity or immutable hardware calibration; an observed early anchor can include early state and measurement effects.

## Simple baseline and substantive learned alternative

**Primary auditable model.** For every rung, standardize continuous variables using outer-training cells only and fit ridge regression with alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}; tune cubic age-spline df in {3,5,7}. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection minimizes family-balanced cell MAE. Refit every rung rather than applying post-hoc residual correction. The scalar D blocks enter directly; each spectral block remains ordered by the frozen grid.

**Sparse companion.** Repeat V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X using Re and stored -Im at exactly 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz. This tests information compression, not acquisition-time savings, because no timed sparse protocol is present.

**Substantive learned alternative.** Within every training fold, fit PCA separately to V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X, retaining the smallest number reaching 99% training variance capped by tuned {10,20}. Concatenate available PCA scores, B, and scalar clock blocks; fit an RBF Nystroem map plus ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks in {128,256} capped by training rows, and the same ridge-alpha grid; fixed seed 20260923. This can reveal nonlinear interactions between capacity history, early spectral geometry, accumulated trajectory, current clock update, and current IX update that additive ridge loses. A learned-only result is model-dependent and cannot satisfy primary support.

The simple model is selected because the scientific contrast is blockwise and chronological, and coefficients/ablations are auditable. The learned model is retained at equal population, inputs, targets, folds, and metrics because nonlinear geometry could otherwise make an apparent absence of current change a linear-model artifact. A neural sequence encoder is deferred because ten independent specimens cannot support its flexibility. Equivalent circuits are deferred because topology and parameter identifiability are not established and fitted circuit values would not be microscopic ground truth.

## Proxy adjudication, controls, and negative results

Fit every primary rung to N and R. A gain concentrated in N is compatible with immediate-capacity proxying; only a gain on R addresses post-c prognosis.

Run the explicitly non-deployable oracle ladder for R:
`O1=A1+Q[c]`, `OD=O1+U_D`, and `OX=OD+U_X`.
Q[c] is observed after LX. Persistence of an update beyond Q[c] is evidence of conditional predictive information under the fitted model, not causal mediation; disappearance is compatible with a near-current-capacity proxy.

Mandatory controls, all on identical origins and specimen folds, are:

1. replace median cycles 1–5 anchors by cycle-1 values and by medians cycles 1–3;
2. replace U_D and U_X by zero, by their one-cycle lags, and by five-cycle slopes available at LV;
3. add absolute experiment time, I/V/IX sweep durations, I-to-V gap, and IX sweep duration only at landmarks where observed;
4. remove each spectrum's highest-frequency complex translation, use highest-frequency-only, and compare direct I/V/IX coordinates with difference coordinates;
5. permute whole S, P, or U trajectories among cells within temperature family on common-support windows; never permute origins independently;
6. hash spectra and reject any train/test cell pair with an exact duplicate;
7. repeat with L/Q0, ox/red=1, common support c=10–25 for H10 (160 origins) and c=10–15 for H20 (60 origins), family holdout, age-forward cutoffs tau={50,100,150}, and both disputed 12-token identity maps;
8. report eligibility and baseline-covariate distributions for censored versus observed tail origins; never impute missing targets.

## Splits, uncertainty, and decision rules

Primary evaluation is ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. Every cycle and acquisition from a physical key remains together. The held cell may contribute only prediction-time measurements available by the stated landmark, including its cycles 1–5 anchors and measurements through c-1; it contributes no outcomes, preprocessing statistics, PCA, Nystroem landmarks, hyperparameters, feature selection, interval calibration, or residual fitting. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection uses family-balanced cell MAE. Random row, frequency, spectrum, cycle, or origin splits are prohibited.

For every training fit, assign origin i,c weight 1/(F*n_f*n_i), where F is the number of represented families, n_f the number of training cells in that origin's family, and n_i the eligible training origins for that cell; renormalize weights to sum to the training-row count. Use these weights in ridge loss, spline tuning, and the learned model. Compute PCA from the correspondingly weighted covariance, and sample Nystroem landmarks with the same fixed-seed weights. This prevents long records and the six-cell 25 C family from dominating while retaining all rows.\n\nAggregate origins within cell, cells equally within family, and the three temperature families equally. Report each origin, cell, family, horizon, and age third. For every model/outcome report MAE in mAh (primary), RMSE, signed bias, R2 when defined, MAE/Q0, and nominal 90% interval coverage, width, and interval score.

Construct intervals only from inner held-cell residuals, reducing each calibration cell to its 90th-percentile absolute residual and taking finite-sample rank `ceil(0.90(m+1))`, clipped to m. Use 10,000 fixed-seed paired bootstraps resampling cells within family and all 2^10 cell-level sign-flip assignments as a sensitivity. Construct one simultaneous 95% max-deviation band over every claim-gating contrast (46 total): the 18 joint-ladder values Delta_I,L, Delta_stable,L, Delta_prior,L, Delta_Dnew,{L,R}, Delta_Xnew,{L,R}, Delta_current,L, and Delta_continue,L at H10/H20; 10 clock-only values for S_D on L, P_D on {L,R}, and U_D on {L,R} at both horizons; the analogous 10 spectrum-only values; four post-Q[c] oracle U_D/U_X increments for R; and four U_D/U_X increments for N on the H10 and H20 risk sets. The ten-cell cohort, especially the two-cell 35C/45C families, makes uncertainty coarse.

All 5% and 10% margins are predeclared relevance thresholds, not literature-derived facts.

- **I informative by end V:** preserve the parent rule: Delta_I,L>=10% at both horizons, simultaneous lower bounds >0, positive improvement in at least two families with none worse than -10%, positive common-support direction, coverage 0.80–1.00, and no stale or representation reversal. Falsify the conjunctive 10% claim if either horizon's upper bound is <10%.
- **Current clock update supported:** Delta_Dnew,L and Delta_Dnew,R are each >=5% at H10 and H20; simultaneous lower bounds exceed 0; the corresponding oracle R increment after adding Q[c] is also >=5% with lower bound >0; at least two families improve and none worsens by >10%; common-support and raw-D directions agree; coverage is 0.80–1.00; and lag, timing, representation, permutation, and learned checks do not reverse the result.
- **Current IX update supported:** the mirror rule for Delta_Xnew,L and Delta_Xnew,R, additionally requiring the oracle R increment after Q[c] to be >=5% with lower bound >0 at both horizons. This supports IX information beyond the complete observed clock and current measured capacity under the specified models.
- **Stable calibration compatible:** in the modality-specific ladder, its S block has >=5% L gain at both horizons with lower bounds >0, while the corresponding P and U blocks have simultaneous upper bounds <5% for L and R. Say only that early measurement anchors carry the useful association; do not call them immutable offsets or intrinsic calibration.
- **Previously accumulated longitudinal change compatible:** the modality-specific P block has >=5% L and R gains at both horizons with lower bounds >0, while the corresponding U block has upper bounds <5%. This means the useful evolution was already observable by c-1, not that no later change exists.
- **Near-current-capacity proxy compatible:** the current U block improves N by >=5% with lower bound >0 on both horizon risk sets, but its R upper bounds are <5% and its oracle R upper bounds after Q[c] are <5%. This is a predictive compatibility statement, not causal mediation or interval semantics.
- **Continuation information-positive:** preserve the parent rule: Delta_continue,L >=10% at both horizons with simultaneous lower bounds >0, at least two families improving, none worsening by >10%, and passing family/common-support/age-forward/coverage gates. This is information value, not an operational recommendation.
- **End V sufficient under the parent's information set:** preserve the parent rule: support only if Delta_continue,L upper bounds are <=5% at both horizons, EV coverage is acceptable, and no family shows >10% late improvement. Falsify if either lower bound exceeds 5%; otherwise unresolved.
- **No value in the current acquisition after prior diagnostics:** support only if Delta_current,L and both current U-block L/R upper bounds are <=5% at both horizons, A1 coverage is acceptable, and no family shows >10% current-acquisition gain. This is distinct from the legacy EV comparison because A1 uses strictly prior D/IX records.
- **Adverse current acquisition:** the relevant U-block upper bounds are <=0 at both horizons and common-support direction does not reverse.

A conjunctive 5% update hypothesis is falsified as posed if either horizon's simultaneous upper bound for L or R is below 5%. Everything else is inconclusive, including horizon disagreement, intervals crossing zero or a margin, family conflict, failed calibration, identity dependence, risk/common-support reversal, raw/decomposed reversal, or simple/learned disagreement. If stable, prior, and current blocks overlap without resolvable conditional increments, report “source of predictive gain unresolved,” not equivalence. Preserve unfavorable results.

## Deliverable, resources, readiness, and verifier boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted LV, LD, and LX held-cell predictions; exact S/P/U decompositions for D and X; modality-specific and joint chronological estimands for L, N, and R; the Q[c] oracle; simultaneous specimen-level uncertainty; all sensitivity branches; and a machine-readable supportive, adverse, or inconclusive attribution. No predictive result is claimed now.

Use Python 3.11 with numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, and joblib; 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and at most 7 hours, within the 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/8-GPU/28,800-s solver envelope. Parallelize outer folds and cap library threads. The anchor audit took 19.5 s in a bounded shell; full nested fitting time is an unmeasured estimate. GPU use adds no scientific value for ten specimens and these regular tabular/spectral models.

Required outputs:

- immutable source/catalog/software/seed manifests and all 48 member/table bindings;
- parser, field-width, header, unit, sign, integer-cycle, grid-hash, identity, and exclusion tests;
- capacity and I/V/IX clock ledgers, with D named `transition_interval_s`;
- proof that cycles 1–5 and c-1 are complete for every frozen origin and that 25C02/03 never enter confirmation;

- cell/family/aggregate metrics, bootstrap/sign-flip draws, simultaneous bands, adverse results, executable code/checkpoints, and `conclusion.json` mapping every claim to exact output fields.

Readiness must reproduce source hashes, table/member existence, field layouts, 60-bin grid, 2,786 triples, 2,054/1,974 risks, chronology, anchor/lag completeness, reconstruction identities, imports, physical-cell split isolation, and a two-cell end-to-end fit. Readiness is not a solved objective.

An automatic verifier can recompute all parsing, joins, timestamps, Q extraction, eligibility, feature availability, S/P/U algebra, splits, transformations, predictions, metrics, uncertainty, thresholds, and conclusion mapping. It must accept correctly computed supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outcomes. Adversarial cases must reject: calling D discharge duration; allowing Q[c] into a deployable rung; fitting transforms or tuning on a held cell; calling S immutable calibration or U a physical innovation; claiming current IX support from a point estimate whose interval crosses a margin; and attaching mechanistic or causal language to correct calculations. It must accept a cautious negative or unresolved attribution.

Automatic verification cannot establish physical identity of 25C02/03, validate unresolved headerless semantics, determine operations within D, judge practical margin or acquisition burden, diagnose informative stopping, or infer microscopic degradation. Those require data-owner/expert adjudication, protocol logs, direct current/voltage records, independent compatible specimens, controlled interventions, or another study.

## Selection and alternatives record

This child keeps the parent's ten-cell population, temporal landmarks, H10/H20 outcomes, risk sets, baseline information, and uncertainty. It replaces model-relative cross-cell residual attribution with an exact measurement decomposition whose components have explicit availability times. The parent remains valuable for asking how much D is predictable without any held-cell transition history; this child answers the complementary and sharper question of what a five-cycle-calibrated held cell gains from a current D or IX acquisition.

The primary ridge ladder is selected for auditable chronological attribution. The matched PCA-Nystroem ladder tests nonlinear spectrum/trajectory interactions at the same specificity. The parent's Dhat/eD model remains a sensitivity: agreement strengthens robustness, while disagreement demonstrates dependence on whether held-cell calibration is allowed and must be reported as inconclusive. Revisit neural sequence models only with materially more independent cells; revisit equivalent circuits only with a validated topology and identifiability criterion; revisit pure interval semantics only with interval-resolved protocol evidence; and revisit operational policy only with measured time, energy, interruption, safety, and utility data.

Population, temporal boundaries, outcomes, estimands, analysis, and falsification criteria are frozen for compilation. Any change requires a Lead-approved scientific child.

# Zhang2020 anchored longitudinal landmark experiment: are late gains calibration, accumulated change, or a current capacity proxy?

## Scientific decision, challenge to the parents, and falsifiable hypothesis

The selected parent correctly treats

`D[i,c] = IX_start[i,c] - V_end[i,c]`

as an observed protocol-transition interval. The configured rows do not continuously record current, voltage, control actions, rest, charge passed, or SOC inside that interval. This proposal never calls D a discharge duration and never assigns D or an impedance contrast a degradation mechanism.

The remaining inferential flaw is that the parent's held-cell predictor `Dhat(B)` cannot learn an unknown, time-stable offset for the held cell. Such an offset is necessarily placed in `eD=D-Dhat(B)`; consequently, a gain from eD need not be within-cell transition-clock change. The leader's stale and cycle-1-centered checks are useful sensitivities, but they do not put stable calibration, previously accumulated longitudinal change, and the newly observed current update into the primary matched estimand.

The unresolved hypothesis is therefore:

> After a five-cycle, outcome-free calibration block and all measurements through cycle c-1 are made explicit, the newly observed within-cell update in the V-to-IX clock at IX start and/or the newly observed within-cell update in the IX-minus-V spectrum at IX end improves held-cell prediction of both H10 and H20 future measured-capacity loss, including the post-c remainder, by at least 5% beyond a strong end-V model. The increment must not be explainable solely by fixed early-cell calibration, already-observed longitudinal evolution, or near-current measured capacity.

This matters scientifically because raw clock or IX gains can support three different conclusions with different acquisition implications: a one-time calibration signature, a slowly evolving history already known before the current IX acquisition, or genuinely new same-cycle information. The experiment can distinguish those predictive explanations. It cannot identify what physical operation generated D, prove causality, or infer a microscopic degradation mechanism.

**Strongest evidence already supported.** The parent audits establish 2,786 complete same-token, same-cycle I/V/IX triples on one exact 60-frequency grid, universal I-before-V-before-IX ordering, 2,054 H10 and 1,974 H20 origins in ten conservatively linked cells, and a 0.000995–0.002005 s gap from IX end to the next capacity-cycle charge record. They also establish a descriptive pooled correlation of 0.9399 between D and Q[c]. The inspected full-text Zhang article (DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`; PMCID `PMC7136228`; source ID `33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79`; SHA-256 `ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144`) supports the 12-cell, nine-state, >20,000-spectrum setting and the paper's EIS capacity/RUL models. It also says states V and IX were electrochemically stable measurement states, but that does not supply interval-resolved semantics for D. No complete supplement inspection is claimed here.

A new read-only audit, `zhang_anchor_audit.py` (SHA-256 `8dcec6cfd3fbe23dc4380a8c38128e89d6573a9dede5a49b7347baaddbefaedc`) with output `zhang_anchor_audit.json` (SHA-256 `8fde9f9e0f6bff2ddcb06a7283a14adbb04457069bb0744fe9e9e078b5262a21`), shows that all ten retained cells have complete, contiguous V/IX spectra from cycle 1 through their last complete cycle. Thus cycles 1–5 and cycle c-1 exist for every frozen c>=10 origin and add no exclusions. Across cells, the SD of the five-cycle median D anchor is 165.26 s; median within-cell post-anchor D SD is 105.81 s. The pooled descriptive correlation is 0.93986 for D versus Q[c], but 0.26404 for first differences of D versus Q[c]. The median L2 norm of post-anchor change in the 120-component IX-minus-V vector is 0.2680 ohm. These repeated-cycle summaries establish feasibility and nonzero variation only. They are not held-cell prognostic evidence, do not make cycles independent, and do not identify stable physical calibration or a mechanism.

The substantive advance is an exact, observation-based decomposition rather than a cross-cell fitted residual. For z equal to scalar D or the 120-component `X=dIX=IX-V` vector, define:

- `S_z[i] = componentwise median(z[i,1],...,z[i,5])`, the fixed early calibration anchor;
- `P_z[i,c] = z[i,c-1] - S_z[i]`, accumulated change already observed before origin c;
- `U_z[i,c] = z[i,c] - z[i,c-1]`, the current within-cell update.

Then `z[i,c] = S_z[i] + P_z[i,c] + U_z[i,c]` exactly. “Anchor,” “accumulated change,” and “current update” describe recorded quantities, not latent physical states.

## Frozen predictors and primary chronological decomposition

The unchanged base history B contains c, log(1+c), fixed numeric and one-hot temperature family, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, ten Q[c-10:c-1]/Q0 values, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle OLS slopes, their difference, ten-cycle quadratic coefficient and residual SD, and predeclared temperature-by-age/level/slope interactions. No post-V value enters B.

Let `dI(c)=V(c)-I(c)` and `X(c)=dIX(c)=IX(c)-V(c)`, each with Re and stored -Im at all 60 frequencies. Do not form ratios. Let:

- **P:** OLS extrapolation from Q[c-10:c-1], predicting `-H*slope10` without clipping.
- **B:** standardized ridge on history only.
- **V:** B plus the 120 current V components.
- **EV:** V plus the 120 current dI components, frozen at LV.
- **A0:** EV plus stable anchors S_D and S_X, frozen at LV.
- **A1:** A0 plus prior accumulated changes P_D and P_X, frozen at LV.
- **AD:** A1 plus current clock update U_D, frozen at LD.
- **AX:** AD plus current spectral update U_X, frozen at LX.

The primary chronological estimands for Y in {L,R} are family-balanced held-cell MAE reductions:

- `Delta_I,L = [E(V,L)-E(EV,L)]/E(V,L)`, preserving the parent's I-information test;
- `Delta_stable,Y = [E(EV,Y)-E(A0,Y)]/E(EV,Y)`;
- `Delta_prior,Y = [E(A0,Y)-E(A1,Y)]/E(A0,Y)`;
- `Delta_Dnew,Y = [E(A1,Y)-E(AD,Y)]/E(A1,Y)`;
- `Delta_Xnew,Y = [E(AD,Y)-E(AX,Y)]/E(AD,Y)`;
- `Delta_current,L = [E(A1,L)-E(AX,L)]/E(A1,L)`, the fair stop/continue contrast after using all prior diagnostics;
- `Delta_continue,L = [E(EV,L)-E(AX,L)]/E(EV,L)`, preserving the parent's total post-V information contrast.

Report absolute MAE changes as well. Percentage increments are not additive and the order is deliberately chronological, not causal.

To identify modality rather than only the joint ladder, fit two matched side ladders on identical rows and folds:

- clock: `EV -> EV+S_D -> +P_D -> +U_D`;
- spectrum: `EV -> EV+S_X -> +P_X -> +U_X`.

Also fit `EV+D(c)`, `EV+X(c)`, and `EV+D(c)+X(c)`. Because S+P+U equals the current raw quantity exactly, a directional reversal between raw and decomposed parameterizations makes the affected attribution inconclusive; ridge shrinkage can prevent numerical equality. Save maximum reconstruction errors, required <=1e-9 s for D and <=1e-12 ohm for X.

S_D and S_X are held-cell measurements known from cycles 1–5, not predictors learned from held-cell outcomes. They change the deployment question from zero-measurement transfer to prognosis after five early diagnostic cycles, which is already compatible with the ten-cycle capacity-history requirement. They must never be described as cell identity or immutable hardware calibration; an observed early anchor can include early state and measurement effects.

## Simple baseline and substantive learned alternative

**Primary auditable model.** For every rung, standardize continuous variables using outer-training cells only and fit ridge regression with alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}; tune cubic age-spline df in {3,5,7}. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection minimizes family-balanced cell MAE. Refit every rung rather than applying post-hoc residual correction. The scalar D blocks enter directly; each spectral block remains ordered by the frozen grid.

**Sparse companion.** Repeat V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X using Re and stored -Im at exactly 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz. This tests information compression, not acquisition-time savings, because no timed sparse protocol is present.

**Substantive learned alternative.** Within every training fold, fit PCA separately to V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X, retaining the smallest number reaching 99% training variance capped by tuned {10,20}. Concatenate available PCA scores, B, and scalar clock blocks; fit an RBF Nystroem map plus ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks in {128,256} capped by training rows, and the same ridge-alpha grid; fixed seed 20260923. This can reveal nonlinear interactions between capacity history, early spectral geometry, accumulated trajectory, current clock update, and current IX update that additive ridge loses. A learned-only result is model-dependent and cannot satisfy primary support.

The simple model is selected because the scientific contrast is blockwise and chronological, and coefficients/ablations are auditable. The learned model is retained at equal population, inputs, targets, folds, and metrics because nonlinear geometry could otherwise make an apparent absence of current change a linear-model artifact. A neural sequence encoder is deferred because ten independent specimens cannot support its flexibility. Equivalent circuits are deferred because topology and parameter identifiability are not established and fitted circuit values would not be microscopic ground truth.

## Proxy adjudication, controls, and negative results

Fit every primary rung to N and R. A gain concentrated in N is compatible with immediate-capacity proxying; only a gain on R addresses post-c prognosis.

Run the explicitly non-deployable oracle ladder for R:
`O1=A1+Q[c]`, `OD=O1+U_D`, and `OX=OD+U_X`.
Q[c] is observed after LX. Persistence of an update beyond Q[c] is evidence of conditional predictive information under the fitted model, not causal mediation; disappearance is compatible with a near-current-capacity proxy.

Mandatory controls, all on identical origins and specimen folds, are:

1. replace median cycles 1–5 anchors by cycle-1 values and by medians cycles 1–3;
2. replace U_D and U_X by zero, by their one-cycle lags, and by five-cycle slopes available at LV;
3. add absolute experiment time, I/V/IX sweep durations, I-to-V gap, and IX sweep duration only at landmarks where observed;
4. remove each spectrum's highest-frequency complex translation, use highest-frequency-only, and compare direct I/V/IX coordinates with difference coordinates;
5. permute whole S, P, or U trajectories among cells within temperature family on common-support windows; never permute origins independently;
6. hash spectra and reject any train/test cell pair with an exact duplicate;
7. repeat with L/Q0, ox/red=1, common support c=10–25 for H10 (160 origins) and c=10–15 for H20 (60 origins), family holdout, age-forward cutoffs tau={50,100,150}, and both disputed 12-token identity maps;
8. report eligibility and baseline-covariate distributions for censored versus observed tail origins; never impute missing targets.

## Splits, uncertainty, and decision rules

Primary evaluation is ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. Every cycle and acquisition from a physical key remains together. The held cell may contribute only prediction-time measurements available by the stated landmark, including its cycles 1–5 anchors and measurements through c-1; it contributes no outcomes, preprocessing statistics, PCA, Nystroem landmarks, hyperparameters, feature selection, interval calibration, or residual fitting. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection uses family-balanced cell MAE. Random row, frequency, spectrum, cycle, or origin splits are prohibited.

For every training fit, assign origin i,c weight 1/(F*n_f*n_i), where F is the number of represented families, n_f the number of training cells in that origin's family, and n_i the eligible training origins for that cell; renormalize weights to sum to the training-row count. Use these weights in ridge loss, spline tuning, and the learned model. Compute PCA from the correspondingly weighted covariance, and sample Nystroem landmarks with the same fixed-seed weights. This prevents long records and the six-cell 25 C family from dominating while retaining all rows.\n\nAggregate origins within cell, cells equally within family, and the three temperature families equally. Report each origin, cell, family, horizon, and age third. For every model/outcome report MAE in mAh (primary), RMSE, signed bias, R2 when defined, MAE/Q0, and nominal 90% interval coverage, width, and interval score.

Construct intervals only from inner held-cell residuals, reducing each calibration cell to its 90th-percentile absolute residual and taking finite-sample rank `ceil(0.90(m+1))`, clipped to m. Use 10,000 fixed-seed paired bootstraps resampling cells within family and all 2^10 cell-level sign-flip assignments as a sensitivity. Construct one simultaneous 95% max-deviation band over every claim-gating contrast (46 total): the 18 joint-ladder values Delta_I,L, Delta_stable,L, Delta_prior,L, Delta_Dnew,{L,R}, Delta_Xnew,{L,R}, Delta_current,L, and Delta_continue,L at H10/H20; 10 clock-only values for S_D on L, P_D on {L,R}, and U_D on {L,R} at both horizons; the analogous 10 spectrum-only values; four post-Q[c] oracle U_D/U_X increments for R; and four U_D/U_X increments for N on the H10 and H20 risk sets. The ten-cell cohort, especially the two-cell 35C/45C families, makes uncertainty coarse.

All 5% and 10% margins are predeclared relevance thresholds, not literature-derived facts.

- **I informative by end V:** preserve the parent rule: Delta_I,L>=10% at both horizons, simultaneous lower bounds >0, positive improvement in at least two families with none worse than -10%, positive common-support direction, coverage 0.80–1.00, and no stale or representation reversal. Falsify the conjunctive 10% claim if either horizon's upper bound is <10%.
- **Current clock update supported:** Delta_Dnew,L and Delta_Dnew,R are each >=5% at H10 and H20; simultaneous lower bounds exceed 0; the corresponding oracle R increment after adding Q[c] is also >=5% with lower bound >0; at least two families improve and none worsens by >10%; common-support and raw-D directions agree; coverage is 0.80–1.00; and lag, timing, representation, permutation, and learned checks do not reverse the result.
- **Current IX update supported:** the mirror rule for Delta_Xnew,L and Delta_Xnew,R, additionally requiring the oracle R increment after Q[c] to be >=5% with lower bound >0 at both horizons. This supports IX information beyond the complete observed clock and current measured capacity under the specified models.
- **Stable calibration compatible:** in the modality-specific ladder, its S block has >=5% L gain at both horizons with lower bounds >0, while the corresponding P and U blocks have simultaneous upper bounds <5% for L and R. Say only that early measurement anchors carry the useful association; do not call them immutable offsets or intrinsic calibration.
- **Previously accumulated longitudinal change compatible:** the modality-specific P block has >=5% L and R gains at both horizons with lower bounds >0, while the corresponding U block has upper bounds <5%. This means the useful evolution was already observable by c-1, not that no later change exists.
- **Near-current-capacity proxy compatible:** the current U block improves N by >=5% with lower bound >0 on both horizon risk sets, but its R upper bounds are <5% and its oracle R upper bounds after Q[c] are <5%. This is a predictive compatibility statement, not causal mediation or interval semantics.
- **Continuation information-positive:** preserve the parent rule: Delta_continue,L >=10% at both horizons with simultaneous lower bounds >0, at least two families improving, none worsening by >10%, and passing family/common-support/age-forward/coverage gates. This is information value, not an operational recommendation.
- **End V sufficient under the parent's information set:** preserve the parent rule: support only if Delta_continue,L upper bounds are <=5% at both horizons, EV coverage is acceptable, and no family shows >10% late improvement. Falsify if either lower bound exceeds 5%; otherwise unresolved.
- **No value in the current acquisition after prior diagnostics:** support only if Delta_current,L and both current U-block L/R upper bounds are <=5% at both horizons, A1 coverage is acceptable, and no family shows >10% current-acquisition gain. This is distinct from the legacy EV comparison because A1 uses strictly prior D/IX records.
- **Adverse current acquisition:** the relevant U-block upper bounds are <=0 at both horizons and common-support direction does not reverse.

A conjunctive 5% update hypothesis is falsified as posed if either horizon's simultaneous upper bound for L or R is below 5%. Everything else is inconclusive, including horizon disagreement, intervals crossing zero or a margin, family conflict, failed calibration, identity dependence, risk/common-support reversal, raw/decomposed reversal, or simple/learned disagreement. If stable, prior, and current blocks overlap without resolvable conditional increments, report “source of predictive gain unresolved,” not equivalence. Preserve unfavorable results.

## Deliverable, resources, readiness, and verifier boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted LV, LD, and LX held-cell predictions; exact S/P/U decompositions for D and X; modality-specific and joint chronological estimands for L, N, and R; the Q[c] oracle; simultaneous specimen-level uncertainty; all sensitivity branches; and a machine-readable supportive, adverse, or inconclusive attribution. No predictive result is claimed now.

Use Python 3.11 with numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, and joblib; 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and at most 7 hours, within the 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/8-GPU/28,800-s solver envelope. Parallelize outer folds and cap library threads. The anchor audit took 19.5 s in a bounded shell; full nested fitting time is an unmeasured estimate. GPU use adds no scientific value for ten specimens and these regular tabular/spectral models.

Required outputs:

- immutable source/catalog/software/seed manifests and all 48 member/table bindings;
- parser, field-width, header, unit, sign, integer-cycle, grid-hash, identity, and exclusion tests;
- capacity and I/V/IX clock ledgers, with D named `transition_interval_s`;
- proof that cycles 1–5 and c-1 are complete for every frozen origin and that 25C02/03 never enter confirmation;
- H10/H20 analytic tables containing exact Q indices, target endpoints, censoring, landmark masks, S/P/U provenance, and reconstruction checks;
- outer/inner split, preprocessing, tuning, PCA, Nystroem, calibration, thread, and seed manifests;
- every held-cell prediction for P, B, V, EV, joint and modality ladders, raw, sparse, learned, N/R, oracle, lag, timing, representation, permutation, common-support, family, age, polarity, normalization, censoring, and identity branches;
- cell/family/aggregate metrics, bootstrap/sign-flip draws, simultaneous bands, adverse results, executable code/checkpoints, and `conclusion.json` mapping every claim to exact output fields.

Readiness must reproduce source hashes, table/member existence, field layouts, 60-bin grid, 2,786 triples, 2,054/1,974 risks, chronology, anchor/lag completeness, reconstruction identities, imports, physical-cell split isolation, and a two-cell end-to-end fit. Readiness is not a solved objective.

An automatic verifier can recompute all parsing, joins, timestamps, Q extraction, eligibility, feature availability, S/P/U algebra, splits, transformations, predictions, metrics, uncertainty, thresholds, and conclusion mapping. It must accept correctly computed supportive, adverse, or inconclusive outcomes. Adversarial cases must reject: calling D discharge duration; allowing Q[c] into a deployable rung; fitting transforms or tuning on a held cell; calling S immutable calibration or U a physical innovation; claiming current IX support from a point estimate whose interval crosses a margin; and attaching mechanistic or causal language to correct calculations. It must accept a cautious negative or unresolved attribution.

Automatic verification cannot establish physical identity of 25C02/03, validate unresolved headerless semantics, determine operations within D, judge practical margin or acquisition burden, diagnose informative stopping, or infer microscopic degradation. Those require data-owner/expert adjudication, protocol logs, direct current/voltage records, independent compatible specimens, controlled interventions, or another study.

## Selection and alternatives record

This child keeps the parent's ten-cell population, temporal landmarks, H10/H20 outcomes, risk sets, baseline information, and uncertainty. It replaces model-relative cross-cell residual attribution with an exact measurement decomposition whose components have explicit availability times. The parent remains valuable for asking how much D is predictable without any held-cell transition history; this child answers the complementary and sharper question of what a five-cycle-calibrated held cell gains from a current D or IX acquisition.

The primary ridge ladder is selected for auditable chronological attribution. The matched PCA-Nystroem ladder tests nonlinear spectrum/trajectory interactions at the same specificity. The parent's Dhat/eD model remains a sensitivity: agreement strengthens robustness, while disagreement demonstrates dependence on whether held-cell calibration is allowed and must be reported as inconclusive. Revisit neural sequence models only with materially more independent cells; revisit equivalent circuits only with a validated topology and identifiability criterion; revisit pure interval semantics only with interval-resolved protocol evidence; and revisit operational policy only with measured time, energy, interruption, safety, and utility data.

Population, temporal boundaries, outcomes, estimands, analysis, and falsification criteria are frozen for compilation. Any change requires a Lead-approved scientific child.

Required columns are `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, `Current (mA)`, `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`. Representative table: table-48e85d15b6c70efa.

A specimen is exact `experiment directory|cell letter`; letters alone are not unique. Parse integer RPT and join one-to-one on experiment, cell, RPT. Parse `RPT start date` day-first. Require unique increasing dates and consecutive RPT indices. Retain finite curve rows with -550 <= current <= -450 mA, preserve negative sign, and set q=Charge-Charge_first. Abort on hash, member, schema, key, chronology, sign, or uniqueness failure. Charge is a phase-local coulomb counter, not independent SOC truth. E1–E5 are opaque fixed strata, not mechanism labels or independent cohorts.

## Population, clocks, and outcomes

At RPT t>=1:

- capacity Y=(C[t+2]-C[t])/C[0], using measured `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`;
- resistance Y=log(R[t+2]/R[t]), using finite positive scheduled `Mean_R (Ohms)`.

Exact counts are capacity E1=71, E2=36, E3=56, E4=32, E5=80 (275), and resistance E1=30, E2=13, E3=23, E4=8, E5=33 (107). All 40 specimens contribute. Do not impute endpoints.

For each outer row at index date d, train only on other same-family specimens whose t+2 target date is strictly earlier than d, with at least 12 rows and four specimens. Exclude same-day targets. Exclude the complete held specimen from fitting, preprocessing, registration templates, components, and tuning. Inner folds repeat these boundaries. With fewer than two validation specimens or eight validation rows, use one component and the frozen default penalty.

Every predictor must exist by the end of RPT t. Never use t+1/t+2 curves, endpoints, dates, exposure, temperatures, duration, or achieved future dose. A sibling increment is eligible only when both curves exist and its endpoint date is strictly before the row index date.

## Frozen representations

Let C0 be RPT0 capacity, q_end active span, and L=q_end/C0. Span, median current, median temperature, start/end voltage, and span-summary discrepancy are scalar controls, not phase.

Smooth voltage for landmark extraction only with a centered 101-sample moving average. Use first downward crossings with linear interpolation:

- primary: [4.05,3.90,3.75,3.60,3.45,3.30,3.15,3.00,2.80] V
- shifted: [4.00,3.85,3.70,3.55,3.40,3.25,3.10,2.95,2.75] V
- sparse: [4.00,3.75,3.50,3.25,3.00] V

Phase is ordered p=q(V)/q_end, fitted through an ILR transform of positive interval proportions learned on training data only. Append endpoints and build the unique monotone piecewise-linear warp to equally spaced canonical knots. Evaluate at 193 canonical points, remove structural fixed-voltage knots and the training-fitted affine voltage component, and condition amplitude corrections on scalar controls.

Repeat endpoint models for all three grids and smoothing windows 1/101/501. Retain U2, the 97-coordinate own-span representation at s=0.02,...,0.98. Report q/C0=0.02,...,0.44 as descriptive only.

Forecast current phase/amplitude without the current curve from the held specimen's t-1 representation plus family-specific earlier-resolved sibling increments. Ridge predicts phase-ILR increments. Training-only FPCA (1–6 components) plus ridge predicts amplitude increments from stage, log exposure through increment endpoint, backward exposure increments, nominal/measured temperature, median current, and prior scores. Innovations are observed minus forecast representations.

## Matched models

Use identical rows, folds, weights, and target scales:

- P0 persistence/fallback.
- B0 linear ridge with scalar chronology, endpoint history, exposure, acquisition, span, and missingness.
- C0 cubic-spline ridge on exactly B0 variables, tuning 3–5 knots and penalty.
- H = C0 plus no-new-current forecast phase/amplitude.
- P1/A1/PA1 = H plus structured phase, amplitude, or both.
- P2/A2/PA2 = H plus independently residualized, training-only FPCA phase/amplitude channels and rank-bounded PLS.
- U2 = own-span fresh-innovation comparator.

Structured amplitude summaries are signed area, absolute area, RMS, and derivative extrema per interval. Run dimension/tuning-matched sibling-swap, held-specimen-lag, within-specimen time-permutation, and target-trajectory-shuffle controls. Report temperature-matched sibling donors where available.

P2/A2/PA2 preserve distributed deformation; P1/A1/PA1 are lower-variance checks. Learned-only improvement or disagreement makes attribution inconclusive. Neural sequence, elastic/SRVF, and electrode-mechanistic models were deferred and must not replace this design.

## Metrics and uncertainty

Compute absolute error by mean over rows within specimen, specimens within family, then equal mean over E1–E5. Report family-balanced MAE, RMSE, reconstructed absolute-state error, training sizes, family/specimen effects, and capacity on resistance-complete rows.

For H/P2/A2/PA2 MAEs:
`gain=1-MAE_PA2/MAE_H`
`phi_phase=0.5*((MAE_H-MAE_P2)+(MAE_A2-MAE_PA2))`
`phi_amplitude=0.5*((MAE_H-MAE_A2)+(MAE_P2-MAE_PA2))`.
Retain negative terms and require phi_phase+phi_amplitude=MAE_H-MAE_PA2.

Use 10,000 paired trajectory bootstraps resampling specimens within fixed family and a family–RPT-stage block bootstrap; interpret the wider interval. Compute simultaneous minima across primary/shifted/sparse/own-span gains and across landmark grids for normalized Shapley terms. Families are fixed. Training-only group-conformal 90% intervals are descriptive; report coverage and width.

## Frozen interpretation

Registration-robust fresh information for an endpoint requires all gates:

1. primary/shifted/sparse PA2 and U2 gains >=0.10 and simultaneous minimum-gain 95% lower >0;
2. >=4/5 family effects positive, none worsens >5%, and every leave-one-specimen-out contrast positive;
3. PA2 beats H, C0, B0, static-RPT0, and every matched negative control;
4. PA1 agrees in sign, stage-centered score positive, and smoothing 1/101/501 preserves support/classification;
5. for resistance, alternative resistance definitions all agree in sign and results are not driven by E4 or E5|A.

After total support, phase is supported when every grid normalized phase point >=0.05 and simultaneous lower >0; amplitude is analogous. Both => `mixed`. Exactly one plus the other channel simultaneous upper <0.05 => `phase_only` or `amplitude_only`; otherwise `robust_unattributed`.

If U2 improves but registered PA2 does not, or signs reverse across registrations/smoothing, use `coordinate_sensitive`. Adverse at the planned effect means simultaneous upper minimum-gain <0.10; <=0 supports no detectable benefit or harm. Use `inconclusive` for intervals crossing 0 or 0.10, structured/learned disagreement, placebo retention, calibration failure, unstable family influence, or resistance-definition conflict. Endpoint conclusions may differ; joint support requires both.

Never interpret phase/amplitude as a degradation mode, LLI, LAM, plating, equilibrium OCV, microscopic cause, causal intervention effect, or external transport.

## Required outputs

Write all declared outputs directly under /workspace, plus `/workspace/model_artifacts/manifest.json`. Parquet names must be real Parquet. Core schemas:

- source_audit.json: hashes, member counts, summary_count=40, discharge_count=511, specimen_count=40, status;
- source_manifest.csv: source_id, member, kind, experiment, cell, rpt;
- forecast_rows.parquet: row_id, endpoint, family, specimen, rpt, index_date, target_date, C0, C_t, C_t2, R_t, R_t2, y_true;
- folds.csv: row_id, endpoint, held_specimen, train_specimen, train_target_date, index_date, inner_fold;
- increment_folds.csv: row_id, held_specimen, donor_specimen, increment_endpoint_date, index_date;
- predictions.parquet: row_id, endpoint, family, specimen, rpt, representation, smoothing, model, y_true, y_pred;
- metrics.json: records with endpoint, representation, smoothing, model, mae, rmse, family_mae;
- shapley_attribution.json: records with endpoint, representation, smoothing, gain, phi_phase, phi_amplitude, normalized_phase, normalized_amplitude;
- uncertainty.parquet: endpoint, statistic, lower, upper, method, replicates;
- influence.csv: endpoint, unit_type, unit, contrast;
- registration_sensitivity.json, negative_controls.json, resistance_sensitivity.json: per-endpoint evidence including gate booleans gain_gate, family_gate, control_gate, stability_gate, resistance_gate;
- verdict.json: endpoint verdicts, joint verdict, exact gate booleans, and claim_scope;
- report.md: cite computed fields and distinguish supported evidence from the hypothesis.

Auxiliary representation files must be nonempty and provenance-linked. Missing fitting, uncertainty, controls, or outputs is incomplete. The verifier independently recomputes outcome arithmetic, chronology exclusions, balanced loss, gains, Shapley identities, uncertainty/verdict logic, and rejects unsupported conclusions.

## Boundary and resources

Automatic checks cannot establish physical uniqueness, microscopic mechanism, equilibrium OCV, causality, or external transport. These require expert review, half-cell/thermodynamic or post-mortem evidence, controlled overlapping protocols, and another independent cohort. Li/Kirkaldy share lineage and are not independent validation.

Budget: 8 CPU cores, 32 GiB RAM, no GPU, 7,200 seconds. Prior ~20-second archive audits establish extraction feasibility only. Readiness checks imports, bindings, representative headers, and a tiny fixture; it is not completion.
