# Does waiting from q30 to a causal 3.60-V stop add future-trajectory information, or only sharpen the current-capacity proxy?

## Scientific question, hypothesis, and advance

The strongest evidence currently supports feasibility, not prognostic value. Li2025 contains 511 measured C/10 discharge curves from 40 specimens in five experiment families; the assigned parents established a causal q30 clock, a causal 3.60-V clock, and usable future-capacity and scheduled-resistance outcomes. Public partial-curve literature supports the broad claim that partial voltage curves can encode contemporaneous health, but does not establish the incremental claim below under held-specimen, forward-resolution-safe testing. No outcome model has been fitted.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among Li2025 origins for which the causal 3.60-V event follows q30, morphology acquired strictly between q30 and 3.60 V contains information about the measured future capacity trajectory at RPT t+1,t+2,t+3 beyond resolved history, all q30 information, added elapsed-time/current/temperature/charge scalars, and either an out-of-specimen reconstruction or the retrospectively observed contemporaneous capacity.

This is an information-acquisition hypothesis, not a causal effect of discharging, and “causal clock” only means computable online from observations up to the stop. Its advance is to localize when trajectory-relevant information is acquired. A favorable q30 model alone cannot show whether later waiting helps; a favorable 3.60-V model alone can be a better proxy for completed capacity. The decisive contrast forces the added segment to predict the zero-sum future slope after actual current state, prior slope, protocol family, RPT stage, and acquisition conditions are supplied.

The primary endpoint is capacity. Scheduled resistance is a secondary endpoint because only a current-to-t+2 change is well supported; it can test incremental future-change information but cannot independently establish multi-horizon shape.

## Population, clocks, and audited support

The population is the same 40 Li/Kirkaldy-lineage specimens and five opaque experiment-family strata, with 511 RPT states dated 2020-06-26 through 2021-07-22. Specimen identity is `experiment directory|cell`; a cell letter alone is invalid. Families are represented schedules, not mechanisms or an external population. RPT rows and horizons within a specimen are repeated observations.

For RPT origin t>=1:

1. q30 is the first linearly interpolated active-discharge point where phase-local q equals 0.30 times that specimen’s already resolved measured RPT0 C/10 capacity C0.
2. V360 is the first sample completing 20 consecutive causal trailing-101-row mean-voltage samples at or below 3.60 V after a trailing mean above 3.60 V. Windows 1 and 501 and thresholds 3.75/3.45 V are sensitivities. The event time includes the confirmation samples. Centered filters are forbidden.
3. Require V360 strictly after q30. Do not swap or redefine clocks when order fails.

A new complete read-only audit found V360 after q30 in 509/511 curves. Expt-1 cell B RPT14 and cell F RPT14 reverse order and are excluded from any segment interpretation. Neither is in a primary forecast set. All 200 nominal common-capacity origins and all 107 nominal resistance origins pass the order gate. For the 200 capacity origins, V360 occurs at q/C0=0.4453–0.6001 (median 0.5501) and 84.8–173.9 minutes after q30 (median 145.9). Family median added times range 137.3–159.0 minutes. For resistance origins, q/C0=0.3614–0.5999 (median 0.5415) and added time is 35.8–173.7 minutes (median 140.9). This strong stage/family dependence motivates mandatory controls; it is not evidence of outcome information.

The inherited forward-resolution gate gives:

- primary capacity: the same 200 origins, all 40 specimens and five families, with all t+1,t+2,t+3 capacities and at least 6 safe earlier training origins from at least four other same-family specimens; mandatory conservative replication has 166 origins with at least 12 safe origins/four specimens;
- secondary resistance: 107 t-to-t+2 origins across all 40 specimens/five families; mandatory conservative replication has 67 origins/32 specimens and omits E4;
- sparse resistance t+4 is descriptive only and cannot establish horizon dependence.

## Measured outcomes and estimands

Capacity scoring uses the measured vector

`Y_C=(C[t+1],C[t+2],C[t+3])/C0`.

Its prespecified summaries are future mean level `L=(Y1+Y2+Y3)/3`, primary trajectory slope `S=(Y3-Y1)/2` per RPT, and secondary curvature `K=Y3-2Y2+Y1`. The primary scientific loss is family-balanced MAE for S; vector-level MAE and L are required companion outcomes. A morphology effect common to all horizons is level information, not trajectory information.

Resistance uses finite positive scheduled `Mean_R (Ohms)`: future level `log(R[t+2]/R0)` and change `S_R=log(R[t+2]/R[t])/2`. Calendar-rate change per 30 days is a sensitivity. Alternative definitions are `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`. Since S_R algebraically includes current R[t], a resistance trajectory claim requires the retrospective actual-state comparison and cannot rest on operational prediction alone.

No endpoint is interpolated or imputed. C/10 capacity and resistance are measured diagnostic summaries. q is coulomb-counted from a phase-local counter and checked by signed-current integration; it is not independent SOC. Reconstructed states and future predictions are fitted quantities, not measurements or degradation mechanisms.

## Exact read-only data binding

Use:

- archive source `[private path]`;
- runtime mount `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`;
- SHA-256 `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`; 835,141,024 bytes and 3,993 members;
- catalog source `[private path]`;
- runtime catalog `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`;
- catalog SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

The catalog records 1,801 Li2025 tables. This experiment reads the 511 discharge and 40 extracted-summary tables only.

Summary members match
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`.
Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-92783194d5d74ccc.json` has 15 rows and columns unnamed first field (RPT), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, and the four resistance fields above.

Discharge members match
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C discharge data.csv`.
Representative table `datasets/Li2025/table-48e85d15b6c70efa.json` binds Expt-1 cell-A RPT0 and contains `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, signed `Current (mA)`, phase-local `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`.

Join one-to-one on independently parsed experiment, cell, and integer RPT. Parse `RPT start date` day-first. Require unique consecutive RPTs and strictly increasing dates. Retain finite active-discharge rows with -550<=current<=-450 mA; subtract first retained time and charge; preserve sign; verify charge against `-integral(I dt)/3600`. Abort on source hash, member, schema, key, chronology, units, sign, monotonicity, required endpoint, or boundary-order failure in an included origin.

## Information firewall and splits

For each scored specimen, exclude that entire specimen from outcome fitting, state reconstruction, expected-segment construction, registration, residualization, scaling, basis/FPCA/PLS estimation, tuning, and calibration.

A capacity training origin j is eligible only when its t+3 target date is strictly earlier than the scored origin’s t date. A resistance training origin requires its t+2 target date strictly earlier. Same-day resolution is excluded. Inner validation repeats held-specimen and latest-target masks.

At q30, operational inputs may use RPT0 values, summary/curve history through t-1, and current rows through q30. At V360 they may additionally use rows after q30 through the confirmed V360 event. Current completed capacity/resistance; achieved future exposure; current `Ageing Cycles`, throughput, degradation days, or age-set end values lacking a within-RPT availability time; complete duration/span/end voltage; post-stop rows; and future records are forbidden. Actual current C[t] and R[t] appear only in labeled retrospective models.

Two firewalls are required: poisoning all post-q30 rows must leave q30 features/predictions bitwise unchanged; poisoning all post-V360 rows and current/future summary values must leave V360 operational features/predictions unchanged. Feature ancestry records every source column and last sample.

## Representations and controls

Every model contains identical training-only standardization, fixed family indicators, nominal temperature, RPT stage and a prespecified cubic stage basis; family-by-stage shrinkage terms are included where support permits. Report early/middle/late stage blocks and within-family effects. A no-family/no-stage sensitivity diagnoses dependence but cannot support transport.

The q30 representation is frozen from the trajectory parent: structured voltage crossings/areas/slopes/derivative extrema and a 61-point q/C0 functional prefix with held-specimen, earlier-date expected-prefix innovations.

The incremental segment has two comparable branches. Every segment feature is calculated strictly from samples after q30 through V360; a voltage crossing that occurred before q30 is masked as already-acquired information.

- **Structured ridge (simple baseline):** added duration; q increment and V360 q/C0; signed-current median, drift and variability; temperature level, drift and excursion; charge-integration discrepancy; post-q30 q/C0 locations and elapsed times at those of 3.90, 3.85, 3.80, 3.75, 3.70, 3.65 and 3.60 V that remain ahead of q30; missing/already-passed indicators; and interval signed/absolute areas, slopes, RMS, and derivative extrema. It is transparent and tests whether a few landmarks suffice.
- **Functional segment (substantive alternative):** a primary fixed physical q/C0 grid from 0.30 to 0.44, which the boundary audit shows is available before V360 for every primary capacity origin, plus a post-0.44 tail represented on causal voltage landmarks down to 3.60 V. Phase/amplitude innovations are relative to the held specimen’s t-1 segment and strictly earlier same-family sibling increments. Residualize against q30 predictors and all added scalars training-only; fit scalar-on-function ridge with cubic B-splines and second-difference penalty or separate 1–4 component training-only FPCA/PLS channels. It can reveal distributed/localized deformation that landmark summaries lose.

Registration controls are mandatory: (a) the primary fixed physical q/C0 grid 0.30–0.44; (b) post-q30 fixed-voltage landmarks with already-passed masking; and (c) normalized segment progress as a sensitivity only. The latter uses the causally observed V360 q span but cannot establish coordinate-robust morphology. Causal windows 1/101/501 and 3.75/3.45-V events are additional sensitivities. A gain confined to one registration is inconclusive.

The neural alternative is deferred because family fits contain only 5–8 specimens and at most tens of safe resolved rows; low-rank functional regression tests the relevant distributed-shape uncertainty with materially lower variance. Revisit after reproducible functional underfit or at least 30 additional specimens per schedule. Mechanistic electrode fitting is deferred because the executable tables lack independent half-cell anchors and adjudicated mode targets.

## State reconstruction and matched forecast models

First fit out-of-specimen, forward-date cross-fitted current-state models at both clocks:

- `G30`: reconstruct C[t]/C0 and, for resistance rows, jointly log(R[t]/R0), from resolved history plus q30 scalars/morphology.
- `G360-scalar`: G30 inputs plus added duration/q/current/temperature/family/stage scalars, but no added morphology.
- `G360-shape`: the same plus structured or functional segment innovation.

Report native-scale MAE/RMSE, bias, calibration and specimen/family/stage influence. This directly quantifies whether the segment mostly refines current state.

Forecast comparisons use identical rows, folds, outcome transforms, family-balanced weights, predictor budgets, and nested tuning:

- `H`: resolved history through t-1, including last capacity/resistance, fixed history trends and prior slopes.
- `Q30`: H plus q30 acquisition scalars.
- `F30-T`: H+Q30 plus the selected q30 state and morphology model, allowed to predict L/S/K.
- `D-scalar`: F30-T plus all q30-to-V360 elapsed-time/q/current/temperature and stage/family controls, no added shape.
- `D-G0`: D-scalar plus G360-shape reconstructed current state, no residual segment morphology.
- `D-GL`: D-G0 plus residual segment morphology constrained to affect only L; S/K remain those of D-G0.
- `D-GT`: same predictors and penalty budget as D-GL, now allowing a prespecified zero-sum horizon interaction to predict S and secondarily K.
- `D-T0/D-TL/D-TT`: exact retrospective counterparts replace generated current state with measured C[t]/C0 (and measured R[t]/R0 for resistance). D-TT versus D-TL is decisive: added segment shape must improve future slope after actual present state while its level channel is held constant.
- `Full-T`: matched completed-discharge trajectory model, an information upper comparator, not required for the incremental hypothesis.

Family-specific fits are used when the inherited support permits; otherwise use a pooled hierarchical ridge with fixed family effects and training-only family-stage shrinkage. Freeze the parent’s earlier-family median/default penalty fallback whenever fewer than 12 safe rows or two validation specimens exist. Do not silently drop a family.

The key capacity contrasts, with M denoting family-balanced slope MAE, are:

- total waiting value `I_wait=1-M(D-GT)/M(F30-T)`;
- value beyond acquisition scalars `I_shape=1-M(D-GT)/M(D-scalar)`;
- value beyond generated-state persistence `I_gen=1-M(D-GT)/M(D-GL)`;
- decisive value beyond actual-state persistence `I_true=1-M(D-TT)/M(D-TL)`;
- state-error reduction from G30 to G360-shape and the fraction of total level gain captured by that reduction.

Resistance uses matched D-G0/D-GT and D-T0/D-TT models for log change, with recovered future resistance level also scored. It is an endpoint-specific secondary analysis.

## Evaluation, uncertainty, and negative controls

Average absolute loss first over origins within specimen, then specimens within family, then equally over the five fixed families. Horizons are not independent rows. Report native-scale MAE/RMSE for all three capacities, L/S/K, resistance level/change, 90% training-only specimen-group conformal coverage/width, donor counts, and exact leave-one-specimen/family influence.

Use 10,000 paired trajectory bootstraps resampling whole specimens within fixed family. A family-stage block bootstrap is a sensitivity and the wider interval governs. Use max-statistic simultaneous 95% intervals across generated/actual-state capacity contrasts, two representation branches, and resistance. Families are fixed; intervals do not describe a family superpopulation.

Required controls are dimension-matched sibling-segment swap, held-specimen lagged segment, within-specimen time permutation, target-trajectory shuffle, current-state-label shuffle, horizon-label permutation, and training-feature noise. Target shuffling must remove systematic gain. Temperature-matched sibling swaps are required where available. Also report correlations and variance-inflation diagnostics between segment scores and q increment, elapsed time, current, temperature, RPT stage, family, and actual C[t]. High collinearity widens inference; it is not “corrected” by deleting unfavorable rows.

## Prespecified verdict gates

Support **incremental multi-horizon capacity-trajectory information** only if all hold on both 200-row nominal and 166-row conservative sets:

1. `I_wait`, `I_shape`, `I_gen`, and `I_true` are each at least 0.05 and their simultaneous 95% lower bounds exceed zero;
2. D-TT beats D-TL for S, not merely L or the three-vector average; no horizon reverses the forecast gain;
3. structured and functional branches agree in sign, and fixed-voltage and fixed-q/C0 registrations agree;
4. at least four families improve, no family worsens by more than 5%, early/middle/late stage blocks retain sign, and every leave-one-specimen aggregate remains positive;
5. current/temperature/acquisition controls, prior-slope and calendar-time sensitivities, causal filter/cutoff sensitivities, firewalls, and negative controls pass.

Call a **state/capacity-proxy explanation** affirmatively only if waiting improves future-level prediction, G360 improves current-state reconstruction, at least 80% of the added level gain is captured by D-G0 or D-scalar, and simultaneous upper bounds for both I_gen and I_true are below 0.05. If only elapsed time/q/current/temperature accounts for the gain, label it acquisition-scalar proxy. If generated-state models improve slope but actual-state models do not, label it correction of state-reconstruction error, not future-trajectory information. If both state and true-slope gates pass, report a mixed result.

Support **secondary resistance future-change information** only after its operational future-level model improves F30-T and D-scalar by at least 5%, I_gen and I_true are at least 0.05 with simultaneous lower bounds above zero on nominal and conservative sets, nominal gains occur in four of five families, conservative gains in three of four represented families, and at least two alternative resistance definitions agree. This does not establish multi-horizon resistance trajectory.

Adverse evidence at the planned effect is a simultaneous upper bound below 0.05 for I_wait or I_true; an upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm from waiting. Also adverse are q30 matching V360 while the full curve helps, actual state erasing a generated-state gain, or prior slope matching the segment.

Inconclusive includes intervals crossing 0/0.05, nominal/conservative conflict, poor state reconstruction, structured/functional or registration reversal, family/specimen/stage dependence, acquisition collinearity too strong for stable attribution, calibration failure, placebo retention, or capacity/resistance disagreement. Capacity-only conclusions are allowed. Preserve adverse and inconclusive results. Leakage, row-random splitting, failed joins/order, endpoint imputation, or shuffled-target gain invalidates computation.

## Deliverable, compute, and claim boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted held-specimen and forward-resolution-safe G30/G360 state reconstructions plus F30, scalar-only, generated-state, actual-state, and full-curve trajectory predictions. Completion requires `source_audit.json`, `source_manifest.csv`, `boundary_order.parquet`, `horizon_support.csv`, `forecast_origins.parquet`, `outer_folds.csv`, `inner_folds.csv`, `stop_events.parquet`, `feature_provenance.json`, `tail_firewall.json`, `segment_registration.parquet`, `segment_features.parquet`, `state_crossfit_predictions.parquet`, `state_metrics.json`, `trajectory_targets.parquet`, `predictions.parquet`, `trajectory_metrics.json`, `attribution_contrasts.json`, `registration_sensitivity.json`, `negative_controls.json`, `uncertainty.parquet`, `influence.csv`, `model_artifacts/`, `environment.json`, `verdict.json`, and `report.md`. Every conclusion must cite computed fields and distinguish measurements from reconstructions.

Plan 12 CPU cores, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and 18,000 seconds, within the configured 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/28,800-s solver envelope. Parent extraction audits took roughly 84–123 seconds; the new complete boundary audit took 21.3 seconds. These establish extraction feasibility only. Functional ridge/FPCA and grouped bootstraps are CPU-suitable. Cache extracted representations first; if runtime is tight, defer curvature, sparse resistance t+4, and 3.45-V sensitivity, never the population, clocks, actual-state contrast, primary slope, or falsification gates.

An automatic verifier can recompute hashes, members, joins, clocks/order, masks, feature ancestry, folds, reconstructions, predictions, hierarchical losses, intervals, controls, and deterministic verdict mapping. It must accept warranted supportive, proxy/state-only, mixed, adverse, endpoint-specific, and inconclusive conclusions.

It cannot decide that an effect is electrochemically causal or economically sufficient, identify LLI/LAM/plating/SEI, prove that physically interrupting an RPT is harmless, or establish transfer beyond these five families and one Li/Kirkaldy lineage. ## Evaluation boundary

feature ancestry, prediction/loss arithmetic, intervals, control status, and deterministic

# Does waiting from q30 to a causal 3.60-V stop add future-trajectory information, or only sharpen the current-capacity proxy?

## Scientific question, hypothesis, and advance

The strongest evidence currently supports feasibility, not prognostic value. Li2025 contains 511 measured C/10 discharge curves from 40 specimens in five experiment families; the assigned parents established a causal q30 clock, a causal 3.60-V clock, and usable future-capacity and scheduled-resistance outcomes. Public partial-curve literature supports the broad claim that partial voltage curves can encode contemporaneous health, but does not establish the incremental claim below under held-specimen, forward-resolution-safe testing. No outcome model has been fitted.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among Li2025 origins for which the causal 3.60-V event follows q30, morphology acquired strictly between q30 and 3.60 V contains information about the measured future capacity trajectory at RPT t+1,t+2,t+3 beyond resolved history, all q30 information, added elapsed-time/current/temperature/charge scalars, and either an out-of-specimen reconstruction or the retrospectively observed contemporaneous capacity.

This is an information-acquisition hypothesis, not a causal effect of discharging, and “causal clock” only means computable online from observations up to the stop. Its advance is to localize when trajectory-relevant information is acquired. A favorable q30 model alone cannot show whether later waiting helps; a favorable 3.60-V model alone can be a better proxy for completed capacity. The decisive contrast forces the added segment to predict the zero-sum future slope after actual current state, prior slope, protocol family, RPT stage, and acquisition conditions are supplied.

The primary endpoint is capacity. Scheduled resistance is a secondary endpoint because only a current-to-t+2 change is well supported; it can test incremental future-change information but cannot independently establish multi-horizon shape.

## Population, clocks, and audited support

The population is the same 40 Li/Kirkaldy-lineage specimens and five opaque experiment-family strata, with 511 RPT states dated 2020-06-26 through 2021-07-22. Specimen identity is `experiment directory|cell`; a cell letter alone is invalid. Families are represented schedules, not mechanisms or an external population. RPT rows and horizons within a specimen are repeated observations.

For RPT origin t>=1:

1. q30 is the first linearly interpolated active-discharge point where phase-local q equals 0.30 times that specimen’s already resolved measured RPT0 C/10 capacity C0.
2. V360 is the first sample completing 20 consecutive causal trailing-101-row mean-voltage samples at or below 3.60 V after a trailing mean above 3.60 V. Windows 1 and 501 and thresholds 3.75/3.45 V are sensitivities. The event time includes the confirmation samples. Centered filters are forbidden.
3. Require V360 strictly after q30. Do not swap or redefine clocks when order fails.

A new complete read-only audit found V360 after q30 in 509/511 curves. Expt-1 cell B RPT14 and cell F RPT14 reverse order and are excluded from any segment interpretation. Neither is in a primary forecast set. All 200 nominal common-capacity origins and all 107 nominal resistance origins pass the order gate. For the 200 capacity origins, V360 occurs at q/C0=0.4453–0.6001 (median 0.5501) and 84.8–173.9 minutes after q30 (median 145.9). Family median added times range 137.3–159.0 minutes. For resistance origins, q/C0=0.3614–0.5999 (median 0.5415) and added time is 35.8–173.7 minutes (median 140.9). This strong stage/family dependence motivates mandatory controls; it is not evidence of outcome information.

The inherited forward-resolution gate gives:

- primary capacity: the same 200 origins, all 40 specimens and five families, with all t+1,t+2,t+3 capacities and at least 6 safe earlier training origins from at least four other same-family specimens; mandatory conservative replication has 166 origins with at least 12 safe origins/four specimens;
- secondary resistance: 107 t-to-t+2 origins across all 40 specimens/five families; mandatory conservative replication has 67 origins/32 specimens and omits E4;
- sparse resistance t+4 is descriptive only and cannot establish horizon dependence.

## Measured outcomes and estimands

Capacity scoring uses the measured vector

`Y_C=(C[t+1],C[t+2],C[t+3])/C0`.

Its prespecified summaries are future mean level `L=(Y1+Y2+Y3)/3`, primary trajectory slope `S=(Y3-Y1)/2` per RPT, and secondary curvature `K=Y3-2Y2+Y1`. The primary scientific loss is family-balanced MAE for S; vector-level MAE and L are required companion outcomes. A morphology effect common to all horizons is level information, not trajectory information.

Resistance uses finite positive scheduled `Mean_R (Ohms)`: future level `log(R[t+2]/R0)` and change `S_R=log(R[t+2]/R[t])/2`. Calendar-rate change per 30 days is a sensitivity. Alternative definitions are `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`. Since S_R algebraically includes current R[t], a resistance trajectory claim requires the retrospective actual-state comparison and cannot rest on operational prediction alone.

No endpoint is interpolated or imputed. C/10 capacity and resistance are measured diagnostic summaries. q is coulomb-counted from a phase-local counter and checked by signed-current integration; it is not independent SOC. Reconstructed states and future predictions are fitted quantities, not measurements or degradation mechanisms.

## Exact read-only data binding

Use:

- archive source `[private path]`;
- runtime mount `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`;
- SHA-256 `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`; 835,141,024 bytes and 3,993 members;
- catalog source `[private path]`;
- runtime catalog `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`;
- catalog SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

The catalog records 1,801 Li2025 tables. This experiment reads the 511 discharge and 40 extracted-summary tables only.

Summary members match
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`.
Representative catalog table `datasets/Li2025/table-92783194d5d74ccc.json` has 15 rows and columns unnamed first field (RPT), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, and the four resistance fields above.

Discharge members match
`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C discharge data.csv`.
Representative table `datasets/Li2025/table-48e85d15b6c70efa.json` binds Expt-1 cell-A RPT0 and contains `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, signed `Current (mA)`, phase-local `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`.

Join one-to-one on independently parsed experiment, cell, and integer RPT. Parse `RPT start date` day-first. Require unique consecutive RPTs and strictly increasing dates. Retain finite active-discharge rows with -550<=current<=-450 mA; subtract first retained time and charge; preserve sign; verify charge against `-integral(I dt)/3600`. Abort on source hash, member, schema, key, chronology, units, sign, monotonicity, required endpoint, or boundary-order failure in an included origin.

## Information firewall and splits

For each scored specimen, exclude that entire specimen from outcome fitting, state reconstruction, expected-segment construction, registration, residualization, scaling, basis/FPCA/PLS estimation, tuning, and calibration.

A capacity training origin j is eligible only when its t+3 target date is strictly earlier than the scored origin’s t date. A resistance training origin requires its t+2 target date strictly earlier. Same-day resolution is excluded. Inner validation repeats held-specimen and latest-target masks.

At q30, operational inputs may use RPT0 values, summary/curve history through t-1, and current rows through q30. At V360 they may additionally use rows after q30 through the confirmed V360 event. Current completed capacity/resistance; achieved future exposure; current `Ageing Cycles`, throughput, degradation days, or age-set end values lacking a within-RPT availability time; complete duration/span/end voltage; post-stop rows; and future records are forbidden. Actual current C[t] and R[t] appear only in labeled retrospective models.

Two firewalls are required: poisoning all post-q30 rows must leave q30 features/predictions bitwise unchanged; poisoning all post-V360 rows and current/future summary values must leave V360 operational features/predictions unchanged. Feature ancestry records every source column and last sample.

## Representations and controls

Every model contains identical training-only standardization, fixed family indicators, nominal temperature, RPT stage and a prespecified cubic stage basis; family-by-stage shrinkage terms are included where support permits. Report early/middle/late stage blocks and within-family effects. A no-family/no-stage sensitivity diagnoses dependence but cannot support transport.

The q30 representation is frozen from the trajectory parent: structured voltage crossings/areas/slopes/derivative extrema and a 61-point q/C0 functional prefix with held-specimen, earlier-date expected-prefix innovations.

The incremental segment has two comparable branches. Every segment feature is calculated strictly from samples after q30 through V360; a voltage crossing that occurred before q30 is masked as already-acquired information.

- **Structured ridge (simple baseline):** added duration; q increment and V360 q/C0; signed-current median, drift and variability; temperature level, drift and excursion; charge-integration discrepancy; post-q30 q/C0 locations and elapsed times at those of 3.90, 3.85, 3.80, 3.75, 3.70, 3.65 and 3.60 V that remain ahead of q30; missing/already-passed indicators; and interval signed/absolute areas, slopes, RMS, and derivative extrema. It is transparent and tests whether a few landmarks suffice.
- **Functional segment (substantive alternative):** a primary fixed physical q/C0 grid from 0.30 to 0.44, which the boundary audit shows is available before V360 for every primary capacity origin, plus a post-0.44 tail represented on causal voltage landmarks down to 3.60 V. Phase/amplitude innovations are relative to the held specimen’s t-1 segment and strictly earlier same-family sibling increments. Residualize against q30 predictors and all added scalars training-only; fit scalar-on-function ridge with cubic B-splines and second-difference penalty or separate 1–4 component training-only FPCA/PLS channels. It can reveal distributed/localized deformation that landmark summaries lose.

Registration controls are mandatory: (a) the primary fixed physical q/C0 grid 0.30–0.44; (b) post-q30 fixed-voltage landmarks with already-passed masking; and (c) normalized segment progress as a sensitivity only. The latter uses the causally observed V360 q span but cannot establish coordinate-robust morphology. Causal windows 1/101/501 and 3.75/3.45-V events are additional sensitivities. A gain confined to one registration is inconclusive.

The neural alternative is deferred because family fits contain only 5–8 specimens and at most tens of safe resolved rows; low-rank functional regression tests the relevant distributed-shape uncertainty with materially lower variance. Revisit after reproducible functional underfit or at least 30 additional specimens per schedule. Mechanistic electrode fitting is deferred because the executable tables lack independent half-cell anchors and adjudicated mode targets.

## State reconstruction and matched forecast models

First fit out-of-specimen, forward-date cross-fitted current-state models at both clocks:

- `G30`: reconstruct C[t]/C0 and, for resistance rows, jointly log(R[t]/R0), from resolved history plus q30 scalars/morphology.
- `G360-scalar`: G30 inputs plus added duration/q/current/temperature/family/stage scalars, but no added morphology.
- `G360-shape`: the same plus structured or functional segment innovation.

Report native-scale MAE/RMSE, bias, calibration and specimen/family/stage influence. This directly quantifies whether the segment mostly refines current state.

Forecast comparisons use identical rows, folds, outcome transforms, family-balanced weights, predictor budgets, and nested tuning:

- `H`: resolved history through t-1, including last capacity/resistance, fixed history trends and prior slopes.
- `Q30`: H plus q30 acquisition scalars.
- `F30-T`: H+Q30 plus the selected q30 state and morphology model, allowed to predict L/S/K.
- `D-scalar`: F30-T plus all q30-to-V360 elapsed-time/q/current/temperature and stage/family controls, no added shape.
- `D-G0`: D-scalar plus G360-shape reconstructed current state, no residual segment morphology.
- `D-GL`: D-G0 plus residual segment morphology constrained to affect only L; S/K remain those of D-G0.
- `D-GT`: same predictors and penalty budget as D-GL, now allowing a prespecified zero-sum horizon interaction to predict S and secondarily K.
- `D-T0/D-TL/D-TT`: exact retrospective counterparts replace generated current state with measured C[t]/C0 (and measured R[t]/R0 for resistance). D-TT versus D-TL is decisive: added segment shape must improve future slope after actual present state while its level channel is held constant.
- `Full-T`: matched completed-discharge trajectory model, an information upper comparator, not required for the incremental hypothesis.

Family-specific fits are used when the inherited support permits; otherwise use a pooled hierarchical ridge with fixed family effects and training-only family-stage shrinkage. Freeze the parent’s earlier-family median/default penalty fallback whenever fewer than 12 safe rows or two validation specimens exist. Do not silently drop a family.

The key capacity contrasts, with M denoting family-balanced slope MAE, are:

- total waiting value `I_wait=1-M(D-GT)/M(F30-T)`;
- value beyond acquisition scalars `I_shape=1-M(D-GT)/M(D-scalar)`;
- value beyond generated-state persistence `I_gen=1-M(D-GT)/M(D-GL)`;
- decisive value beyond actual-state persistence `I_true=1-M(D-TT)/M(D-TL)`;
- state-error reduction from G30 to G360-shape and the fraction of total level gain captured by that reduction.

Resistance uses matched D-G0/D-GT and D-T0/D-TT models for log change, with recovered future resistance level also scored. It is an endpoint-specific secondary analysis.

## Evaluation, uncertainty, and negative controls

Average absolute loss first over origins within specimen, then specimens within family, then equally over the five fixed families. Horizons are not independent rows. Report native-scale MAE/RMSE for all three capacities, L/S/K, resistance level/change, 90% training-only specimen-group conformal coverage/width, donor counts, and exact leave-one-specimen/family influence.

Use 10,000 paired trajectory bootstraps resampling whole specimens within fixed family. A family-stage block bootstrap is a sensitivity and the wider interval governs. Use max-statistic simultaneous 95% intervals across generated/actual-state capacity contrasts, two representation branches, and resistance. Families are fixed; intervals do not describe a family superpopulation.

Required controls are dimension-matched sibling-segment swap, held-specimen lagged segment, within-specimen time permutation, target-trajectory shuffle, current-state-label shuffle, horizon-label permutation, and training-feature noise. Target shuffling must remove systematic gain. Temperature-matched sibling swaps are required where available. Also report correlations and variance-inflation diagnostics between segment scores and q increment, elapsed time, current, temperature, RPT stage, family, and actual C[t]. High collinearity widens inference; it is not “corrected” by deleting unfavorable rows.

## Prespecified verdict gates

Support **incremental multi-horizon capacity-trajectory information** only if all hold on both 200-row nominal and 166-row conservative sets:

1. `I_wait`, `I_shape`, `I_gen`, and `I_true` are each at least 0.05 and their simultaneous 95% lower bounds exceed zero;
2. D-TT beats D-TL for S, not merely L or the three-vector average; no horizon reverses the forecast gain;
3. structured and functional branches agree in sign, and fixed-voltage and fixed-q/C0 registrations agree;
4. at least four families improve, no family worsens by more than 5%, early/middle/late stage blocks retain sign, and every leave-one-specimen aggregate remains positive;
5. current/temperature/acquisition controls, prior-slope and calendar-time sensitivities, causal filter/cutoff sensitivities, firewalls, and negative controls pass.

Call a **state/capacity-proxy explanation** affirmatively only if waiting improves future-level prediction, G360 improves current-state reconstruction, at least 80% of the added level gain is captured by D-G0 or D-scalar, and simultaneous upper bounds for both I_gen and I_true are below 0.05. If only elapsed time/q/current/temperature accounts for the gain, label it acquisition-scalar proxy. If generated-state models improve slope but actual-state models do not, label it correction of state-reconstruction error, not future-trajectory information. If both state and true-slope gates pass, report a mixed result.

Support **secondary resistance future-change information** only after its operational future-level model improves F30-T and D-scalar by at least 5%, I_gen and I_true are at least 0.05 with simultaneous lower bounds above zero on nominal and conservative sets, nominal gains occur in four of five families, conservative gains in three of four represented families, and at least two alternative resistance definitions agree. This does not establish multi-horizon resistance trajectory.

Adverse evidence at the planned effect is a simultaneous upper bound below 0.05 for I_wait or I_true; an upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm from waiting. Also adverse are q30 matching V360 while the full curve helps, actual state erasing a generated-state gain, or prior slope matching the segment.

Inconclusive includes intervals crossing 0/0.05, nominal/conservative conflict, poor state reconstruction, structured/functional or registration reversal, family/specimen/stage dependence, acquisition collinearity too strong for stable attribution, calibration failure, placebo retention, or capacity/resistance disagreement. Capacity-only conclusions are allowed. Preserve adverse and inconclusive results. Leakage, row-random splitting, failed joins/order, endpoint imputation, or shuffled-target gain invalidates computation.

## Deliverable, compute, and claim boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted held-specimen and forward-resolution-safe G30/G360 state reconstructions plus F30, scalar-only, generated-state, actual-state, and full-curve trajectory predictions. Completion requires `source_audit.json`, `source_manifest.csv`, `boundary_order.parquet`, `horizon_support.csv`, `forecast_origins.parquet`, `outer_folds.csv`, `inner_folds.csv`, `stop_events.parquet`, `feature_provenance.json`, `tail_firewall.json`, `segment_registration.parquet`, `segment_features.parquet`, `state_crossfit_predictions.parquet`, `state_metrics.json`, `trajectory_targets.parquet`, `predictions.parquet`, `trajectory_metrics.json`, `attribution_contrasts.json`, `registration_sensitivity.json`, `negative_controls.json`, `uncertainty.parquet`, `influence.csv`, `model_artifacts/`, `environment.json`, `verdict.json`, and `report.md`. Every conclusion must cite computed fields and distinguish measurements from reconstructions.

Plan 12 CPU cores, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and 18,000 seconds, within the configured 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/28,800-s solver envelope. Parent extraction audits took roughly 84–123 seconds; the new complete boundary audit took 21.3 seconds. These establish extraction feasibility only. Functional ridge/FPCA and grouped bootstraps are CPU-suitable. Cache extracted representations first; if runtime is tight, defer curvature, sparse resistance t+4, and 3.45-V sensitivity, never the population, clocks, actual-state contrast, primary slope, or falsification gates.

An automatic verifier can recompute hashes, members, joins, clocks/order, masks, feature ancestry, folds, reconstructions, predictions, hierarchical losses, intervals, controls, and deterministic verdict mapping. It must accept warranted supportive, proxy/state-only, mixed, adverse, endpoint-specific, and inconclusive conclusions.

It cannot decide that an effect is electrochemically causal or economically sufficient, identify LLI/LAM/plating/SEI, prove that physically interrupting an RPT is harmless, or establish transfer beyond these five families and one Li/Kirkaldy lineage. Those require electrochemical expert review, a randomized interrupted-versus-completed RPT study, half-cell/post-mortem evidence, future-use interventions, and an independent cohort. Kirkaldy metadata are not independent validation; its experiment archives are unavailable here. Severson’s cohort is unavailable. The configured Li paper is metadata/review plus selected reproduction files, not inspected full paper or supplementary methods, and this proposal claims no reproduction.

# Oxford density-free support identity

## Objective

Complete the frozen, open-ended scientific experiment below. Determine whether specimen-specific longitudinal information in the Oxford `ReZ_Ohm` observed-support bounds is localized to the SOC-common projection, the SOC-differential projections, both, or neither when no probability mass is assigned to rows.

A favorable result is not required. Compute the registered experiment and report the conclusion warranted by its outputs. Adverse and inconclusive results are scientifically valid outcomes.

The strongest claim supported before this task is only computational: the admitted archive contains 66 canonical, finite 35-row `ReZ_Ohm` tables for 11 cells at BoL/MoL and nominal 20/50/80% SOC, from which sharp support bounds can be computed. The unresolved hypotheses are:

- H_C: the fixed two-slope BoL linkage model reduces held-cell common-projection descriptor loss by at least 10% versus exact-protocol peers.
- H_D: the same model reduces held-cell linear/curvature SOC-contrast descriptor loss by at least 10%.
- H_sep: only after H_C or H_D is supportive, distinct center and breadth slopes improve by at least 10% over a nested single-slope model and remain distinguishable under uncertainty and influence checks.

This is a complete investigation, not a source audit or a request to reproduce the earlier bounded screen. You must newly fit the models, run exact relinkings, uncertainty, influence, endpoint-contamination, and invariance analyses, and derive the conclusion.

## Evidence and scientific boundary

The bound README describes 12 NCR18650BD NCA/graphite 3 Ah cells, chamber setpoint 24 degC, four schedule/rate groups, and EIS at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC at BoL and MoL with 100 mA peak-to-peak excitation over 5 kHz to 10 mHz at six points per decade. The admitted EIS ZIP has paired coverage for only the 11 cells below.

The archive does not provide authoritative row frequencies, row-to-frequency mapping, acquisition weights/order, exact sweep coverage, complex impedance, repeat/remount spectra, instrument uncertainty, verified physical SOC, elapsed exposure, capacity, or a common health threshold at MoL. `N_A` has no authoritative meaning or unit here and is audit-only.

Accordingly, support can establish only that observed `ReZ_Ohm` support-bound descriptors at BoL contain held-cell information about corresponding ordinal-MoL descriptors beyond exact protocol in these cells. It cannot establish an actual frequency-weighted mean/distribution, an EIS arc, ECM/DRT parameter, ageing rate, schedule causality, fixture independence, mechanism, common physical MoL age, engineering utility, or transfer to another population. Those stronger claims require missing measurements, electrochemical expert review, or another study.

## Runtime inputs and exact population

Read only:

- `/data/e05ee114fa-oxford-eis.zip`, SHA-256 `64d1fc94dcd3b2403d3f84b88666781a4f6153068e2ef4311d7cde97106a6d27`
- `/data/4a245ba1d6-oxford-readme.txt`, SHA-256 `59489534eaa5cddd2cef74b057855d2074bbef802d3aa12db6e082f9886dc59c`
- `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`

Use exactly these independent specimens:

| group | specimen keys | rate | cycling block | calendar block | periodicity |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | G1_C15, G1_C20 | C/2 | 1 day | 5 days | short |
| 2 | G2_C3, G2_C4, G2_C8 | C/4 | 1 day | 5 days | short |
| 3 | G3_C10, G3_C11, G3_C14 | C/2 | 2 days | 10 days | long |
| 4 | G4_C12, G4_C18, G4_C19 | C/4 | 2 days | 10 days | long |

Exclude G1_C9 because paired MoL tables are absent. Exclude Groups 5–10 because they are outside the documented four-group longitudinal experiment and lack paired coverage here. The only time field is ordinal `stage`: BoL precedes MoL. Do not interpret rows, projections, endpoints, or SOCs as independent cells.

For each listed cell, `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, and `soc in {20,50,80}`, the archive member and canonical internal table are both:

`EIS/{stage}/Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{soc}.mat`

`Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{soc}`

Require exact member-stem/internal-name agreement, 35 rows, columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`, finite numeric `ReZ_Ohm`, and 66 tables/2,310 rows.

### MATLAB v5 table decoding note

These are native MATLAB table/MCOS objects. With SciPy 1.14, `scipy.io.loadmat` exposes the table descriptors and the `__function_workspace__` byte array. The following archive-specific layout was checked over all members and is supplied as schema documentation, not as scientific results:

- Split variables with `scipy.io.matlab._mio5.varmats_from_mat`; each opaque `None` variable contains the internal table name in field `s0`, in workspace order.
- Interpret `__function_workspace__.tobytes()` as little-endian float64.
- A one-table container has `ReZ_Ohm = workspace[81:116]` and `N_A = workspace[123:158]`.
- A three-table container has, for descriptor ordinal `k=0,1,2`, `ReZ_Ohm = workspace[111+282*k:146+282*k]` and `N_A = workspace[153+282*k:188+282*k]`.
- Only the three G2_C3 MoL containers and G3_C11 MoL SOC20 container have three tables. Select the descriptor whose name exactly matches the canonical name. Audit every duplicate copy and require bitwise-equal numeric columns.

Do not infer meanings from this encoding. Preserve `source_row_index` only for audit and never join stages or SOCs by row index.

Write `normalized_eis.parquet` with exact columns:

`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,source_row_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.

The table key is `(group,cell_id,stage,SOC_label_pct)`. SOC is nominal supplied metadata, not independently verified physical or coulomb-counted SOC.

## Sharp density-free identified sets

For cell i, stage t, and SOC s, let the 35 values be z. Compute:

`lower=min(z)`, `upper=max(z)`, `center=(lower+upper)/2`, and `radius=(upper-lower)/2`.

Require every radius > 1e-12 Ohm. The closure of all weighted means under arbitrary nonnegative row weights summing to one is exactly `[lower,upper]`. The three-SOC set is the box `center + diag(radius)[-1,1]^3`.

Use fixed orthonormal axes:

- `C/common = (1,1,1)/sqrt(3)`
- `D/linear = (-1,0,1)/sqrt(2)`
- `D/curvature = (1,-2,1)/sqrt(6)`

For axis a, compute sharp marginal bounds:

`projection_center = a' center`
`projection_radius = abs(a)' radius`
`projection_lower = projection_center - projection_radius`
`projection_upper = projection_center + projection_radius`
`log_breadth = log(projection_radius / 1 Ohm)`

Retain the three original centers/radii so the joint zonotope is auditable. Do not claim the two differential intervals form a jointly attainable Cartesian rectangle.

`support_intervals.parquet` must have one row per table and exact columns:
`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,lower_Ohm,upper_Ohm,center_Ohm,radius_Ohm,min_neighbor_gap_fraction,max_neighbor_gap_fraction`.

The gap fractions are the distances from the minimum/maximum to their nearest distinct neighbors divided by table width.

`projection_bounds.parquet` must have 66 rows and exact columns:
`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,block,axis,projection_center_Ohm,projection_radius_Ohm,projection_lower_Ohm,projection_upper_Ohm,log_breadth,soc20_center_Ohm,soc50_center_Ohm,soc80_center_Ohm,soc20_radius_Ohm,soc50_radius_Ohm,soc80_radius_Ohm`.

## Frozen models and loss

Run 11 leave-one-specimen-out folds. Seal held-cell MoL descriptors until scoring. Run blocks C (one common axis) and D (linear and curvature axes).

For each fold, block, descriptor channel `q in {center,log_breadth}`, and stage separately:

1. On training specimens, calculate exact-protocol means at each axis.
2. Calculate within-protocol deviations.
3. A group contributes to slopes/scales only if it has at least two training cells.
4. Weight contributing groups equally, cells equally within group, axes equally within cell.
5. The RMS scale is the square root of the weighted mean squared within-group deviation. Require all BoL and MoL scales > 1e-12 and finite.
6. Standardize within-group deviations by the corresponding stage/channel scale.

Every fold must have six within-protocol contrast degrees and at least three contributing groups.

Fit and predict:

- P_B, protocol baseline: held protocol peers' mean MoL center/log-breadth at each axis.
- S_B, scalar persistence: one zero-intercept weighted least-squares slope shared across center and log-breadth standardized deviations.
- A_B, center/breadth transport: one zero-intercept weighted slope for center and one for log-breadth.

For S and A, add the fitted standardized BoL deviation of the held cell from its training protocol mean to the training MoL protocol mean, transformed through the fold-local scales. Predicted breadth is `exp(predicted log_breadth)` Ohm. No basis, rank, regularization, or model is selected from outcomes. A is the hypothesis model; S cannot rescue A.

For model M, block B, and held cell i:

`L_MBi = mean_axes(0.5*((mY-mhat)/sYm)^2 + 0.5*((bY-bhat)/sYb)^2)`.

Use the fold-local training MoL scales. Define equal-cell mean loss `E_MB` and:

`G_BA=1-E_AB/E_PB`
`G_BS=1-E_SB/E_PB`
`G_Bsep=1-E_AB/E_SB`.

Also report raw center error, log-breadth error, reconstructed bounds, and one-dimensional Hausdorff interval error. These do not replace the primary loss.

`outer_predictions.parquet` columns:
`specimen_key,group,block,axis,model,observed_center_Ohm,observed_log_breadth,predicted_center_Ohm,predicted_log_breadth,predicted_lower_Ohm,predicted_upper_Ohm,center_scale_Ohm,log_breadth_scale`.

`outer_losses.csv` columns:
`specimen_key,group,block,model,primary_loss,center_abs_error_Ohm,log_breadth_abs_error,hausdorff_Ohm`.

`transport_coefficients.csv` columns:
`held_specimen_key,block,model,gamma_center,gamma_breadth,bol_center_scale,mol_center_scale,bol_breadth_scale,mol_breadth_scale,contrast_df,contributing_groups`.
For S, repeat its scalar slope in both gamma columns.

## Exact relinking calibration

Enumerate all `2! * 3! * 3! * 3! = 432` allocations, lexicographically by group and donor index, including identity first. Within each group, permute each cell's complete three-SOC BoL bundle. The bundle includes all six endpoints and derived C/D descriptors. Keep MoL, protocol, stage, and SOC fixed. Never permute endpoints, axes, channels, or rows separately.

For every allocation rerun all 11 folds, group means, scales, S, and A. P must be invariant within 1e-12. For observed `T_C=G_CA` and `T_D=G_DA`:

`p_C = count(max(T_C^a,T_D^a) >= T_C_obs)/432`
`p_D = count(max(T_C^a,T_D^a) >= T_D_obs)/432`.

Store one row per allocation and support variant in `all_432_relinkings.parquet` with columns:
`support_variant,allocation_id,is_identity,gain_A_C,gain_A_D,gain_S_C,gain_S_D,gain_sep_C,gain_sep_D,p_loss_C,p_loss_D`.

The five variants are `primary,remove_min,remove_max,remove_min_max,remove_two_each`, giving 2,160 rows. `p_loss_C/D` are the invariant P mean losses.

Only after a block supports A versus P, calculate its separation fraction using the maximum separation statistic across all A-supportive blocks. Relinking fractions are conditional diagnostics under unverified within-group exchangeability, not randomization/population p-values.

## Stability and influence

Use exactly `numpy.random.Generator(numpy.random.PCG64(20260924))`. Generate 10,000 group-stratified cell resamples, preserving group sizes 2/3/3/3, from fixed observed-fold cell losses. Recompute `G_CA,G_DA,G_CS,G_DS,G_Csep,G_Dsep`, A/P and A/S cell-win mass, and `G_CA-G_DA`. Percentile intervals use NumPy's default linear 2.5th/97.5th percentiles. These are conditional stability summaries, not population confidence intervals or posterior probabilities of physical truth.

`bootstrap_metrics.parquet` has 10,000 rows:
`draw_id,gain_A_C,gain_A_D,gain_S_C,gain_S_D,gain_sep_C,gain_sep_D,win_mass_A_C,win_mass_A_D,win_mass_sep_C,win_mass_sep_D,gain_A_C_minus_D`.

For every held cell/block, compute fixed-prediction omission metrics in `held_influence.csv`:
`omitted_specimen_key,block,gain_A,gain_S,gain_sep,wins_A,wins_sep`.

Refit the complete primary analysis after deleting each of the nine Group 2–4 cells. Group 1 full deletion is structurally undefined and must be recorded, not repaired by changing the baseline. `deletion_refits.csv` columns:
`deleted_specimen_key,group,block,status,gain_A,gain_S,gain_sep,gamma_center_mean,gamma_breadth_mean`.
Include four Group-1 rows (two cells by two blocks) with `status=structurally_undefined` and null numeric fields, plus 18 fitted rows.

`group_metrics.csv` columns:
`group,block,model,mean_loss,gain_vs_P,wins_vs_P`.
For adverse classification, “no group has a multiplicity-compatible 10% gain” means no observed group-level A gain versus P is >=0.10.

## Endpoint-contamination and invariance gates

Rerun the complete 432-allocation experiment after:

1. removing only each table minimum;
2. removing only each table maximum;
3. removing both minimum and maximum;
4. removing two smallest and two largest.

These are support-contamination tests, not alternate density choices. `support_contamination_metrics.csv` columns:
`support_variant,block,gain_A,gain_S,gain_sep,p_familywise_A,wins_A,min_group_gain_A,min_fixed_omission_gain_A,min_full_deletion_gain_A,classification_before_endpoint_gate`.

Audit:

- at least 1,000 seeded row permutations;
- at least 1,000 seeded random positive integer row-multiplicity draws in [1,100], retaining every unique value;
- at least 1,000 seeded independent positive affine BoL/MoL transforms;
- every duplicate-container choice;
- reconstruction from stored endpoints.

Use PCG64(20260924) for audit randomness. Standardized gains and branch decisions must agree within 1e-12 where invariance is required. Row permutation/multiplicity must also preserve endpoints exactly. Run equal-cell rather than equal-contributing-group slope weights as a non-rescuing sensitivity. Report 5% and 20% margins descriptively.

`invariance_audit.json` must record counts, maximum absolute endpoint/gain differences, duplicate equality, endpoint reconstruction, branch agreement, affine parameters or their hash, and the equal-cell-weight sensitivity. Any failed registered gate forces an inconclusive classification.

## Frozen classification

The 10% margin is a dataset-scale loss convention, not instrument resolution or engineering utility.

A block B is `supportive` only if all are true:

- G_BA >= 0.10;
- family-wise p_B <= 0.05;
- bootstrap 95% lower bound for G_BA > 0;
- A beats P in at least 9/11 held cells;
- all 11 fixed-loss omissions retain gain >0 and at least 9 retain gain >=0.10;
- no group gain is <=-0.10;
- all source, scale, positivity, finite, fit, and invariance gates pass;
- remove_min, remove_max, and remove_min_max each retain G_BA >0; remove_min_max retains G_BA >=0.10; remove_two_each retains G_BA >0;
- every admissible Group 2–4 deletion/refit retains gain >0.

A block is `adverse` for the registered 10% claim only if all are true:

- G_BA <0.10;
- bootstrap 95% upper bound for G_BA <0.10;
- p_B >0.05;
- A beats P in at most 7/11 cells;
- no group A gain is >=0.10;
- computability gates pass;
- none of the four endpoint variants is supportive under all supportive criteria applicable to that variant.

Every other valid result, including exactly 8/11 wins, endpoint reversal, margin-spanning uncertainty, group opposition, influential cells, or calibration/stability disagreement, is `inconclusive`.

Overall classification:

- `common-confined support identity`: C supportive, D adverse, and bootstrap lower bound for G_CA-G_DA >0.
- `SOC-differential support identity: differential-specific`: D supportive and C adverse.
- `SOC-differential support identity: distributed`: C and D supportive.
- `common-supported, differential unresolved`: C supportive and D inconclusive.
- `absent at the registered margin`: C and D adverse.
- `inconclusive/endpoint-unstable`: every other pattern.

A `location-versus-breadth separation` claim for block B additionally requires G_Bsep >=0.10, gated family-wise separation fraction <=0.05, A beats S in at least 9/11 cells, positive bootstrap lower bound, and a nonzero same-sign `gamma_center-gamma_breadth` under every valid fixed omission, full refit, and support variant. Otherwise do not make that claim even if A supports linkage.

## Required machine-readable outputs

Write all 18 required files directly under `/workspace`. CSV and Parquet files must use the exact columns and row counts above, finite numeric values unless explicitly allowed null, and no duplicate logical keys.

`member_manifest.csv` columns:
`member,canonical_variable,container_sha256,rows,columns,selected_descriptor_ordinal,duplicate_copy_count`.

`duplicate_audit.json` records every canonical internal variable with more than one copy, all source members, SHA-256 hashes of both numeric columns, and `bitwise_equal=true`.

`source_audit.json` records the three bound hashes, source schema, expected/actual counts, exclusions, ordinal time field, MAT extraction layout, finite/positivity checks, and `all_gates_pass`.

`metrics.json` must contain:

- `blocks.C` and `blocks.D`: P/S/A mean losses; G_A/G_S/G_sep; A-vs-P and A-vs-S wins; family-wise A and gated separation fractions; bootstrap lower/upper/mass-above-0/mass-above-0.10; fixed omission minima/count-above-margin; minimum group gain; minimum deletion gain; per-variant gains; and all gate booleans.
- `gain_A_C_minus_D` bootstrap interval.
- `sensitivity_margins` for 0.05, 0.10, 0.20.
- `random_seed=20260924`, `bootstrap_draws=10000`, `allocations=432`, `invariance_draws>=1000`.
- `computational_claims_checkable` and `scientific_adjudication_required` lists.

`conclusion.json` must contain exactly:

- `block_classification`: object with C and D, each one of `supportive/adverse/inconclusive`;
- `overall_classification`: one exact overall label above;
- `separation_claims`: list containing only blocks that pass every separation gate;
- `supported_claim`: a concise archive-conditional claim consistent with classification;
- `adverse_scope`: state that adverse evidence concerns only the registered low-capacity observed-support model and 10% margin;
- `limitations`: include unknown frequency/weights, endpoint coverage/noise, ordinal MoL, unverified exchangeability, tiny cohort, no mechanism/causality/external transfer;
- `required_additional_evidence`: include authoritative frequency/channel semantics, complex impedance, repeat/remount uncertainty, verified SOC/exposure clocks, more cells/protocols, expert review, external validation;
- `trace`: all threshold operands used to classify each block and overall result.

The verifier independently checks source values, bound arithmetic, key model/result arithmetic, relinking/uncertainty summaries, and deterministic classification. It rewards warranted supportive, adverse, and inconclusive outcomes equally. It rejects favorable overclaims, overbroad adverse claims, inconsistent uncertainty, and canned outputs.

## Resources and completion boundary

Use CPU. The planned workload is 8 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic thread settings, and checkpoints every 36 allocations. The full study was estimated at 10–30 CPU minutes and must fit within 7,200 seconds. GPU use adds no scientific value for extrema, tiny least-squares fits, and finite relinkings.

Completion means all specified fits, estimates, resamples, stress tests, audits, outputs, and a warranted conclusion are present. Readiness checks only establish dependency and input access; they are not evidence that this objective was solved.
