`Y[c,s,k] = q[c,MoL,s,k] - q[c,BoL,s,k]`.

This subtraction aligns equal empirical probabilities only. It is not a row join, frequency join, tracked spectral point, or claim that the same acquisition generated rank `k` at both stages. Independently sorting each table makes all results exactly invariant to source-row permutations.

For rank interval `I_k=((k-1)/35,k/35]`, define five probability-mass vertices
`w^(a,b)_k=F_Beta(a,b)(k/35)-F_Beta(a,b)((k-1)/35)`:

- uniform `(1,1)`;
- center-emphasized `(2,2)`;
- tail-emphasized `(1/2,1/2)`;
- low-`ReZ` emphasized `(1,2)`;
- high-`ReZ` emphasized `(2,1)`.

Require finite strictly positive weights summing to one within `1e-12`. Let `M` be their convex hull and `wbar` their arithmetic mean. “Low” and “high” refer only to sorted real-impedance values, never frequency.

Every fitted coefficient, standardization, ridge penalty, and hyperparameter is learned once under `wbar`; evaluation at a vertex or mixture cannot change predictions or select a model. For fixed predictions, baseline and candidate losses are linear in `w`. Because denominators must be positive, directed gains, same-target gain contrasts, shape increments, and pairwise fixed-action loss ratios are linear-fractional; extrema over `M` occur at vertices. Verify this against 10,000 seeded random convex mixtures.

The class is deliberately bounded. All nonnegative weights would allow an adversary to concentrate on one observed value and make the scientific target vacuous. Conclusions apply to `M`, not to unknown frequency integration or every possible acquisition schedule.

## Matched models with one frozen substantive alternative

Let `u_k=(k-0.5)/35`. Build once a cubic spline basis with `SplineTransformer(n_knots=5,degree=3,knots="uniform",include_bias=False,extrapolation="constant")`. Under inner product `<f,g>_wbar=sum_k wbar_k f_k g_k`, residualize its columns against the constant vector, take deterministic weighted SVD, fix each retained vector’s sign by making its largest-absolute entry positive, and retain singular values above `1e-10` of the largest. Require the reported rank, weighted orthonormality, and reconstruction checks.

For every possible source anchor `a`, define:

- quantile location `mu[c,a]=sum_k wbar_k Y[c,a,k]`;
- smooth centered quantile shape `h[c,a,:]=P_Q Y[c,a,:]`;
- discarded residual `e=Y-mu-h`.

Report location, smooth-shape, and discarded weighted energy under every vertex plus maximum residual. This is a low-rank empirical-quantile description, not a complete spectrum or process decomposition.

Fit each directed edge `a->t, a != t` separately. All models use exactly the same cells, outer/inner folds, target scales, protocol information, and BoL inputs:

- **B0, no-MoL-anchor baseline:** intercept; the fixed spline basis in `u`; protocol contrasts `r=+1/-1` for C/2/C/4, `p=+1/-1` for short/long, and `rp`; all protocol-by-spline interactions; and the same-rank independently sorted BoL `ReZ_Ohm` values at 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC.
- **L, simple location transfer:** B0 plus source-anchor `mu[c,a]`, repeated across target ranks.
- **H, substantive quantile-shape transfer:** L plus `h[c,a,k]`.

H is the frozen primary model; it cannot be replaced after seeing which model gives a preferred conclusion. L is the matched simple comparator. L asks whether a single shift of the source empirical distribution is enough. H retains a smooth rank-varying redistribution across observed `ReZ` quantiles that L discards. The incremental H-versus-L result determines whether any primary advantage specifically requires the registered shape information.

No source-row coordinate, frequency, `N_A`, outcome-tuned representation, or held-cell MoL target enters B0. The same-rank BoL predictors align empirical probability across tables, not source rows.

## Specimen-held-out fitting and losses

Use 11 outer leave-one-specimen-out folds. Within every outer fold tune each edge/model separately by leave-one-specimen-out folds among the ten outer-training cells, using ridge `alpha in {1e-4,1e-3,...,1e4}`, an unpenalized intercept, and `wbar`-weighted mean squared loss with equal total weight per fitting specimen. Standardize non-intercept columns on fitting rows only, report and drop exact-zero-variance columns, recompute all scales and transforms inside each split, and break alpha ties toward larger regularization.

For outer fold `o`, target `t`, and rank `k`, compute once from outer-training specimens:
`q[o,t,k]=max(raw_MAD({Y[c,t,k]:c != o}),1e-6 ohm)`.
The same `q` is used for B0/L/H, both candidate anchors, all vertices, and every action involving target `t`. Fit-local versions are used in inner tuning.

For model `m`, edge `a->t`, held cell `o`, and vertex `v`:
`L[m,a,t,o,v]=sum_k w[v,k]*((Y[o,t,k]-Yhat[m,a,t,o,k])/q[o,t,k])^2`.
Aggregate the 11 held cells equally:
`E[m,a,t,v]=(1/11)sum_o L[m,a,t,o,v]`.

B0 predictions must be bitwise identical between the two candidate anchors for a target. Define:

`G_H[a,t,v]=1-E[H,a,t,v]/E[B0,t,v]`,
`G_L[a,t,v]=1-E[L,a,t,v]/E[B0,t,v]`, and
`G_shape[a,t,v]=1-E[H,a,t,v]/E[L,a,t,v]`.

Report raw-ohm quantile RMSE secondarily. A 10% gain is an archive-scale model-loss margin, not instrument resolution or engineering utility.

Repeat the full observed fit using only inner validation folds whose fitting partition retains all four groups. A conclusion changed by this rule is inconclusive.

## Primary target-matched estimands

Freeze the parent’s orientations:

- target 20: `D20(v)=G_H[50,20,v]-G_H[80,20,v]`;
- target 50: `D50(v)=G_H[20,50,v]-G_H[80,50,v]`;
- target 80: `D80(v)=G_H[20,80,v]-G_H[50,80,v]`.

For each target, robust positive superiority requires `min_v D_t(v)>=0.10`; robust negative superiority requires `max_v D_t(v)<=-0.10`. Because the compared gains share the exact target-specific B0 denominator, each contrast is linear-fractional in the measure, and its extrema occur at vertices. Report all vertices and 5%/20% margins descriptively.

A favored directed edge must also be **robust-useful**: `min_v G_H[a,t,v]>=0.10`, multiplicity-controlled linkage evidence, a positive simultaneous stability lower bound, and the deletion/tuning gates below. Relative superiority without useful absolute transfer is inconclusive.

Report the corresponding L contrasts and shape increments. H support with no L support and robust positive `G_shape` localizes the archive-level information to the registered smooth quantile-shape component. Robustly opposite L and H directions make the anchor conclusion model-dependent and therefore inconclusive.

## Secondary prospective fixed-action estimand

For constant action `a`, define its held-cell two-omitted-target loss:
`A[a,v]=(1/11)sum_o (1/2)sum_(t != a) L[H,a,t,o,v]`.

For each ordered action pair define `C[a,b,v]=1-A[a,v]/A[b,v]`. Robust dominance of `a` over `b` requires `min_v C[a,b,v]>=0.10`. All actions give one observed MoL table and require reconstruction of exactly two SOCs, but their target composition differs; report each target’s contribution.

To simulate a prospective decision without outcome leakage, within each outer fold regenerate fully inner-cross-fitted H losses for its ten training cells. For each action, calculate its worst vertex mean loss and choose the minimax action; ties use 20, then 50, then 80. Apply that one action to the untouched outer-held cell. No held-cell MoL value, error, quality statistic, or outcome-derived representation may affect its choice. Report the 11 selected actions and the selected-policy held loss at every vertex.

A fixed anchor `a*` may be recommended for a prospective study only if all hold:

1. the nested minimax selector chooses `a*` in all 11 outer folds and every full deletion refit;
2. `a*` robustly dominates each of the two constant alternatives by at least 10%, with familywise calibration and simultaneous stability;
3. for each of the two targets `t != a*`, the target-matched H contrast favors `a*` over the other available non-target anchor by at least 10% throughout `M` and passes all target-specific gates;
4. both directed edges `a*->t` are robust-useful;
5. L never robustly favors the competitor, and tuning/trim/weighting checks preserve the decision.

This two-part gate prevents an action recommendation driven only by choosing to observe the intrinsically hardest target. Failure of the gate does not erase valid target-specific superiority.

## Exact linkage calibration and multiplicity

Enumerate all `2!*3!*3!*3!=432` within-group allocations, identity included. For each allocation move a donor cell’s complete three-SOC anchor-displacement bundle `{Y20,Y50,Y80}` jointly to one recipient record within the same protocol group. Keep recipient target outcomes, all recipient BoL profiles, protocol labels, outer folds, and target scales fixed. Rerun the complete six-edge nested B0/L/H pipeline and the nested minimax action selector. Joint movement preserves the observed covariance among candidate source anchors. B0 may be cached only after equality verification. All 432 allocations must complete.

For each of the three target contrasts and three unordered fixed-action contrasts, create both signed robust branches:
`T[h,+]=min_v contrast_h(v)` and `T[h,-]=min_v -contrast_h(v)`.
Across the 432 allocations, center and scale each of the 12 branches by its allocation mean and nonzero SD. For each allocation take the maximum standardized branch statistic. The identity allocation’s max-T exceedance fractions are familywise p-values controlling target/action contrast, direction, and measure-robust claims. Use separate max-T families for six robust directed-edge gains and six H-versus-L shape increments. No raw or vertex-wise p-value supports a robust claim.

For measure dependence, retain every contrast at every vertex and its range
`R_h=max_v contrast_h(v)-min_v contrast_h(v)`. Calibrate vertex evidence with a max statistic over all contrast/vertex/signed branches and calibrate ranges with a max over all six contrasts. A measure-dependence claim requires robust superiority to fail, familywise range `p<=0.05`, one vertex with at least 0.10 calibrated superiority and positive simultaneous stability, and another vertex with calibrated opposite superiority or a simultaneous upper bound below 0.10. Mere winner changes, unadjusted significance, or margin crossing are inconclusive.

Enumeration is computationally exact. Scientific p-value interpretation requires unverified conditional exchangeability within groups and is not randomization-based population inference, a test of protocol effects, or proof that an undocumented acquisition schedule caused the difference.

## Stability, influence, and invariance

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260924))`, draw 20,000 resamples independently within the four groups at sizes 2/3/3/3. Keep all models, edges, targets, vertices, and actions for a specimen together. Recompute gains and contrasts from frozen outer losses and form 95% simultaneous max-standardized-deviation bands across all three target contrasts, three action contrasts, and five vertices. Report invalid draws. These are conditional cell-weighting summaries, not population confidence intervals; outer training sets overlap and protocol groups are not replicated.

Delete each specimen and rerun the complete observed nested pipeline, including model tuning, scales, all vertices, and the training-only minimax action choice. A robust target direction must keep its sign and `|D|>=0.10` in every deletion. A fixed decision must satisfy its stricter rule above. Report protocol-group gains without treating four groups as independent treatment replicates.

Required checks:

1. 1,000 independent source-row permutations reproduce sorted profiles, predictions, and classifications to `1e-12`;
2. no code path joins on source row or uses it as a predictor;
3. 10,000 random convex mixtures lie within all reported vertex extrema to `1e-12`;
4. predictions are bitwise identical across evaluation vertices;
5. duplicate internal variables remain exactly equal;
6. joint positive unit multipliers 0.1 and 10 leave relative gains, p-fractions, and classification invariant;
7. trim only the lowest and highest order statistic in every table, rebuild 33-rank weights, and require every robust conclusion’s direction to persist;
8. equal-cell rather than equal-contributing-group fit weights cannot create support;
9. group-complete inner tuning cannot create or reverse support.

Checks are non-rescuing: a favorable sensitivity cannot overturn an adverse primary result.

## Frozen outcomes and falsification

A target is **measure-stably anchor-dependent** only when one signed H contrast is at least 0.10 throughout `M`, its robust max-T p-value is at most 0.05, its simultaneous stability band excludes zero in that direction, every deletion preserves direction and margin, the favored edge is robust-useful, tuning and trim checks preserve classification, and L is not robustly opposite.

- **Supportive target-specific result:** at least one target is measure-stably anchor-dependent. Conclude only that for that named target and these cells, the registered correctly linked quantile-displacement reconstruction depends on which other nominal SOC is observed.
- **Supportive fixed action:** the full five-part prospective gate is met. Conclude only that the named action is sufficiently stable to freeze for a new prospective validation study in this protocol family.
- **Adverse, robust anchor-insensitivity:** for every target all simultaneous bands lie inside [-0.10,+0.10] throughout `M`, while at least one robust-useful directed edge exists per target. Conclude useful transfer without materially resolved anchor choice.
- **Adverse, transfer absent/moot:** all six directed edges have robust stability upper bounds below 0.10 or nonpositive robust gains with adjusted p above 0.05. Conclude that the registered model does not demonstrate useful cross-SOC transfer, making anchor selection moot.
- **Measure-dependent:** the calibrated measure-dependence rule is met for a named target or action contrast. Conclude dependence on the declared empirical-rank measure, not on known frequency density.
- **Fixed-decision adverse:** no action robustly dominates both alternatives, or the nested selector does not choose one action consistently, while target-specific results may still stand. Do not recommend an anchor.
- **Inconclusive/unstable:** every other valid pattern, including broad bands, influential cells, calibration/stability disagreement, model-direction conflict, incomplete allocations, or a relative winner whose edge is not useful.

A smooth-shape claim additionally requires `min_v G_shape>=0.10` and its own multiplicity, stability, deletion, and tuning gates. Otherwise report whether location-only transfer accounts for the result. Preserve all unfavorable and inconclusive outputs.

## Alternatives, deferrals, resources, and deliverable

B0 is the no-follow-up-anchor baseline. L is the simple matched alternative using only the source distribution’s measure-blind location. H is the scientifically substantive learned alternative on the identical inputs, targets, splits, and training measure; it can expose smooth quantile-dependent redistribution that L loses. H is chosen prospectively for the primary test, not selected by performance.

Stored-index spline transfer is rejected for this crossover because source order has no admitted semantics. An unrestricted learned 5x5 shape operator, PLS/PCA, kernel map, or neural encoder could represent cross-rank deformation more flexibly, but 11 specimens and only six within-protocol contrast degrees per outer fold cannot identify outcome-trained representations reliably. Equivalent-circuit, DRT, and frequency-weighted models require authoritative frequency and complex-impedance fields. Raw residual transfer requires repeated EIS to distinguish fine structure from noise. Revisit these alternatives with those dependencies and a larger independent cohort.

Scientific completion requires newly computing:

1. source/member/internal-variable/schema/duplicate/finite-value audits;
2. 66 independently sorted profiles, empirical-quantile displacements, basis audit, and five measure vectors;
3. all outer/inner B0/L/H fits, predictions, vertex losses, six directed gains, three target contrasts, three constant-action losses, and the nested minimax policy;
4. all 432 complete-pipeline relinkings and max-T/range calibration;
5. 20,000 stability draws, 11 full deletion refits, group summaries, and all registered invariant checks;
6. a deterministic conclusion with sentence-to-output provenance.

Required outputs are `source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`, `empirical_quantiles.parquet`, `quantile_displacements.parquet`, `measure_weights.json`, `basis_audit.json`, `information_set_audit.json`, `outer_predictions.parquet`, `losses_by_measure.parquet`, `edge_metrics.csv`, `target_contrasts.csv`, `fixed_action_metrics.csv`, `nested_action_choices.csv`, `all_432_relinkings.parquet`, `multiplicity.json`, `stability_metrics.parquet`, `deletion_metrics.csv`, `group_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`, `metrics.json`, and `conclusion.json`.

Use 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS/thread settings, and checkpoints every 36 allocations. Native conversion is measured at 18.55 s. The complete nested crossover is estimated, not measured, at 1–4 wall-hours and fits the configured 16-CPU, 262,144-MiB, 28,800-s solver envelope. A readiness timing probe must extrapolate one nonidentity allocation; caching mathematically identical B0 fits is allowed, but scientific folds, models, measures, or allocations may not be dropped. GPU use adds no scientific value for these small ridge fits and exact enumerations.

## Claim and verifier boundaries

The verifier can recompute hashes, exact canonical selection, independent sorting, displacement construction, measure weights, basis, masking, fold-local scales and fits, prediction identity across measures, vertex extrema, all contrasts, selector nesting, all 432 relinkings, seeded stability draws, deletions, sensitivities, and deterministic wording. It must reject leakage from held MoL targets, source-row joins, evaluation-measure-specific fitting, post hoc model choice, a fixed-action claim lacking target-matched corroboration, and correct numbers paired with frequency, mechanism, cost, causal, or external-validity overclaims. It must accept correctly justified supportive, adverse, measure-dependent, or inconclusive outcomes.

Scientific adjudication remains necessary for the reasonableness of `M`, the 10% practical margin, within-group exchangeability, nominal-SOC validity/equilibration, BoL/MoL comparability, and whether quantile displacement is a useful electrical diagnostic object. Stronger claims require authoritative row frequencies and complex impedance, acquisition-order/timestamp and repeat/remount metadata, fixture/contact controls, common-horizon capacity/throughput/temperature records, acquisition duration/safety/cost data, electrochemical expert review, and a prospective independent cohort with the anchor frozen before MoL measurement.

No branch establishes frequency-resolved behavior, causal ageing, a microscopic mechanism, a common physical MoL age, fixture independence, forecasting, or transfer to other cells, protocols, chemistries, or laboratories.

## Inspected references

- Raj and Howey, *Path Dependent Battery Degradation Dataset 1*, DOI `10.5287/bodleian:v0ervBv6p`: the admitted README, configured catalog/metadata, ZIP inventory, and fresh exact native-table export were inspected.
- Raj et al. (2020), *Investigation of Path-Dependent Degradation in Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI `10.1002/batt.202000160`: only repository/literature-summary metadata available in prior work was used; publisher full text and supplementary methods were not inspected and no claim depends on them.
- The configured research-ambition method brief was inspected for adaptation/reproduction and compute boundaries. This proposal is a bounded adaptation, not a reproduction of a published analysis.

# Proposal: is an Oxford single-SOC anchor decision stable to empirical-mass versus trace-support representation?

## Scientific question and advance

For the exact 11 Oxford NCR18650BD cells with paired beginning-of-life (BoL) and ordinal middle-of-life (MoL) tables at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, does one observed MoL SOC anchor improve reconstruction of a specified withheld MoL SOC over the other possible anchor, and does the target-matched conclusion agree between:

1. independently sorted, documented `ReZ_Ohm` rank displacement evaluated over a prespecified class of rank measures; and
2. duplicate- and interior-resampling-invariant directional support displacement of the observed paired `(ReZ_Ohm,N_A)` point sets?

The primary hypothesis is **representation-stable target-specific anchor superiority**: for at least one withheld target, the same named anchor beats its competitor by at least 0.10 gain in both representations, with the ReZ result holding under every registered rank measure and both favored edges useful. A stronger fixed-anchor hypothesis requires the same named anchor to win both target-matched comparisons involving it in both representations.

This is not an omnibus prediction contest. Each representation predicts its own withheld-target object against its own target-matched no-anchor baseline. Raw losses are never pooled, averaged, or compared across representations. Only prespecified dimensionless gain signs, practical margins, and classifications are compared. A direct equal-complexity ReZ-endpoint anchor ablation predicts the *same paired-support target on the same loss* as the paired-anchor model; it adjudicates whether paired-support conclusions require information beyond documented ReZ extrema.

The advance is a falsifiable validity result for a prospective measurement decision. Concordance would show that the target-specific anchor conclusion is not an artifact of either empirical rank mass or unchanged-hull interior density in this archive. Discordance would identify a consequential representation boundary. It would not establish frequency localization, physical Nyquist correspondence, acquisition cost, a universal anchor, or an ageing mechanism.

The admitted README documents a 100 mA peak-to-peak EIS sweep from 5 kHz to 10 mHz at six points per decade, but the selected tables provide no row-level frequency, acquisition timestamp/order, repeat identifier, channel dictionary, unit, or sign convention for `N_A`. Independently sort `ReZ_Ohm` within each specimen-stage-SOC table:
`Q[i,z,s,1] <= ... <= Q[i,z,s,35]`, and define
`dR[i,s,k]=Q[i,MoL,s,k]-Q[i,BoL,s,k]`.
This is equal-order-statistic displacement, not row-, frequency-, or pointwise change.

For rank interval `((k-1)/35,k/35]`, define beta interval masses and freeze five vertices:
uniform `Beta(1,1)`, center `Beta(2,2)`, tails `Beta(1/2,1/2)`, low-ReZ rank `Beta(1,2)`, and high-ReZ rank `Beta(2,1)`. Let `M` be their convex hull and `wbar` their mean. With `x_k=(k-1)/34`, project an anchor displacement into `aR=P_[1,x]dR`, a fixed five-dimensional non-affine cubic-spline component `qR` obtained by weighted residualization/SVD of `SplineTransformer(n_knots=5,degree=3,include_bias=False)`, and discarded residual. Require deterministic signs, ranks 2/5/7, tolerance `1e-10`, and weighted orthogonality.

## Representation P: density-invariant paired support displacement

In every outer or inner fit, derive a density-invariant affine normalization from fitting specimens only. For each fitting table and channel compute its midpoint `(min+max)/2` and span `max-min`; set the channel center to the median of the table midpoints and scale to the median of the table spans, giving every specimen and its six tables equal total weight. Require both scales above `1e-12`; apply the locked transform to validation/held tables. Minima, maxima, midpoints, and spans are unchanged by row permutation, duplicate multiplicity, and insertion/deletion of strictly interior points, so preprocessing does not defeat the support invariance. This creates dimensionless geometry but gives `channel2_raw` no physical meaning.

Collapse exact paired duplicates. For fixed `theta_j=2*pi*j/64`, `v_j=(cos theta_j,sin theta_j)`, define
`h[i,z,s,j]=max_r v_j' z[i,z,s,r]`
and `dP[i,s,j]=h[i,MoL,s,j]-h[i,BoL,s,j]`.
No row is joined across tables. The same angular direction is a geometric coordinate, not a shared frequency or physical point. Require at least three noncollinear hull vertices per table.

Decompose the observed anchor support displacement under uniform angular weight into
`aP=P_F0 dP`, where `F0=span{1,cos(theta),sin(theta)}`, and
`qP=P_Fshape dP`, where `Fshape` contains sine/cosine harmonics 2–8 after residualization against `F0`. Require deterministic orthogonality and rank 3/14/17. The residual is reported. `aP` represents low-order translation/radial envelope change; `qP` retains smooth boundary-shape change. Neither is a mechanism.

Predicted directional vectors need not be valid support functions. Report sublinearity/discrete convexity violations and rerun loss after nearest feasible cyclic-support projection as a non-rescuing sensitivity.

Exact invariance gates: at least 1,000 independent source-row permutations, arbitrary positive duplicate replication factors, deletion of duplicate copies, and insertion/deletion of strictly interior points while preserving every hull must reproduce P representations, predictions, metrics, and classification to `1e-12`. No model may select the anchor using the held target, use another MoL SOC, infer row correspondence, or use validation/held data in normalization, scale estimation, basis fitting, standardization, or tuning.

- `B0_R`: no MoL anchor.
- `A_R`: `B0_R + aR_anchor`, the simple linked alternative.
- `H_R`: `A_R + qR_anchor`, the substantive smooth-shape alternative.

For P, use `B0_P` with the identical information budget: intercept; six nonconstant Fourier terms through harmonic 3; `r,p,rp`; their 18 interactions; and same-direction BoL supports `h20,h50,h80`.

- `B0_P`: no MoL anchor.
- `A_P`: `B0_P + aP_anchor`, simple low-order envelope transfer.
- `H_P`: `A_P + qP_anchor`, substantive smooth boundary-shape transfer.

A target direction is **supported in R** only if its worst-vertex directional contrast is at least 0.10, its 12-direction family-wise fraction is at most 0.05, simultaneous bands exclude zero in that direction at all vertices, every deletion preserves direction and margin, the favored edge is robust-useful, and sensitivities agree. **Supported in P** uses the same gates for its single angular loss. - **representation-conflicting**: opposite directions are supported in R and P;
- **ReZ-only supported**: R supports a direction and P supports neither direction;
- **paired-only supported**: P supports a direction and R supports neither direction;
- **practically anchor-insensitive**: both arms’ simultaneous bands lie inside [-0.10,0.10] and each arm has a useful edge for that target;
- **transfer absent**: neither arm has any edge whose upper stability bound reaches 0.10 and all adjusted edge tests are adverse;
- **inconclusive**: otherwise.

- 50% requires positive D20 and negative D80;
- 80% requires negative D20 and D50.

1. **supportive representation-stable fixed-anchor eligibility**: one anchor satisfies both wins in R and P and all four favored edges are robust-useful;
2. **supportive representation-stable target dependence only**: at least one target is stable, but no fixed anchor qualifies and no conflict exists;
3. **representation-dependent choice**: at least one target conflicts and no fixed anchor qualifies;
4. **ReZ-only fixed-anchor eligibility**: one anchor satisfies both R wins but not both P wins and P has no opposite supported win; this is not representation-stable;
5. **paired-geometry-only signal**: P supports but R does not; no acquisition recommendation is made because `N_A` semantics are unknown;
6. **adverse, practically anchor-insensitive**: all targets satisfy the corresponding adverse equivalence gate in both arms;
7. **adverse, transfer absent/moot**: all six edges in both arms satisfy transfer-absent gates;
8. **inconclusive**: every other valid outcome, including mixed targets, margin crossing, calibration/stability disagreement, deletion dependence, or failed audit gates.

Supportive results establish only archive-conditional held-cell reconstruction and a criterion-specific prospective anchor eligibility for another cell under these represented protocols. Adverse results falsify only the registered low-dimensional transfer families at the 10% margin. Inconclusive results mean 11 cells and four protocol groups do not discriminate the alternatives. Preserve all unfavorable outcomes.

No branch establishes frequency correspondence, imaginary impedance, a physical Nyquist envelope, equal support coverage, common exposure at MoL, path causality, fixture/contact exclusion, electrochemical mechanism, practical acquisition burden, or external transfer. Stronger claims require an authoritative channel/frequency/order dictionary, repeat/remount controls, common-boundary capacity/throughput/temperature histories, validated SOC/equilibration, more independent cells/protocols, prospective frozen-anchor validation, and electrochemical expert review.

Interior-distribution paired models await a justified acquisition measure or repeat/noise model. Personalized anchor policies are deferred because the present question is fixed target-matched eligibility.

## Representation P: density-invariant paired support displacement

In every outer or inner fit, derive a density-invariant affine normalization from fitting specimens only. For each fitting table and channel compute its midpoint `(min+max)/2` and span `max-min`; set the channel center to the median of the table midpoints and scale to the median of the table spans, giving every specimen and its six tables equal total weight. Require both scales above `1e-12`; apply the locked transform to validation/held tables. Minima, maxima, midpoints, and spans are unchanged by row permutation, duplicate multiplicity, and insertion/deletion of strictly interior points, so preprocessing does not defeat the support invariance. This creates dimensionless geometry but gives `channel2_raw` no physical meaning.

Collapse exact paired duplicates. For fixed `theta_j=2*pi*j/64`, `v_j=(cos theta_j,sin theta_j)`, define
`h[i,z,s,j]=max_r v_j' z[i,z,s,r]`
and `dP[i,s,j]=h[i,MoL,s,j]-h[i,BoL,s,j]`.
No row is joined across tables. The same angular direction is a geometric coordinate, not a shared frequency or physical point. Require at least three noncollinear hull vertices per table.

Decompose the observed anchor support displacement under uniform angular weight into
`aP=P_F0 dP`, where `F0=span{1,cos(theta),sin(theta)}`, and
`qP=P_Fshape dP`, where `Fshape` contains sine/cosine harmonics 2–8 after residualization against `F0`. Require deterministic orthogonality and rank 3/14/17. The residual is reported. `aP` represents low-order translation/radial envelope change; `qP` retains smooth boundary-shape change. Neither is a mechanism.

Predicted directional vectors need not be valid support functions. Report sublinearity/discrete convexity violations and rerun loss after nearest feasible cyclic-support projection as a non-rescuing sensitivity.

Exact invariance gates: at least 1,000 independent source-row permutations, arbitrary positive duplicate replication factors, deletion of duplicate copies, and insertion/deletion of strictly interior points while preserving every hull must reproduce P representations, predictions, metrics, and classification to `1e-12`. Hull-vertex deletion changes the estimand and is an influence analysis, not an invariance requirement.

## Information mask and six directed edges

Fit all six `anchor a -> target t`, `a != t`. At held-cell prediction, available inputs are protocol, all three BoL tables, and exactly one MoL anchor table. Only that anchor’s displacement is available. Both non-anchor MoL tables are sealed; the target table is opened only for scoring. Audit every feature lineage against this prospective mask.

No model may select the anchor using the held target, use another MoL SOC, infer row correspondence, or use validation/held data in normalization, scale estimation, basis fitting, standardization, or tuning.

## Matched baselines and alternatives

For representation R and target `t`, use the parent’s 31-column `B0_R`: intercept; six fixed rank-spline columns; protocol `r,p,rp` with `r=+1/-1` for C/2/C/4 and `p=+1/-1` for short/long; 18 protocol-by-nonconstant-spline terms; and same-rank BoL `Q20,Q50,Q80`.

- `B0_R`: no MoL anchor.
- `A_R`: `B0_R + aR_anchor`, the simple linked alternative.
- `H_R`: `A_R + qR_anchor`, the substantive smooth-shape alternative.

For P, use `B0_P` with the identical information budget: intercept; six nonconstant Fourier terms through harmonic 3; `r,p,rp`; their 18 interactions; and same-direction BoL supports `h20,h50,h80`.

- `B0_P`: no MoL anchor.
- `A_P`: `B0_P + aP_anchor`, simple low-order envelope transfer.
- `H_P`: `A_P + qP_anchor`, substantive smooth boundary-shape transfer.

Thus each arm has a target-matched no-anchor baseline, one simple anchor feature, and one additional prespecified shape feature. `H_R` can retain nonlinear empirical-rank bending that `A_R` loses. `H_P` can retain angular boundary deformation that `A_P` loses. Both use two learned anchor coefficients and identical folds; neither learns row/frequency correspondence.

### Same-loss ReZ-endpoint ablation

For each P anchor table, embed only its normalized ReZ interval as `{(min ReZ,0),(max ReZ,0)}`; compute its 64-direction support displacement `e_anchor`, then the same `F0/Fshape` projections. Fit `H_Z=B0_P+aZ+qZ` with the same two anchor coefficients, tuning, predictions, and *paired-support target loss* as `H_P`. The increment
`I_pair=(E[H_Z]-E[H_P])/E[B0_P]`
tests whether observed paired trace geometry adds held-target information beyond documented ReZ endpoints at equal complexity. It does not identify the meaning of `N_A`.

## Losses and target-matched estimands

In every outer fold, estimate target-coordinate scales from outer-training specimens only:
`sR[o,t,k]=max(raw_MAD(dR_train[:,t,k]),1e-6 ohm)`;
`sP[o,t,j]=max(raw_MAD(dP_train[:,t,j]),1e-6 normalized units)`.

Use equal-specimen losses:
`L_R[m,a->t,i,v]=sum_k w_v[k]*((dR_i,t[k]-pred)/sR)^2`;
`L_P[m,a->t,i]=(1/64)sum_j ((dP_i,t[j]-pred)/sP)^2`.
Require positive finite baseline error. Define gains `G_R=1-E[H_R]/E[B0_R]`, `G_P=1-E[H_P]/E[B0_P]`, simple gains, and shape increments. Raw-ohm rank RMSE and normalized-support RMSE are secondary and never compared across arms.

For each target:
`D20=G[50->20]-G[80->20]`;
`D50=G[20->50]-G[80->50]`;
`D80=G[20->80]-G[50->80]`.
Compute `D_R(v)` at all five vertices and `D_P` once. The practical margin is 0.10. No averaging over targets, anchors, vertices, or representations may select an anchor.

## Leakage-safe fitting for n=11

Use 11 outer leave-one-specimen-out folds. Standardize non-intercept columns from fitting rows only, with equal total specimen weight and equal coordinate weight within specimen. Ridge alphas are `{1e-4,1e-3,...,1e4}`; intercepts are unpenalized; exact-zero-variance columns are dropped and reported. Tune each edge/model by inner leave-one-specimen-out folds, recomputing normalizations, scales, projections, standardization, dropped columns, and predictions. Ties choose the larger alpha. Fit each target B0 once and reuse it for its two anchors only after prediction equality checks.

Group sizes are 2/3/3/3. These folds test transfer to another cell under a represented protocol, not transfer to a new protocol. Group 1 has one training peer in its outer fold; influence is therefore mandatory. A sensitivity restricts inner validation to splits whose fitting partition retains all four groups. Another uses equal contributing-protocol rather than equal-specimen fit weights. Neither sensitivity can create support; a changed classification is inconclusive.

## Shared 432-allocation linkage calibration

Enumerate all `2!*3!*3!*3!=432` within-group specimen permutations, identity included. In each fold first lock the density-invariant P normalization from the unpermuted fitting population, then compute every specimen’s complete three-SOC source bundle `{dR20,dR50,dR80,dP20,dP50,dP80,endpoint20,endpoint50,endpoint80}`. Move that whole source bundle jointly from donor to recipient. Recipient target outcomes, recipient all-BoL B0 context, protocol, folds, target scales, and locked normalization remain fixed. Thus a table can supply a permuted anchor representation while its recipient target role remains sealed and fixed; no raw row or SOC is partly relinked. Use the identical donor allocation in all arms. Rerun nested anchor fits and scores; cache only quantities proven allocation-invariant. All allocations must finish.

Use one maximum of allocation-standardized statistics only for multiplicity control—not effect aggregation:

- 12 directional superiority statistics: two directions × three targets × R/P; R uses its worst vertex.
- 12 robust-edge statistics: six edges × R/P; R uses its worst vertex.
- six paired-increment statistics `I_pair`.
- separately, three R measure-range statistics and 30 R edge-by-vertex statistics.

Compute exact one-sided family-wise fractions after centering/scaling by all 432 allocations; require nonzero allocation SD. No combined effect size, vote, rank, or mean across representations is reported. Interpretation remains conditional on unverified within-group exchangeability of complete source bundles, not randomized treatment or population inference.

## Uncertainty, influence, and checks

With `Generator(PCG64(20260924))`, draw 10,000 group-stratified cell resamples at sizes 2/3/3/3, preserving each cell’s complete cross-model/edge/representation loss vector. Report percentile intervals and simultaneous max-standardized-deviation bands over all 15 R target-by-vertex contrasts, three P contrasts, 12 edge minima/gains, and six paired increments. These are conditional cell-weighting stability summaries, not population confidence intervals.

Delete each specimen and rerun both complete nested pipelines on 10 cells. Report all edges, contrasts, paired increments, and fixed-anchor statuses. Also report per-group gains, rank sectors, angular sectors, selected alphas, matrix ranks/conditions, discarded energies, hull vertices, and each hull-vertex deletion’s worst influence.

Additional non-rescuing checks: 32/128 support directions and half-step phase; nearest feasible support; ReZ global unit multipliers 0.1/10; positive channel-wise affine scaling with fold refitting; rank trim of one low/high value with recomputed 33-rank weights; R’s 10,000 convex mixtures; group weighting; group-complete tuning; and bitwise-identical predictions across R evaluation vertices. Required mathematical invariances must pass; substantive sensitivity disagreement yields inconclusive status.

## Deterministic falsification and conclusions

An R or P edge is **robust-useful** only if gain is at least 0.10 (R at every vertex), its 12-edge family-wise fraction is at most 0.05, its stability lower bound is above zero, every deletion retains gain at least 0.10, no group gain is at or below -0.10, and all required invariances and non-rescuing sensitivities preserve positive classification.

A target direction is **supported in R** only if its worst-vertex directional contrast is at least 0.10, its 12-direction family-wise fraction is at most 0.05, simultaneous bands exclude zero in that direction at all vertices, every deletion preserves direction and margin, the favored edge is robust-useful, and sensitivities agree. **Supported in P** uses the same gates for its single angular loss. R measure reversal retains the parent’s strict opposite-vertex, useful-edge, adjusted-range, simultaneous-band, deletion, and 0.10 gates.

Target status is assigned without an omnibus:
- **representation-stable**: the same direction is supported in R and P;
- **representation-conflicting**: opposite directions are supported in R and P;
- **ReZ-only supported**: R supports a direction and P supports neither direction;
- **paired-only supported**: P supports a direction and R supports neither direction;
- **practically anchor-insensitive**: both arms’ simultaneous bands lie inside [-0.10,0.10] and each arm has a useful edge for that target;
- **transfer absent**: neither arm has any edge whose upper stability bound reaches 0.10 and all adjusted edge tests are adverse;
- **inconclusive**: otherwise.

The paired-coordinate increment is **supportive** only if `I_pair>=0.10`, six-increment family-wise fraction <=0.05, stability lower bound >0, at least 9/11 held cells favor `H_P`, every deletion is positive with at least 9/11 retaining 0.10, no group increment <=-0.10, and direction-grid/phase/scaling sensitivities stay positive. It is **adverse at 10%** if its estimate and stability upper bound are below 0.10, adjusted fraction >0.05, at most 7/11 cells favor it, and no sensitivity supports it; otherwise it is inconclusive. A representation conflict plus supportive paired increment is described as dependence on unlabeled paired geometry, not as an `N_A` mechanism. Without supportive increment, the conflict cannot be attributed specifically to the second channel.

A fixed anchor maps to pairwise wins exactly:
- 20% requires positive D50 and D80;
- 50% requires positive D20 and negative D80;
- 80% requires negative D20 and D50.

Exactly one global branch is reported:
1. **supportive representation-stable fixed-anchor eligibility**: one anchor satisfies both wins in R and P and all four favored edges are robust-useful;
2. **supportive representation-stable target dependence only**: at least one target is stable, but no fixed anchor qualifies and no conflict exists;
3. **representation-dependent choice**: at least one target conflicts and no fixed anchor qualifies;
4. **ReZ-only fixed-anchor eligibility**: one anchor satisfies both R wins but not both P wins and P has no opposite supported win; this is not representation-stable;
5. **paired-geometry-only signal**: P supports but R does not; no acquisition recommendation is made because `N_A` semantics are unknown;
6. **adverse, practically anchor-insensitive**: all targets satisfy the corresponding adverse equivalence gate in both arms;
7. **adverse, transfer absent/moot**: all six edges in both arms satisfy transfer-absent gates;
8. **inconclusive**: every other valid outcome, including mixed targets, margin crossing, calibration/stability disagreement, deletion dependence, or failed audit gates.

Supportive results establish only archive-conditional held-cell reconstruction and a criterion-specific prospective anchor eligibility for another cell under these represented protocols. Adverse results falsify only the registered low-dimensional transfer families at the 10% margin. Inconclusive results mean 11 cells and four protocol groups do not discriminate the alternatives. Preserve all unfavorable outcomes.

No branch establishes frequency correspondence, imaginary impedance, a physical Nyquist envelope, equal support coverage, common exposure at MoL, path causality, fixture/contact exclusion, electrochemical mechanism, practical acquisition burden, or external transfer. Stronger claims require an authoritative channel/frequency/order dictionary, repeat/remount controls, common-boundary capacity/throughput/temperature histories, validated SOC/equilibration, more independent cells/protocols, prospective frozen-anchor validation, and electrochemical expert review.

## Alternatives and selection record

The simple alternatives are no-anchor B0 and low-order anchor transfer A. The substantive H alternatives add one prespecified smooth shape feature on identical inputs, folds, targets, scales, and losses. They are selected because they ask whether nonlinear rank bending or angular boundary deformation contains transferable information that a location/translation model loses, while adding only one coefficient.

A flexible learned 5×5 rank operator, full 17×17 support map, kernels, trees, PCA/PLS selection, and neural encoders are deferred because 11 independent specimens cannot adjudicate their degrees of freedom. This is not a categorical objection to GPUs or neural methods; revisit with materially more cells. Source-index, frequency-localized, ECM, DRT, and complex-plane models await authoritative row frequency and `N_A` meaning/unit/sign. Interior-distribution paired models await a justified acquisition measure or repeat/noise model. Personalized anchor policies are deferred because the present question is fixed target-matched eligibility.

The ReZ-endpoint ablation is retained because it uniquely answers whether paired support adds information on the same target loss. It is not promoted to a third decision representation, avoiding an incoherent three-way omnibus.

## Scientific deliverable, compute, and verifier boundary

Completion requires newly fitting R and P B0/A/H models plus endpoint ablations for all six edges; all rank vertices/mixtures; all 432 shared allocations; 10,000 stratified resamples; 11 deletion refits; all invariance, feasibility, influence, and sensitivity checks; and deterministic target/global branches.

Required outputs:
`source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_rows.parquet`, `rank_displacements.parquet`, `measure_weights.json`, `paired_hulls.parquet`, `support_displacements.parquet`, `basis_audit.json`, `information_mask_audit.json`, `outer_predictions.parquet`, `losses_by_representation.parquet`, `directed_edge_metrics.csv`, `target_contrasts.csv`, `endpoint_ablation.csv`, `all_432_allocations.parquet`, `multiplicity.json`, `stability.parquet`, `deletion_metrics.csv`, `group_coordinate_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`, `invariance_audit.json`, `metrics.json`, and `conclusion.json` with sentence-to-field provenance.

Use 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS threads, allocation-level parallelism, cached B0/invariant matrices after equality checks, and checkpoints every 36 allocations. Measured parent facts: native export 20–22 s, a prior unoptimized six-edge fit 22.8 s, and hull/support screens under 3 s. Estimated crossover workload is 45–90 wall-minutes and at most 48 CPU-hours; this fits the 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/28,800-s solver envelope and 7,200-s reference cap. A <=600-s readiness probe must time at least 36 complete allocations and extrapolate below 6,600 s, leaving output-finalization margin. If it fails, optimize/cachify mathematically identical work; changing population, estimands, models, calibration, or falsification returns to the Lead. GPU use adds no value to these small ridge systems.

The verifier can recompute hashes, exact table selection, duplicates, folds, sorting, rank weights, hulls, supports, bases, masks, scales, nested predictions, all allocations/max-T families, seeded stability summaries, deletions, invariances, and branch logic. It must accept warranted supportive, adverse, conflicting, or inconclusive conclusions and reject correct calculations paired with unsupported channel, frequency, mechanism, causality, cost, universal-anchor, or population claims. Scientific adjudication remains necessary for the reasonableness of the rank-measure class, meaning of the paired coordinate and hull, exchangeability, SOC comparability, and practical importance of 10%.

# Proposal: does a three-protocol Oxford single-SOC action transport to the fourth protocol?

## Question, hypothesis, and scientific advance

For the exact 11 Oxford NCR18650BD cells in four cycling-schedule groups, does a single middle-of-life (MoL) SOC acquisition action selected using three complete protocol groups retain a material, measure-robust advantage when applied to the wholly unseen fourth group?

The scientific parent, `candidate-3643233d62a094d53caf5b68`, makes the within-archive action question identifiable: independently sorted real-impedance empirical quantiles avoid an undocumented row join; target-matched contrasts prevent an action from winning merely because it elects to observe the hardest target; and a fixed action is recommendable only if both omitted targets corroborate it. The unresolved boundary is protocol transport. Its specimen-LOSO fits contain peer cells from every protocol, so protocol terms and exact-schedule peers can help both the model and the action selector. That evidence cannot show that an action learned without any outcome from a new schedule will work there.

This child freezes four leave-one-protocol-group-out (LOGO) trials. In each trial, every representation, scale, coefficient, ridge choice, and SOC action is learned using only the other three groups. A held cell supplies all three beginning-of-life (BoL) tables and, as the prospective action permits, its one selected MoL anchor table; its other two MoL tables remain sealed until scoring.

The primary hypothesis is **zero-shot action transport**: one SOC is selected in all four training-three-groups folds; on the four untouched groups it reduces two-target loss by at least 10% versus each constant alternative throughout the parent's empirical-rank measure class; and both corresponding same-target anchor contrasts independently favor it by at least 10%. The substantive alternative is **one-cell sparse calibration**: after the action is frozen, one commissioning cell from the held protocol is measured at all three MoL SOCs and supplies target-specific scalar residual offsets for the other held cells. This tests whether failure is compatible with a low-dimensional protocol location shift rather than loss of the rank-varying source-to-target map.

A positive zero-shot result would advance the archive-level claim from “one action is robust when every protocol is represented in training” to “the action and pooled smooth transfer survive four observed train-three/test-fourth schedule shifts.” A calibration-only result would instead show that the action is one-full-profile-cell recoverable under these four schedules. Neither result establishes a universal anchor, a protocol population, a fifth-protocol guarantee, cost effectiveness, or an ageing mechanism.

## Supported evidence and unresolved claim

The inspected Oxford README supports 12 nominal 3 Ah NCA/graphite NCR18650BD cells, testing in a 24 °C chamber, and four groups combining C/2 or C/4 cycling with short one-cycling-day/five-calendar-day or long two-cycling-day/ten-calendar-day blocks at 90% nominal SOC. It reports EIS at ordinal BoL and MoL at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, with 100 mA peak-to-peak excitation over a document-level 5 kHz–10 mHz range and six points per decade.

The configured ZIP inventory contains the 66 required BoL/MoL containers for 11 cells. The parent's native export (`job-c77242e0a0edb30774eebca8`, 18.55 s) selected 66 exact container-stem/internal-table matches and 2,310 rows; every canonical table had 35 rows, columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`, finite untied `ReZ_Ohm`, and repeated internal copies equal to their canonical table. The converter verified round-trip structure, not field semantics.

The strongest evidence currently supported is therefore that the frozen 11-cell, 66-table corpus is available and admits the row-order-invariant representation. No LOGO action choice, transport loss, target contrast, calibration rescue, or protocol-level scientific result has been computed. The experiment tests those unresolved claims. The Raj et al. publisher full text and supplementary methods were not inspected, and no conclusion depends on them.

## Population, protocols, time, and identification limit

The independent specimens are exactly:

- Group 1, C/2 short: `G1_C15,G1_C20` (2 cells);
- Group 2, C/4 short: `G2_C3,G2_C4,G2_C8` (3);
- Group 3, C/2 long: `G3_C10,G3_C11,G3_C14` (3);
- Group 4, C/4 long: `G4_C12,G4_C18,G4_C19` (3).

Exclude `G1_C9` because paired MoL EIS is absent. Groups 5–10 are not part of the README-bound four-group longitudinal population with paired coverage.

Time is only `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, ordered BoL before MoL. There is no admitted timestamp, elapsed exposure, cycle count, throughput, capacity, or common SOH boundary. “MoL” is an ordinal source label, not a common physical age.

These four groups form the four observed combinations of two bundled schedule descriptors, but there is only one group per combination. LOGO can compute whether a rule trained on three observed groups predicts the fourth. It cannot estimate a distribution of protocol effects, separate cycling rate from periodicity causally, identify a rate-by-periodicity interaction, or support conventional inference to new protocols. Group 1 has only two cells and the others three; repeated ranks, SOCs, targets, ordered calibration roles, and folds are not independent cells.

## Exact read-only binding

Use only:

- catalog: `[private path]`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`, runtime `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`;
- README: `[private path]`, SHA-256 `59489534eaa5cddd2cef74b057855d2074bbef802d3aa12db6e082f9886dc59c`, runtime `/data/4a245ba1d6-oxford-readme.txt`;
- EIS ZIP: `[private path]`, SHA-256 `64d1fc94dcd3b2403d3f84b88666781a4f6153068e2ef4311d7cde97106a6d27`, runtime `/data/e05ee114fa-oxford-eis.zip`.

For every listed cell, `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, and `SOC in {20,50,80}`, read archive member

`EIS/{stage}/Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}.mat`

and select only internal table

`Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}`.

Require exact container-stem/internal-name agreement, 35 rows, columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`, finite numeric `ReZ_Ohm`, and unchanged hashes. The three G2_C3 MoL containers expose all three G2_C3 SOC variables, and G3_C11 MoL SOC20 also exposes SOC50 and SOC80. Retain only the stem-matching variable and require every repeated copy to be bitwise equal; any disagreement fails readiness.

Normalize to
`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,source_row_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.
The source-table key is `(group,cell_id,stage,SOC_label_pct)`. Require 11 specimen keys, 66 canonical tables, 2,310 rows, two stages, three SOCs per cell-stage, and 35 rows per table. Preserve `N_A` as `channel2_raw` for audit only; its meaning and unit are unavailable.

Nominal SOC is supplied metadata, not independently validated electrochemical state, coulomb-counted SOC, or a BMS estimate. Exact per-row frequency, imaginary impedance semantics, current sign, charge return, capacity normalization, equilibration, acquisition order, repeats/remounts, and fixture history are unavailable.

## Row-order-invariant target and measure class

Independently sort each table's 35 `ReZ_Ohm` values:
`q[c,z,s,1] <= ... <= q[c,z,s,35]`.
Define the empirical-quantile displacement

`Y[c,s,k]=q[c,MoL,s,k]-q[c,BoL,s,k]`.

This aligns equal empirical probabilities only. It is not a source-row, frequency, or tracked-point join. Never use `source_row_index` as a join key, coordinate, or predictor.

Retain the parent's five rank-probability vertices. For interval `I_k=((k-1)/35,k/35]`,

`w^(a,b)_k=F_Beta(a,b)(k/35)-F_Beta(a,b)((k-1)/35)`

for `(a,b) in {(1,1),(2,2),(1/2,1/2),(1,2),(2,1)}`: uniform, center-emphasized, tail-emphasized, low-ReZ-emphasized, and high-ReZ-emphasized. Require positive finite weights summing to one within `1e-12`. Let `M` be their convex hull and `wbar` their arithmetic mean.

Fit each prediction once under `wbar`; evaluation weights never alter predictions, tuning, or action selection except that the training-only action minimizes worst-vertex validation loss. For fixed predictions, relevant losses are linear in the measure and gain contrasts are linear-fractional with positive denominators, so extrema over `M` occur at vertices. Verify with 10,000 seeded random mixtures. Claims apply only to `M`, not to frequency integration or arbitrary row measures.

## Matched pooled models

Construct the parent's fixed cubic rank-spline basis from `u_k=(k-0.5)/35`: five uniform knots, degree three, no bias, constant extrapolation. Residualize against the constant under `wbar`, take deterministic weighted SVD, sign-fix each component by its largest absolute entry, and retain singular values above `1e-10` of the largest.

For source anchor `a`, define `mu[c,a]=sum_k wbar_k Y[c,a,k]` and the parent's smooth centered shape `h[c,a,:]=P_Q Y[c,a,:]`. Report discarded residual energy under every vertex.

Fit each directed edge `a->t`, `a != t`, separately:

- **B0, matched pooled baseline:** intercept, fixed rank-spline basis, and same-rank independently sorted BoL `ReZ_Ohm` at all three SOCs.
- **L, simple anchor model:** B0 plus source-anchor location `mu[c,a]`, repeated across target ranks.
- **H, learned smooth-shape model:** L plus `h[c,a,k]`.

Unlike the parent, no protocol indicator, rate, periodicity, interaction, held-group mean, or exact-schedule peer term is allowed. With three outer-training groups, the full 2×2 interaction model is rank-deficient; inside inner LOGO only two protocol corners remain, so even intercept plus two additive main effects is unidentified without a coding-dependent penalty. Deferring that model prevents an arbitrary extrapolation convention from masquerading as transport. Revisit additive protocol transport with replicated groups per schedule corner or an independently justified prior.

B0, L, and H use identical cells, group folds, target scales, BoL information, rank weights, and ridge procedure. L asks whether an anchor-wide displacement is sufficient. H adds one learned coefficient on a prespecified smooth rank-varying source displacement, retaining information L loses. H is frozen primary and is never selected because it gives the preferred conclusion. Flexible operators, kernels, and neural encoders cannot be identified credibly from 2/3/3/3 cells; ECM/DRT alternatives require unavailable frequency and complex-impedance semantics.

## Leakage-free nested LOGO and prospective action selection

Use four outer folds, holding Group 1, 2, 3, then 4 completely untouched. Outer training sizes are 9, 8, 8, and 8 cells. Within each outer fold, tune every edge/model by three inner LOGO folds over the three training groups. Each inner fold fits on two whole groups and validates on the third. Recompute target scales, standardization, zero-variance drops, ridge fits, and every outcome-dependent quantity inside each split.

For target `t` and rank `k`, define from fitting cells only
`s[t,k]=max(raw_MAD({Y[c,t,k]}),1e-6 source-labeled ohm)`.
Use the fit-local version in inner folds and the outer-training version for held-group scoring. Standardize non-intercept columns on fitting rows only. Fit ridge with an unpenalized intercept and `alpha in {1e-4,1e-3,...,1e4}`; ties choose larger alpha. Fitting and validation give equal total weight to each protocol group, then each cell, then `wbar` ranks. Report active rank, condition number, dropped columns, alpha, coefficient norm, and extrapolation range.

For model `m`, held cell `c` in outer group `g`, edge `a->t`, and vertex `v`:

`L[m,a,t,c,v]=sum_k w[v,k]*((Y[c,t,k]-Yhat[m,a,t,c,k])/s_outer[t,k])^2`.

For every action `a`, use the fully inner-LOGO cross-fitted H predictions on the outer-training groups to compute its equal-group, equal-cell, two-omitted-target mean loss at each vertex. Select the minimax action with smallest worst-vertex loss; ties use 20, then 50, then 80. Refit the six edges on all outer-training cells with inner-selected hyperparameters and apply the one selected action to every untouched held-group cell. Also predict all three counterfactual constant actions for evaluation. The held group's MoL target tables, errors, means, scales, quality summaries, and group identity as a fitted effect may not affect selection.

The only held-cell MoL information available before prediction is the table at the action SOC. Deliberately modifying either sealed target table must change only that target's score, never its prediction, preprocessing, alpha, coefficient, or selected action.

## Zero-shot transport estimands and target-matched corroboration

Aggregate outer losses equally over the four held groups, then cells. Let `E[m,a,t,v]` be the aggregate edge loss and `E[B0,t,v]` the anchor-invariant baseline. Require B0 predictions to be bitwise equal across candidate anchors.

Report

`G_H[a,t,v]=1-E[H,a,t,v]/E[B0,t,v]`,
`G_L[a,t,v]=1-E[L,a,t,v]/E[B0,t,v]`, and
`G_shape[a,t,v]=1-E[H,a,t,v]/E[L,a,t,v]`.

Freeze the three target-matched H contrasts:

- `D20(v)=G_H[50,20,v]-G_H[80,20,v]`;
- `D50(v)=G_H[20,50,v]-G_H[80,50,v]`;
- `D80(v)=G_H[20,80,v]-G_H[50,80,v]`.

For constant action `a` define

`A[a,v]=(1/4) sum_g (1/n_g) sum_(c in g) (1/2) sum_(t != a) L[H,a,t,c,v]`

and `C[a,b,v]=1-A[a,v]/A[b,v]`. Report target contributions, all vertices, each held group, cell-equal aggregation, raw-ohm RMSE, and 5%/20% margins. The 10% threshold is a model-loss materiality convention, not instrument resolution or economic utility.

A common action `a*` is zero-shot transport-supportive only if:

1. all four outer training-three-group selectors choose `a*`;
2. `min_v C[a*,b,v]>=0.10` for each alternative `b`;
3. for each omitted target `t != a*`, the same-target contrast between `a*` and the other non-target anchor favors `a*` by at least 0.10 at every vertex;
4. both edges `a*->t` have `min_v G_H>=0.10`;
5. H's direction is positive in every held group, with the action and both target-matched margins at least 0.10 in at least three groups;
6. the calibration, stability, deletion, tuning, trim, and multiplicity gates below pass, and L never robustly favors a competitor.

Thus an action cannot win by choosing to observe an intrinsically difficult target. H support with robust `G_shape` localizes information to the registered smooth quantile-shape component; otherwise report whether location-only L accounts for the result.

## One-complete-cell sparse calibration alternative

After the zero-shot selector is frozen, evaluate each possible commissioning cell `j` in a held group and each different target cell `i`. The commissioning cell supplies its complete three-SOC MoL bundle. The target cell still supplies only its candidate action's MoL table; its two target tables remain sealed.

For every model/edge, compute the commissioning cell's target residual from its zero-shot prediction and retain only its scalar `wbar` location:

`delta[j,m,a,t]=sum_k wbar_k*(Y[j,t,k]-Yhat[m,a,t,j,k])`.

Predict target cell `i` by

`Yhat_C[m,a,t,i|j,k]=Yhat[m,a,t,i,k]+delta[j,m,a,t]`.

No rank-varying held-protocol correction or held-group slope is fitted. This is a target- and edge-specific intercept translation from one cell, not a claim that the protocol shift is truly constant. Score all ordered `j->i` roles: 2 in Group 1 and 6 in each other group, keeping the two target outcomes and ranks together. Weight groups equally and ordered roles equally within group. Every candidate action receives the identical full-profile commissioning budget, and the zero-shot-selected action remains fixed.

Report calibrated B0/L/H action and target contrasts, plus rescue `R[a,v]=1-A_C[H,a,v]/A[H,a,v]` on matched roles. A **calibration-only recovery** requires the same `a*` was selected in all four zero-shot outer folds, zero-shot support failed, the fully calibrated version satisfies the action, both target-matched, usefulness, group-direction, multiplicity, stability, deletion, and sensitivity gates, and `min_v R[a*,v]>=0.10` with a positive simultaneous lower bound. The strongest conclusion is “archive-conditional action dominance was recoverable after one complete commissioning profile.” It is not zero-shot transport and does not prove a protocol mean shift: one cell's residual mixes protocol and cell-specific error.

If zero-shot and calibrated tracks both support, calibration is unnecessary for the observed groups. If calibration fails despite a positive within-protocol parent benchmark, a scalar location correction does not rescue the registered transport map. A two-cell average is a sensitivity for Groups 2–4 only and cannot replace the four-group primary because Group 1 has only two cells.

## Conditional linkage, multiplicity, and stability

Enumerate all `2!*3!*3!*3!=432` within-group allocations, identity included. Move each donor's complete predictor-side three-SOC anchor-displacement bundle jointly to one recipient while retaining recipient BoL context, protocol, and scored MoL targets. Rerun all outer/inner LOGO fits, action selection, B0/L/H predictions, and sparse-calibration predictions; commissioning outcomes remain with the commissioning cell. Never permute SOCs, ranks, measures, or coordinates separately. B0 must be allocation-invariant.

For the three target contrasts, three unordered action contrasts, six directed-edge gains, six H-versus-L increments, and calibrated counterparts, form both signed robust branches using the worst vertex. Standardize each branch over all 432 allocations and use one maximum standardized statistic per allocation. Identity upper-tail fractions are familywise conditional linkage p-values. A supportive branch requires adjusted `p<=0.05`. These tests require unverified within-group exchangeability and only ask whether correct cell linkage matters beyond fixed group labels; they do not test treatment assignment or protocol-population transport.

Only four held groups exist. Report all 16 sign patterns for group loss differences, but never use `1/16` as a 0.05 inferential gate.

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260924))`, make 50,000 hierarchical Bayesian-bootstrap weight draws: Dirichlet weights over the four held groups, then over cells within group; for calibration roles use pair weight proportional to the two cell weights. Compute simultaneous max-standardized-deviation bands over all action/target contrasts and vertices. These are sensitivity-to-observed-unit-weight summaries, not confidence or credible intervals for a protocol population.

Report all four held-group losses, all 11 cell losses, all calibration roles, four leave-one-held-group-out aggregate summaries, and 11 full specimen-deletion refits. Support becomes inconclusive if any held group reverses the action or either required target contrast, any held-group omission reverses a required aggregate direction, or any specimen deletion reverses direction; at least 9/11 deletions must retain each 0.10 margin.

## Parent benchmark, sensitivities, and invariance

Recompute the parent's 11-fold specimen-LOSO action benchmark with all four protocols represented, its exact target-matched/action gates, and the same measure class. It cannot support protocol transport. It is required to distinguish “failed to transport” from “no registered action decision was present.”

Rerun the complete LOGO pipeline for: trimming the lowest and highest order statistic in every table with rebuilt 33-rank weights; equal-cell rather than equal-group fitting; ridge grids `{1e-4,1e-2,1,1e2,1e4}` and `{1e-5,...,1e5}`; and target scales with floors `5e-7` and `2e-6`. A sensitivity cannot rescue an adverse primary. Support requires trim direction and every valid sensitivity direction to persist; none may create a robust competitor.

Required exact checks include:

1. 1,000 independent source-row permutations reproduce profiles, predictions, selections, and classifications to `1e-12`;
2. no source-row join or predictor exists;
3. 10,000 random measure mixtures remain inside vertex extrema;
4. predictions are identical across evaluation measures;
5. repeated internal variables are exactly equal;
6. joint positive unit multipliers 0.1 and 10 preserve relative gains, allocation fractions, selection, and classification;
7. all target scales and standardizations use fitting groups only;
8. synthetic changes to held targets trigger no upstream change;
9. outer held-group labels cannot enter a fitted protocol effect;
10. calibrated target cell `i` never contributes its own sealed target or another held cell's outcome except the declared commissioning cell `j`.

## Frozen outcomes and falsification
